name: jev-proxy
description: jev-proxy is a policy firewall for MCP tool calls: inserted between an MCP client and any stdio server, it allows, denies, or holds each `tools/call` for one-time human approval via ordered rules, with an append-only redacted JSONL audit log.

name: jev-creature-forge
description: Turns natural-language creature descriptions into an inspectable typed genome, using Jev's bounded typed judgments for ambiguous traits while deterministic code derives anatomy, tracks provenance, and renders replayable SVG creatures in a local Studio.

name: jev-cli
description: A command-line client for TypeSafe AI's Jev model that answers typed questions about text—yes/no probabilities, multi-option choices, or scored scales—returning calibrated numbers, JSON output, and gate-based exit codes for branching decisions in shell scripts, CI jobs, and AI agents via MCP.

name: transcript-lens
description: A Turkish-language Next.js app that analyzes YouTube or pasted SRT/VTT transcripts via the Jev AI model to surface chapter boundaries, a criteria heatmap, and semantically searched passages, with export to TXT, Markdown, SRT, VTT, or JSON.

name: typesafe-jev-plugin
description: A Claude plugin that turns reusable `.sig.json` signature definitions (state mappings plus Choice/Score/Noul questions) into batched TypeSafe Jev API calls over CSV, Excel, or text-file datasets, writing typed answers, confidences, and review flags back to Excel.

name: typesafe_sdk
description: TypeSafeSDK is a deprecated Elixir/BEAM SDK (final release 0.4.1) whose TypeSafe API client functionality—authentication, endpoint and model configuration, generated wire operations, and typed response handling—has moved to the provider-neutral `system_one_sdk` successor and `typesafe_api_sdk` provider layer.

name: openjev-sglang
description: FastAPI server exposing the TypeSafe/Jev evaluation API backed by Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on SGLang (Modal-deployable on B200), answering up to 64 Noul/Choice/Score questions per request via single-token logprob readouts over a shared radix-cached prefix.

name: JevSpawn
description: JevSpawn is an open-source inference method and GPU runtime that lets LLM agents infer and adapt their own compositional action spaces — combining conditional field probabilities into joint action distributions, exploring beam-selected actions in parallel state copies with backtracking, and batch-evaluating finite choices — achieving competitive task performance at lower latency across eight b

name: Alloy
description: Alloy is a local skill that applies OpenRouter's "Fusion" method to your installed AI CLIs, dispatching one prompt to a parallel read-only panel (codex, grok, claude, agy) then judging and synthesizing the answers to expose consensus, contradictions, and blind spots.

name: zio-evals
description: A ZIO 2/Scala 3 toolkit for agent evals: run tasks across configurable arms (MCP servers, skills, system prompts, models), grade with generative or binary judges and deterministic checks, and aggregate metrics/transcripts for tests or apps.

name: jev-decisionops
description: JEV DecisionOps is a full-stack invoice decision tool that sends invoice and vendor data through a FastAPI backend to TypeSafe JEV for risk, routing, review, reliability, and priority signals, then applies deterministic policy rules to return AUTO_APPROVE, HUMAN_REVIEW, or REJECT — failing safely to human review if JEV is unavailable.

name: typesafe-computer-use
description: A macOS computer-use tool that automates GUI interactions for roughly $0.0002 per step by OCR-ing the screen, classifying the next action with TypeSafe, and clicking.

name: jevline
description: Jevline is an experimental incident-reconstruction tool that, from one confirmed malicious process, address, account, or host, iteratively follows schema-agnostic telemetry links and uses TypeSafe’s Jev model to expand, review, and report the related execution chain, timeline, and evidence.

name: jev-browser-qa
description: A Playwright browser-QA toolkit where the fast Jev model answers yes/no and one-of questions to power natural-language assertions, intent-based element picking, and goal-driven click loops, with a JSON CLI, recorded video/traces, and a local run-history dashboard.

name: jevflow
description: JevFlow is a TypeScript library making probabilistic AI judgments (yes/no probabilities, ordinal scores, label choices) typed, provider-agnostic primitives that compose with deterministic threshold workflows to yield explainable, side-effect-free action sets.

name: vercel-jev-mcp
description: A Hono-based remote MCP server deployable to Vercel that relays Bearer-authenticated evaluation calls (jev_ask, jev_classify, jev_score, jev_check) through Vercel AI Gateway to TypeSafe Jev, letting multiple AI clients share one URL without Jev API keys.

name: jev-playground
description: A Next.js playground that benchmarks TypeSafe AI's Jev against four Gateway-hosted models (GPT-5.6 Luna, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite, GPT-6 Astra) by letting you play tic-tac-toe and Connect Four against each on independent boards, logging every move's legal options, weights, and confidence to inspect decision quality, consistency, and reliability.

name: jev-harness
description: A research-stage Node.js contract where an LLM proposes one action, a pinned Jev model answers four fixed review questions, and a deterministic decision table emits evidence-only verdicts—never applying patches, executing code, or granting permission—plus an offline fixture benchmark.

name: hunch
description: Hunch is a CLI that answers plain-English questions about a repository by scoring code chunks with an LLM provider (or a local model via `--provider semif`) to surface relevant source locations, and runs recurring rule-based reviews on diffs, pull requests, or entire repos.

name: jev-git
description: jev-git is a single statically linked Rust binary that installs as a `git jev` pre-commit/pre-push hook, using TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model to semantically screen staged diffs for unredacted secrets, prompt-injection attacks, and destructive commands in ~80ms.

name: justmem
description: justmem is a Python CLI that encodes long chat sessions into source-linked memory cards and answers questions via deterministic Jev-guided routing (Lookup/Compose/Replay), embedding retrieval, reranking, and cited evidence-grounded answers, with an offline mode for tests.

name: dasheng
description: A Next.js read-aloud trainer that streams microphone audio through Confucius4-R2T2 ASR, aligns recognized words to the target text, asks Jev closed-form questions to flag and classify mismatches, and computes local fluency/completeness scores—with mock mode for offline demos.

name: jevernetes
description: Jevernetes live-tails Kubernetes logs via kubectl into a terminal or localhost dashboard where TypeSafe Jev semantic analysis (or offline keyword rules) flags anomalies, groups repeats, and lets you inspect context, suppress expected events, and copy evidence to coding agents.

name: jev-linkedin-slop-filter
description: A Chrome MV3 extension plus local proxy that stamps LinkedIn feed posts as BAIT, CORP, or BRAG with confidence scores from TypeSafe's Jev model, keeping the API key server-side and using free local keyword rules, per-post caching, and fail-open rendering so a broken judgment never hides a real post.

name: jev-tool-runner
description: jev-tool-runner is a CLI wrapper that routes bounded native Codex tool calls (numbered reads of user-named source files) selected by TypeSafe's Jev model before the coding model runs, keeping execution inside Codex's sandbox and conversation while falling back to ordinary requests when unsupported.

name: visual-jev
description: A local, image-native typed-decision tool on a Qwen3-VL backbone that returns calibrated numerical distributions for choice, score, and noul questions over images—without generating text—via packed question branches, a learned pointer head, and fail-closed checkpoint loading.

name: jev-clef-experiments
description: A uv-managed Python project that drives simulators—Super Mario Bros emulator plus cart-pole and double-inverted-pendulum physics—with typed probability questions (choice/score/noul) answered by Jev or Cloudflare's multimodal Clef models, benchmarking perception-based LLM policies against LQR and logging CSV/GIF results per run.

name: jev-duckdb-analytics-cli
description: A CLI tool that executes DuckDB SQL queries against a database file or in-memory instance and evaluates the results against user-defined binary questions using TypeSafe's Jev model, returning structured JSON with yes/no answers, confidence scores, and probabilities.

name: jev-explained
description: jev-explained is a tool that provides explanations of Jev, helping users quickly understand what it is and how it works without digging through external documentation.

name: typesafe-jev
description: typesafe-jev provides self-contained experiments in decision-model-driven software, including cv-screen, a local workbench that turns CVs into typed judgments, applies transparent editable hiring policies, and rapidly re-scores candidates into sortable shortlists with auditable verdicts.

name: robo-harness
description: Robo Harness is a standalone SO-101 robot-arm playground combining a custom agent loop, Rerun visualization, lease-based manual and supervised chat/decision-run motion, recordings exportable to LeRobot datasets, and CLI/MCP/Python control over mock or real hardware.

name: jrx
description: JEV Reflex (`jrx`) is a deterministic execution-control gateway for autonomous coding agents that intercepts commands, patches, and tool calls via native hooks (Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, and more), applies sub-millisecond hard rules plus bounded TypeSafe JEV semantic risk signals to emit ALLOW/REVIEW/HOLD decisions, and supports OIDC-verified roles, single-use human approvals, signed policy

name: jev-lint
description: A fuzzy linter for coding agents: a post-edit hook for Claude Code and Codex sends newly written code to a fast judgment model that flags team-rule violations needing judgment rather than regex in ~0.3 s, with tested rule packs, custom per-repo rules, and a logging feedback loop.

name: reflexgate
description: ReflexGate is a Node.js/TypeScript API and webhook guardrail gateway that fans each inbound payload across seven risk and routing dimensions via a sub-100ms evaluation, then enforces deterministic policy verdicts, dispatches outbound webhooks, and audits decisions in SQLite.

name: jev-toto
description: A Rust CLI that scores Singapore TOTO numbers against recent draw history by querying TypeSafe's Jev model for each number's next-draw probability and a confidence-rated hot/cold label, with an auto mode that assembles a six-number set and syncs draw data from Singapore Pools.

name: kev-voice
description: Kev Voice is a fully local macOS voice-and-text controller: a floating bar captures spoken or typed commands while a local MLX Kev decision model picks atomic UI actions from the live Accessibility tree in an observe–act–verify loop, requiring no accounts, API keys, or network traffic.

name: jev-review-action
description: A GitHub Action that reviews pull requests or catalog submissions by collecting bounded repository evidence, querying the TypeSafe Jev typed-judgment model via a provider fallback chain, applying a maintainer-defined JSON policy, and posting one updatable advisory PR comment.

name: doom-jev
description: An autonomous ViZDoom agent that couples Doom's 35-tick engine with async ~10 Hz Jev SystemOne inference, using geometric raycasting, line-of-sight target filtering, hybrid macro/micro actuation, and a Rich terminal HUD for stutter-free real-time play.

name: ai-polish.nvim
description: ai-polish.nvim is a Neovim plugin that sends selected text or a buffer to Gemini for proofreading, presenting each suggestion as an anchored underline with up to three replacements and a reason in a floating popup so you accept or reject fixes individually, with optional Jev-based text evaluation, locale-aware labels, and cost estimation.

name: jev-lead-scorer
description: A dependency-free Python toolkit that scores sales leads via Jev's typed AI primitives (fit score, outreach angle, skip flag with confidence), then logs sends, replies, and bookings in SQLite so a per-variant funnel reveals which opener actually books meetings.

name: jevgpt
description: JevGPT is a chat client that coaxes text from a multiple-choice-only decision model, asking "Next word?" over a shuffled 20,000-word dictionary via bucketed parallel calls, run-off re-ranking, and repetition penalties, with a REPL, scripted turns, and JSON run recording.

name: polar_llama
description: Polar Llama is a Python library that runs parallel LLM inference (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Bedrock) directly on Polars dataframe columns, adding structured Pydantic outputs, tool calling, prompt caching, checkpointing, per-row cost tracking, and vector search.

name: jev-canvas
description: jev-canvas combines Web Speech voice commands (English/Ukrainian), MediaPipe fingertip tracking, and the Jev decision model to create, move, recolor, resize, duplicate, delete, or undo shapes on a tldraw canvas.

name: jev-go
description: jev-go is an unofficial, standard-library-only Go client (Go 1.26+, Apache-2.0) for TypeSafe's System One API that returns typed answers—Noul probabilities, Choice categories, and Score scale ratings—with explicit configuration, injectable HTTP clients, optional retries and request-size caps, plus a PR-triage CLI example.

name: figgie-on-jev
description: A dependency-free Python Figgie market simulator that benchmarks the Jev decision model, including persona role-play, against card counting and rule-based traders under order-book and open-outcry rules, with seeded replays, an offline mock, spending limits, and full logging.

name: jev-tetris
description: jev-tetris is a dependency-free Node.js app that pits TypeSafe's Jev model against Claude Haiku or Gemini Flash in real-time versus Tetris—shared seeded pieces, rising gravity, garbage rows for cleared lines—plus human-vs-Jev and solo modes with per-move stats, latency, and cost tracking.

name: Valen
description: Valen is a multimodal decision model that scores candidate actions from text, images, and video via a shared decision head on a Qwen3.5 backbone, delivering low-latency probability-based choices with included SFT/RLCD training, inference, and evaluation tooling.

name: codex-context-diet
description: A Codex plugin whose PostToolUse hook sends bulky tool results to TypeSafe's Jev for keep-or-drop verdicts, replacing stale output with a truncated head plus a one-line note so long sessions stop re-sending dead weight on every request.

name: reflex-gate
description: ReflexGate is a Windows desktop gateway that wraps a local Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B model on llama.cpp into a sub-second HTTP server (127.0.0.1:8090) providing agent-loop endpoints for stop-condition gating, error/status extraction, secret and prompt-injection scanning, and typed yes/no or choice decisions—eliminating cloud latency and token costs for autonomous agent iteration.

name: jev-skill-router
description: jev-skill-router is a local Python MCP service that keeps trusted SKILL.md libraries outside an agent’s context, uses TypeSafe Jev to select only task-relevant instructions, and returns them through one tool to reduce prompt overhead.

name: jev-cli
description: jev-cli (`jev`, npm package `jevctl`) wraps TypeSafe's Jev model to return fast, cheap probabilistic judgments—verify claims, screen for prompt injection, classify, extract, rerank, match, route—via scriptable commands with JSON output and exit codes for gating CI.

name: jevarena
description: JevArena is an open-source web arena for blind head-to-head judging that pits the Jev judge against any OpenRouter model on user-submitted questions, revealing model identity, latency, cost, and confidence only after voting, while keeping API keys in browser memory and including a reproducible Python benchmark harness (JevJudge-Bench) built on pinned JudgeBench, RM-Bench, and RewardBench 2 data.

name: JevEmon
description: JevEmon walks a real Pokémon FireRed ROM by reading overworld state from RAM, offering the LLM typed choices of reachable destinations and legal battle moves, then pathing and pressing buttons to execute its decisions — handling wild encounters and re-planning from wherever they end, verified from the Player's House through Pallet Town to Viridian City.

name: seen
description: Seen is a macOS menu bar app that continuously captures your screens and windows, OCRs their text locally with Apple's Vision framework, and lets you search that visual history from anywhere via Shift-Command-Space — optionally ranking results with the Jev model through your own TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway key.

name: jevlint
description: Jevlint is a CLI linter that uses Tree-sitter to extract code units (functions, types, comments, fields, statements) and evaluates them against plain-language rules via an LLM backend (TypeSafe's Jev or Cloudflare's Clef), offering rule packs, confidence thresholds, localization passes, caching, git-aware checks, and fixture-based rule evaluation.

name: JevFind
description: JevFind is a Rust CLI for semantic code search that turns plain-English queries into ranked file matches with line ranges and confidence scores by filtering paths by relevance, scanning bounded code windows via the TypeSafe API, and supporting tunable thresholds, parallelism, retries, and a live debug tree.

name: decision-gate
description: decision-gate is an npm library that routes Jev calls through one gate enforcing account-wide rate limits with coordinated 429 backoff, per-key daily and per-run spend ceilings, a shared answer cache, batched multi-question requests, and pre-send secret redaction.

name: hermes-jev-plugin
description: A Hermes Agent plugin exposing TypeSafe Jev’s calibrated Noul/Choice/Score judgments as four tools—jev_evaluate, jev_check, jev_route, jev_score—for batched atomic decisions, failure triage, review gates, task routing, and severity scoring in coding-agent workflows, plus a bundled question-design skill.

name: semcheck
description: semcheck is a Go linter whose rules are plain-English yes/no questions—AST matchers pick nodes, a pluggable decision model judges each fragment with type-checker context—so semantic checks like "does this log call leak PII" work via CLI, go vet, or golangci-lint.

name: jev-orchestrator
description: jev-orchestrator is a CLI app that triages inbound Gmail, Typeform, Slack, Discord, and X messages via Composio, using the cheap Jev classifier to route each message to a scoped single-tool LLM agent that drafts replies for one-click human approval, with risky messages always escalated.

name: AskJev
description: AskJev is an MCP server and optional browser extension that lets Claude Desktop drive Brave/Chrome via CDP from plain-English goals, with TypeSafe Jev making on-page action decisions and a Guard freezing irreversible clicks (pay, delete, send, publish) at risk ≥ 0.65.

name: jev-playground
description: An interactive playground of eight widgets for learning TypeSafe's Jev model, which answers typed choice, score, and boolean questions over given state with directly usable probabilities, showing raw request/response, latency, and cost for routing, triage, scoring, agent, and guardrail experiments.

name: AegisSRE-Signoz
description: AegisSRE-Signoz is a governed multi-agent incident response system that classifies service-reported errors, diagnoses root cause, and auto-remediates known failures via risk-tiered runbooks gated by human approval and a command-level safety firewall, with LLM provider failover and OpenTelemetry tracing.

name: shapeshift
description: Shapeshift is a single text input that morphs into the right card—event, checklist, timer, color, split, converter, poll and more—as you type, combining TypeSafe AI's Jev intent model with deterministic parsers and an offline keyword-classifier fallback.

name: commentcop
description: Commentcop is a CLI that uses TypeSafe's Jev to score JS/TS code comments for accuracy and usefulness out of 100, ranking the weakest first while respecting `.gitignore`, skipping generated code and dependencies, and offering dry-run previews, ignore files, and cost estimates to help prioritize comment review.

name: jev-plays-pokemon-red
description: A PyBoy-based Pokemon Red agent that decodes Game Boy RAM into a typed GameState, handles routine play in code, and asks a probability-only model to pick among proven-legal actions at real decision branches—achieving ~1.3 decisions/sec at ~$0.14/hour, with Brier-score self-evaluation and a live probability overlay.

name: jevspire
description: JevSpire is a dependency-free Node 22+ external player that drives Slay the Spire via CommunicationMod's stdin/stdout JSON protocol, translating each game snapshot into a validated action list sent to an OpenRouter LLM (or Jev's decisions endpoint), with per-request prompts, a 24KB payload cap, action limits, auto-pause on unsupported screens, and JSONL run logs for debugging.

name: parallelConstraintDecoding
description: A constrained-decoding engine (Java FFM bindings to llama.cpp, plus a Python/MLX reference port) that fills an entire JSON schema of booleans and enums in two forward passes instead of token-by-token generation, yielding schema-valid-by-construction output with per-field calibrated confidence, benchmarked ~8-18× faster, and demoed via a local web app.

name: jev-safety-gate
description: A safety gate that intercepts every AI agent tool call, uses Jev's calibrated typed queries (risk score, reversibility, production impact, category, human-needed) to evaluate the action, and applies deterministic policy rules to allow, block, or escalate it for human approval before the tool runs.

name: rizzo-flow
description: Rizzo Flow is an open-source local llama.cpp server that turns unstructured state into typed probabilistic decisions—booleans, choices, scores, numbers—by reading answer-letter logits rather than generating tokens, with a Jev-compatible HTTP API.

name: jev-mcp
description: jev-mcp is an MCP server that returns typed judgments — classification labels, rubric scores, yes/no checks, and abstaining candidate matches — over a closed answer set in ~130 ms with no text generation, exposing seven tools, calibrated confidence distributions, and a ~95% agreement rate on clean labels.

name: JevClient.jl
description: JevClient.jl is an unofficial Julia client for TypeSafe AI that evaluates a text `state` against structured question sets (Noul yes/no, Choice, and Score criteria) via `system_one`, returning typed answers with probabilities and confidence, with client lifecycle managed by `with_client`.

name: reflex-router
description: A loopback proxy for Claude Code that decides per task start which model tier (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus) and reasoning effort the work needs, optionally reroutes requests to cheaper models behind a prompt-cache cost guard, and logs decision outcomes (corrections, failed tests, undone edits) for review via `reflex report`.

name: pi-heed
description: pi-heed is a runtime guardrail for the pi coding agent that checks each side-effecting tool call against the user's conversational permissions and prohibitions, keeping structured policy state—including exceptions, lifts, and temporary grants—that survives context compaction.

name: jev-thread-search
description: A Codex plugin that finds past local Codex conversations by matching a natural-language description against thread titles and first/last exchanges, ranking candidates via TypeSafe's Jev API and returning commands to resume them.

name: jev-lexer
description: An experimental language-agnostic syntax highlighter that mechanically splits source into words and symbols, classifies each part via paid Jev LLM queries into nine visual classes, and emits Shiki-compatible tokens, HTML, or ANSI — useful mainly as a measured cost-vs-accuracy experiment, not production tooling.

name: jev_antispam_bot
description: A grammY Telegram bot that asks TypeSafe's pinned `jev-1.13.0` model whether each group message is spam—optionally enriched with sender bio/channel metadata—deletes only high-confidence matches and their linked campaign fragments, fails open on outages, and records optional privacy-safe stats in PostgreSQL.

name: OneRoute
description: OneRoute is a local LLM router (chat app, OpenAI-compatible API, CLI) that classifies each request with a fast "System One" model, then scores ~110 cataloged model×effort combinations against a benchmark capability database to pick the best quality-per-cost/latency, explaining every decision and learning from feedback.

name: jev-scout
description: jev-scout is a Rust CLI and stdio MCP server that matches natural-language prompts to real GitHub repos and crates.io packages, scoring them via TypeSafe AI's Jev System One API to return verified, installable results ranked by architectural fit, license, and maintenance freshness.

name: typesafe-mcp
description: An MCP server that exposes TypeSafe Jev's typed decision engine (choice, score, and noul verdicts with probabilities) as a single `evaluate(state, questions)` tool, with built-in guidance for batching, atomic questions, and confidence gating, installable via npx with a TypeSafe API key.

name: jgrep
description: jgrep is a CLI that semantically greps code by behavior rather than name, lints git diffs with English rules, selects tests a change affects, and scores CSV/JSONL rows via Jev's typed yes/no model — no index or embeddings.

name: jev-minecraft-factory-sorter
description: An anonymously accessible React 19/Canvas 2D Minecraft factory simulator and Express 5 backend for spawning, tossing, inspecting, and routing 429 vanilla/modded blocks through TypeSafe Jev, with server-side credential handling plus cache, latency, cost, and health accounting.

name: pi-stuff
description: A monorepo of seven pi agent extensions that add TypeSafe risk-scored bash auto-approval, live context-window usage charts and status widgets, a Codex usage meter, persistent self-continuing goals, ANSI-free bash output, and encrypted server-side compaction.

name: jevall
description: JEVALL is an inference gateway that turns multimodal language models into constrained decision services, answering typed choice/score/noul questions via one batched backbone pass and candidate-label softmax to return stable labels, probabilities, and latency diagnostics for controlled production workflows.

name: jevclip
description: jevclip is a zero-dependency Python CLI that uses an LLM to score each ~20-second segment of a video's subtitles or transcript, then cuts a ≤3-minute highlight reel and a filler-stripped full version via ffmpeg, outputting a timestamp-cited summary, per-segment keep/drop reasons, and tunable thresholds backed by cached judgments.

name: mobai-ci
description: mobai-ci is a free self-contained CI tool and GitHub Action that runs MobAI `.mob`, Maestro YAML, or AI-driven `.mobflow` UI tests on iOS simulators, Android emulators, USB devices, or cloud device farms, producing JUnit reports with screenshots and UI trees for each failed step.

name: a0-typesafe-ai
description: Agent Zero plugin adding a `typesafe_query` tool that asks Jev typed Choice, Noul, and Score questions over shared evidence in one call, returning probability cards with distributions, token counts, and raw JSON via the official TypeSafe Python SDK.

name: mario-jev
description: A uv-managed Python prototype that plays NES Super Mario Bros. by pausing the emulator, sending decoded RAM state to a Jev model for focused movement/jump decisions, composing answers into controller inputs, and logging decisions, with scripted, replay, and headless modes.

name: Jev-AI-Skill
description: Jev-AI-Skill is a reusable workflow skill for supported AI coding harnesses that turns a goal into checked execution steps, routes tasks to capability tiers/skills/delegation via TypeSafe's Jev API, and recommends gated Git publish actions after independent review.

name: dsh-auto-review-jev
description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that routes every tool call under the Auto permission preset through TypeSafe Jev's numeric risk scoring, locally combining scores into fail-closed allow/deny verdicts and letting the human override a single denied call.

name: jevvy
description: Jevvy is a local Next.js playground for exercising TypeSafe AI decisions—compose a shared state with Choice, Score, and Noul questions, run them live with your own API key, and inspect typed answers—plus an arcade where Jev pilots a space shooter from text radar.

name: jev-mobile
description: jev-mobile is a durable Android automation sub-agent that turns high-level tasks into safe, verified USB-device operations by persisting work in SQLite and looping observe→normalize→decide→mutate→verify with TypeSafe Jev choosing only prevalidated semantic actions.

name: dehydrator
description: Dehydrator is a Python library that wraps Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible LLM clients to replace large tool lists with a single `tool_search` tool, performing client-side BM25 and/or Jev-based semantic search (including MCP tools) so only matched tools are sent, and it can also run as an MCP gateway server.

name: pg-jev
description: pg-jev is a PostgreSQL extension that lets you filter, rank, and classify table rows with plain-language conditions via SQL functions (`jev`, `jev_prob`, `jev_score`, `jev_choice`) backed by TypeSafe's Jev model, which returns calibrated probabilities per row—using batched API requests, read-ahead streaming, and session caching—without indexes or embeddings.

name: pi-jev-guard
description: Pi extension that pre-reviews proposed code edits against Markdown-defined rules via the TypeSafe Jev API, reporting each violation's exact rule text and source line range, with an enforcement mode that blocks noncompliant writes within the configured repository scope.

name: jev-go
description: Go SDK for TypeSafe's Jev API that provides a client (configured via `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or functional options for API key, HTTP client, and base URL) to submit `SystemOne` evaluation requests with `NoulQuestion`, `ChoiceQuestion`, and `ScoreQuestion` types returning matching typed answers, surfacing non-2xx responses as `*APIError` with status, headers, and body for caller-managed retry logic.

name: jev
description: Jev is TypeSafe AI's structured decision model: it answers typed yes/no, choice, and rubric-score questions over a given state in one ~100ms parallel call with calibrated confidence and no text generation, suiting high-volume classification, routing, verification, and agents.

name: jev-linkedin-filter-extension
description: A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that filters LinkedIn's feed by sending post text directly from the browser to the Jev API with a user-supplied key, hiding posts matching blocked topics, optionally requiring matches to allowed topics, and displaying checked/hidden counts without an app backend.

name: jev-triage
description: A dependency-free Go CLI that batch-triages text messages through TypeSafe AI's Jev decision API—returning typed category, urgency score, and frustration probability per message in parallel requests—then prints an urgency-sorted table, routes low-confidence items to a manual-review list, and writes an HTML report.

name: jev-tower
description: jev-tower is a zero-dependency Node air-traffic-control loop that feeds live or replayed ADS-B tracks over San Francisco Bay to TypeSafe's Jev model, vets each conflict call with deterministic Paielli-Erzberger physics, and renders hazards on an E2B-hosted dashboard.

name: wellposed
description: wellposed is a zero-dependency CLI and agent skill that lints TypeSafe jev requests against 35 structural rules (broken references, missing "none of the above" options, oversized data), adds optional jev-based semantic checks, and self-scores against a labelled corpus.

name: smartnof1
description: A Node.js experiment harness that extracts reusable typed Jev primitives from recorded Claude trading-agent reasoning—matched to questions, reviewed, and composed into simulated paper-trading decisions—with Nansen smart-money wallet data powering a specialized cluster, keyless offline demo, and configurable multi-agent comparisons.

name: genigrep
description: genigrep is a CLI tool, MCP server, and library that answers codebase questions by using ripgrep keyword search plus a cheap judge model to rank files and passages, returning only relevant verbatim source excerpts with paths and line numbers to cut agent search cost and time.

name: jevbench
description: jevbench is a preregistered, reproducible harness that tests whether the Jev model's confidence calibration degrades on ChaosNLI items with high human-annotator disagreement, computing bias-corrected ΔECE across equal-size easy/hard strata under hash-pinned data.

name: typed-lm
description: typed-lm is a Rust monorepo whose Candle-based server answers typed questions (noul/choice/score) from local Llama/Qwen/Mistral/Gemma logits in one batched forward pass over a Jev-compatible HTTP API, while its trainer produces LoRA/QLoRA adapters and FP8/FP4 quantized artifacts for deterministic, free-text-free inference on CPU, CUDA, or Metal.

name: pajama-zero
description: PajamaZero is a FastAPI/LangGraph clinical triage engine that uses deterministic JEV decisions to sort portal messages into five acuity lanes in ~65ms, diverting emergencies, delegating routine work, prompting visits, and auto-resolving clutter to cut physician pajama time.

name: cultivar
description: Cultivar is a CLI tool for testing agent skills against YAML-defined tasks, running evals locally or in isolated Modal sandboxes across Claude, Copilot, and Gemini runners, grading results against criteria, and iterating via traces, benchmarks, and parallel repeats.

name: jev-security-scan
description: A Python 3.10+ CLI and Agent skill that statically audits Agent Skills, MCP configs and source code before installation or execution, combining offline pattern checks with optional TypeSafe Jev model analysis to flag prompt injection, credential theft, exfiltration, and supply-chain risks with file/line evidence, verdicts, exit codes, and explicit coverage gaps.

name: jev-usher
description: jev-usher is a preview-stage CLI, Claude Code plugin, and TypeScript library that uses TypeSafe's JEV model to route launch prompts to a suitable Claude model tier and selectively filter noisy tool output within budgets while preserving originals for recovery, reducing context size without losing the ability to restore filtered content.

name: pi-typesafe
description: Pi extension exposing TypeSafe's Jev judgment model as a `typesafe_evaluate` tool returning calibrated probabilities for batched choice/score/noul questions, plus terminal test/playground commands and a typed client API with shared auth, spend tracking, and daily budget caps.

name: jev-browser-plugin
description: Agent plugin that teaches agents to automate websites from high-level goals via the Mac `jev-browser` CLI's indexed controls—instead of screenshot-based computer-use—bundling skills for CLI invocation, JSON output parsing, and setup on a registered Mac host.

name: jev-experiments-public
description: Code, frozen benchmarks, and saved predictions for training a Qwen3.5-2B judge that scores typed probability questions without generating text, plus studies comparing it with Jev and LLM agent judges on proof-spec auditing and AI-text detection.

name: kev.js
description: kev.js is a browser library that runs Kev decision models (0.8B–9B) entirely client-side in a Web Worker on WebGPU or WASM via onnxruntime-web, reproducing kev.serve's System One calibrated-probability request/response API—quantized int8 weights, checkpoint-fitted temperature, GPU cache reuse, and Hugging Face bundles—with measured parity to the PyTorch reference.

name: jev-pii-guardrail
description: A UiPath prior-authorization triage agent whose TypeSafe Jev guardrail scores each model boundary for per-type PII probability and patient identifiability, logging detections fail-open without masking or blocking, plus Action Center escalation and a reviewer-note return loop.

name: pi-jev-sentinel
description: A guard for coding agents that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to judge each tool call's intent and risk, screen tool outputs for prompt injection, and check finished replies—shipping as a Pi extension and as Claude Code/Codex CLI hooks, with secret scrubbing.

name: jev-go
description: A Go client for TypeSafe's Jev model that returns typed judgments—yes/no probabilities, option distributions, and weighted scores—instead of generated text, with parallel question batteries, concurrent batching, retries, and typed errors so application code keeps policy and thresholds.

name: entune
description: Entune is an open-source, cross-platform dictation app that transcribes speech via cloud or local models, keeps recordings local, learns a personal dictionary, and applies only context-fitting corrections via a decision model, with macOS shortcut dictation into other apps.

name: jev-codex-workbench
description: A Codex plugin that gates Jev semantic judgments—routing, ranking, triage, verification—behind a local no-network policy classifier and expiring workspace-scoped grants, reducing unnecessary context expansion while keeping Jev output untrusted and unable to authorize actions.

name: TypeSafe
description: TypeSafe is a SwiftPM client for the TypeSafe System One API mirroring the official JavaScript SDK, letting Swift code ask typed noul, choice, and score questions and decode structured answers via an async client configured with TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

name: agentic-sop
description: SOP is a local-first, provider-neutral CLI orchestrator for agentic software development where AI agents perform bounded implementation work while a deterministic, model-free engine owns state transitions, scheduling, retry bounds, validation, merge eligibility, and explicit human approval gates.

name: jevmeter
description: jevmeter is a CLI that gives any video a live BS meter: it transcribes speech, scores every sentence with Jev's calibrated yes/no probabilities via presets (debate, earnings call, podcast, sales pitch) or custom JSON questions, flags dodges, and renders a postable 16:9 edit with highlights, hyperlapse, and scoreboards.

name: geo-citation-diagnostic
description: A GEO/AEO diagnostic tool that queries web-grounded AI answer engines (Gemini, OpenAI, Perplexity) with a question about your site, checks whether your domain was cited or mentioned, compares your pages against cited sources using typed Jev judgments, and reports the biggest content gap plus one prioritized fix.

name: crowdcut-jev-hedra
description: CrowdCut is a live, audience-directed story demo where viewers' comments steer Hedra-rendered video scenes that cut on the previous scene's last frame, with rewindable shared playback, signed guest handles, rate-limited moderated commenting, owner controls, and an optional always-on Cloudflare Worker producer.

name: python-jev-if
description: A Python helper (`jev_if.py`) exposing `jev()` and `jev_probability()` functions that let ordinary `if` statements branch on yes/no natural-language questions about JSON-serializable `state` data, using TypeSafe's Jev/Noul API with a configurable probability threshold (default 0.5), selectable model, exception-based error handling, and mock-driven tests that run without an API key.

name: astra-jev-harness
description: A local harness for Codex CLI and Codex Desktop that uses the Jev model to select only relevant repository files as context before the Astra model generates code, with dependency retention, freshness checks, sandboxed verification, and explicit apply — though measured token savings were minimal.

name: obsidian-cli-memory-bank-skill
description: A cross-runtime CLI skill that gives AI coding agents persistent project memory in an Obsidian vault by scaffolding linked notes, logging sessions, retrieving context, auditing graph health, and compacting noisy run history into a navigable Markdown knowledge base.

name: typesafe-sdk-rust
description: Rust client for the TypeSafe AI API that sends named questions (noul, choice, or score) about a state payload to System One and returns typed answers, with a typestated builder, configurable retries and timeouts, async/blocking modes, and Python SDK 0.6.0 parity.

name: go-jev
description: Go SDK for TypeSafe Jev's decision-only API—returning typed answers (yes/no probability, choice, score) instead of text—featuring a functional-options client, per-request and batched multi-question evaluation, 429/529 retries, and jev-cli, a UNIX-pipeline tool with grep-style filtering, line-parallel mode, and exit-status gating.

name: jev-pruner
description: A Claude Code plugin that runs TypeSafe's Jev on Bash stdout exceeding ~10,000 estimated tokens, scoring line-chunks against session history to omit noise as `[N lines omitted]` markers while preserving diagnostics, whole documents, and a full-output archive—reducing context carried into later turns without summarizing.

name: yardsort
description: Yardsort is a cross-platform desktop app that runs multiple terminal coding agents in isolated git worktrees, with live diffs, resumable sessions, handoffs, workflows, pull-request actions, notifications, local activity records, and a scriptable `ys` CLI.

name: tracky
description: Tracky is a browser extension that adds meaning-based find-in-page search across web pages and locally rendered PDFs, highlighting only verified exact text slices (never fabricated quotes) via a loopback helper or a bring-your-own-key direct mode.

name: jeff
description: jeff is a self-hosted implementation of TypeSafe's jev System One API powered by the 400M-parameter GLiFormer model, serving SDK-compatible choice, score, and noul classification endpoints more cheaply than jev, though less accurately on reasoning-heavy tasks.

name: jev-leftpad
description: jev-leftpad is a satirical Node.js 20+ package that left-pads a value by sending one non-retried TypeSafe API request per call, where the "Jev" model picks among criteria `space_0`–`space_10` to decide how many spaces (max 10) JavaScript prepends—a costly, failure-prone alternative to `padStart()` not meant for production.

name: J3v
description: J3v is a compiler that distills the Laya cross-encoder into calibrated edge artifacts for Raspberry Pi and no_std MCUs, gating emission on accuracy/ECE bounds and flash/RAM budgets and serving calibrated probabilities via a thresholded cascade using Laya's POST /v1/systemone API.

name: hunk-triage
description: A hunk extension that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to reorder changed files into review-priority groups—core, supporting, tests, fixtures, docs, config, mechanical, generated—using commit or pull-request context, with caching and configurable model, timeout, and threshold settings.

name: typesafe-sdk-swift
description: TypeSafe AI Swift SDK is a dependency-free Swift 6 client for the TypeSafe AI API supporting macOS/iOS/tvOS/watchOS, offering typed SystemOne questions, model listing, retries, cancellation, injectable transports, and backend-proxy or direct API-key authentication.

name: jev-judge
description: Turns a structured legal case record (facts, evidence, arguments, law, precedents) into a probabilistic ruling—prevailing party, remedy, findings, strength scores—with calibrated confidence, via a one-case UI or resumable batch CLI scored against real outcomes.

name: jevmoji
description: Jevmoji is a Cloudflare Worker + Vite web app that scores up to 40 characters of input text against a generated Unicode emoji catalog using TypeSafe's Jev model, returning many ranked emoji matches alongside a keyword-based local "hits" shortlist while keeping the API key server-side.

name: jev-guard
description: jev-guard is a Python library and CLI that wraps LLM apps with input/output guardrails, using the non-generative Jev typed-question model to return explainable allow/review/block verdicts (with severity-weighted confidence, reasons, and cost) in 70–500 ms via YAML-defined policies, multiple online/offline backends, and integrations for OpenAI, Anthropic, agents, and tool calls.

name: jevinize
description: A Claude Code skill that transforms a described use case into a working classifier/router system powered by simple-jev, scaffolding the routing logic that directs inputs to the appropriate handler.

name: typesafe-sdk-python
description: Python SDK for TypeSafe AI that installs via `uv add typesafe-sdk` and provides a `TypeSafeClient` (authenticated via `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) whose `system_one` method classifies input state into structured `Choice` categories defined by instructions and criteria, returning typed results.

name: jevlint
description: jevlint is a concurrent Jev-backed semantic linter that lints files matched by configurable rule sets against Markdown-defined rules with error/warning severities, caching each verdict, localizing violating lines, and streaming watch-mode JSON diagnostics for its bundled VS Code extension.

name: RSI-Jev
description: RSI-Jev is a recursively self-improving research loop that trains and serves small System One models answering typed questions (yes/no, pick-one-of-k, rubric ratings) about documents in a single ~10 ms forward pass, plus tools to serve, load, retrain, and benchmark them.

name: dynajev
description: Dynajev turns a frozen open-weight LLM into a request-time decision model: each typed question (noul, choice, score, flags, quote, open) compiles a custom output head over shared prefill and early exit, returning structured answers with zero generated tokens and lower latency.

name: sensibility
description: A Claude Code plugin that gives Claude a ~0.5s, ~$0.00005 second opinion by routing small judgment calls (does a diff match its ticket, is a Bash command risky) to Jev, TypeSafe's answer-only model, through reusable JSON "batteries" of questions whose gates return act/confirm/escalate verdicts, with optional hooks that auto-check Bash commands and unfinished turns.

name: jev-preflight
description: A Claude Code plugin that snapshots a private Git baseline each turn and sends the redacted diff to TypeSafe's Jev API, scoring eight risk axes so high-risk changes get one focused re-investigation before finishing, while failing open on errors.

name: jev-langfuse-trial
description: A Python harness that runs Jev semantic-correctness signals into a GPT-4o Langfuse managed evaluator, supports paired Jev-enabled/Jev-disabled runs and a 10-case benchmark, and records traces and scores for comparing semantic-equivalence judgments.

name: jgrep
description: A grep-style CLI filter that matches lines, paragraphs, diff hunks, functions, or JSON/CSV fields against a plain-language description by scoring each record with the Jev decision model's yes/no probability — fast and cheap enough to sit in a pipe on live streams like `tail -f`.

name: gavel
description: An OpenClaw plugin exposing a `jev_decide` tool that lets agents make structured decisions — probabilities, option picks, and rubric scores with calibrated confidence — via TypeSafe's Jev model on OpenRouter in ~200ms for ~$0.00002, replacing slower, costlier LLM calls.

name: jevwright
description: A Playwright/Chromium test tool where business flows are written as user-worded steps an AI grounds to controls once and replays deterministically, while code—declared requests, verify callbacks, invariants—decides pass/fail with evidence-backed failure attribution.

name: jev-compaction
description: A context-management library and HTTP sidecar that has the Jev model score, gate, compress into losslessly expandable pointers, supersede, and recall agent tool outputs—without generating text—preserving prompt cache, quarantining injections, and cutting request size and cost.

name: flagship-jev
description: A dependency-free TypeScript source library for Cloudflare Workers that uses Jev semantic matching on fuzzy application attributes to select Flagship feature-flag rules, while the native Flagship binding retains final evaluation, rollout, and default handling.

name: jev-gate
description: A Claude Code plugin that routes coding work through a cheap Jev judge—deciding whether a request runs directly or is decomposed by a strong planner, then picking a Claude tier (haiku–fable) per task behind an execution guard—so frontier models are reserved for the hard parts.

name: jev-drone
description: A research prototype where the Jev model autonomously flies a simulated PX4 X500 drone through an eight-room Gazebo house—choosing tasks and movement controls from structured camera/depth observations and memory to find a hidden marker—with a replayable browser demo, mission runner, safety auditing, and video export tooling.

name: lintpal
description: LintPal is a CLI and GitHub Action that enforces repository-owned, plain-English Markdown rules against committed pull-request diffs, emitting line-anchored findings with a configurable severity gate, deterministic inline GitHub review comments, and JSON/Markdown artifacts for CI.

name: jev-comment-triage
description: A WordPress plugin that auto-moderates comments with the TypeSafe Jev model—scoring spam, scam/phishing, and toxicity in an asynchronous per-minute WP-Cron drain that approves, spams, or holds comments without blocking submission or overriding the site's own moderation policy.

name: heyreach-jev-bot
description: HeyReach-jev-bot is a Claude Code-driven CLI that uses the Jev model to score HeyReach leads and first-message variants against your ICP, predict reply probability (optionally calibrated on your inbox history), and write ranked lead lists and draft campaigns back to HeyReach without ever sending messages.

name: jevidence
description: Python sandbox that replays TypeSafe Jev issue-triage judgments through an editable routing policy to propose queues and review hints offline, benchmark thresholds against labeled records without further model calls, and optionally make one live API request.

name: consort
description: Consort is a Bun/PostgreSQL web app that recommends LLMs for a described task via OpenRouter's Jev Decisions endpoint, presenting swipeable model profiles to pass or match and exporting a shareable match card, without running the selected model.

name: jev-rubik-solver
description: Interactive article and Bun CLI demonstrating a small hosted model solving 98/100 random-state Rubik's cubes within 100 face turns via grouped decision menus over supplied algorithms, with recorded replays, a request/response inspector, offline verification, and budget-capped live solves.

name: TiVM
description: TiVM is a computer-use test agent that drives a disposable Dockerized Linux desktop, perceiving apps via the AT-SPI accessibility tree, planning with GPT or TypeSafe Jev, acting through a11y invoke or xdotool, and exporting verdicts, timelines, and videos per run.

name: discern
description: Discern is an Effect v4 library that batches provider-neutral `DecisionModel` judgments (classifications, probabilities, ratings) into type-safe pattern-matching policies and routable procedures, treating uncertain model output as an explicit branch instead of silently rounding it away.

name: arbiter
description: arbiter serves typed-decision models on NVIDIA GPUs or Apple Silicon, exposing a Jev-compatible HTTP API where one `/v1/systemone` call returns every question's typed answer (noul, choice, score) with probabilities in tens of milliseconds via a single forward pass.

name: jev-rules
description: A Claude Code plugin that asks the Jev decision model, per prompt and per edited file, which of a project's Markdown rules and codebase-map documents apply, injecting only the matches in under a second and failing open to all rules on any error.

name: konsitent-jev
description: konsitent-jev pairs Vercel's Konsistent structural checks (which files, imports, or exports must exist) with Jev's API-based source review of behavioral requirements like retry idempotency, exposing a `check` CLI, agent post-edit hooks, and runnable examples to catch correctness issues tests and lint rules miss.

name: jev-eval-agent
description: A benchmark agent with 100 mocked tools (eve + OpenRouter) that measures the steps, calls, tokens, and efficiency needed to finish 6 tasks when the LLM picks tools itself versus when TypeSafe's Jev classifier routes each step, with a results dashboard.

name: jev-buildathon-team-aymaan
description: A hands-on buildathon tool for evaluating and constraining four unsafe domain agents, bundling task-running CLI commands, transcripts, and policy/Jev hooks to detect failures, block harmful tool calls, and measurably improve behavior.

name: jev-ultrafast
description: jev-ultrafast is a browser-use tool built for maximum speed, providing ultra-fast browser operations when execution latency is the priority.

name: jev-tweet-radar
description: A Chrome MV3 extension that scores each X timeline post and your drafts with one Jev (TypeSafe System One) API call, showing calibrated probabilities for engagement-worthiness and tags like spam/buzz/AI-ish, with goal-aware judging, opacity-based timeline filtering, reply-context scoring, and per-day cost tracking.

name: nimble
description: Nimble scores text against a flat schema of enum and boolean questions, returning the chosen answer and per-candidate probabilities from a single forward pass without generating reasoning, and provides the contrastive data-curation and LoRA fine-tuning recipe for its 9B model.

name: bouncer
description: Bouncer is a PreToolUse judgment layer for agent tool calls that asks plain-English policy questions via a cheap, fast judgment model returning probabilities checked against YAML-owned thresholds, flanked by deterministic hard rules and fast paths, with calibration gating enforcement.

name: swift-typesafe
description: Swift 6.4 SDK for TypeSafe AI mirroring the Python 0.7.0 API, providing macro-generated typed and runtime-dynamic question schemas, retry/backoff policies, typed errors, swift-log logging with credential redaction, and pluggable HTTP transports on Apple platforms and Linux.

name: rust-bevy-jev-ants
description: A Bevy ant-colony demo where each ant queries the TypeSafe Jev model every ~2s for intents chosen from runtime-built, vision-scoped options—rejected below a 0.22 confidence threshold—then executed by a classical 60 Hz simulation, with live-editable prompt files, per-request inspection, and CLI probe/measure/compare modes.

name: dejevu
description: A Python browser agent that drives Chrome via CDP with any OpenAI-compatible model, issuing one guarded JSON action per settled page state, and matches or beats specialized decision-model agents on verified Google Flights and Wikipedia benchmarks.

name: jev-spring-boot-bookstore
description: A Spring Boot 4 bookstore API demonstrating TypeSafe Jev via jev-spring-boot-starter for automated genre/audience tagging, review moderation with sentiment and inferred ratings, and natural-language recommendations atop Spring MVC, JPA, and seeded H2.

name: Tranche
description: Tranche is a self-contained Rust CLI that snapshots a public GitHub repo's open PRs, scores each via batched Jev model judgments on category, risk, and duplication, groups likely duplicates into reviewable batches, and publishes bound reports plus an HTML workbench for human triage.

name: JevWantstoBeaMillionaire
description: A reverse quiz-show game where a jailed LLM agent (claude, codex, gemini, or copilot) writes questions to stump Jev, a probability-only decision-model contestant climbing a 15-rung money ladder, with a cross-vendor referee, tamper-evident logs, and human play-along.

name: Daybow
description: Daybow is a Chrome extension that uses the Jev model to auto-categorize and color-code Google Calendar events—predicting categories from titles as you type, painting chips before Google finishes saving, and writing Calendar API labels that sync to phones.

name: bonsai-decision-engine
description: A tool that runs the 5.95 GB ternary Bonsai 2 27B as a generation-free typed decision model on one RTX 4060 8GB, returning calibrated probabilities over declared options (192/231 public231, ECE 0.037) via local API, CLI, and Python client.

name: open-jev
description: openjev is a CLI and HTTP server that scores pre-written options against a context using a local Gemma 3 4B on Apple silicon via MLX — prefill once, batch-score all options in one forward pass — with normalization modes, a TypeSafe System One-compatible API, evals, benchmarks, and trainable heads on frozen features.

name: clash-jev
description: clash-jev plays Clash Royale on a real Android device, converting adb video into JSON game state via OpenCV and a hand-trained troop classifier, then querying TypeSafe's Jev model for strategy/card/square picks, which it validates, taps, and logs with synced video for analysis.

name: Visual-Jev
description: Visual Jev answers many independent multiple-choice questions about one image by normalizing backbone LM-head logits over each question's supplied choices, caching the visual encoding and shared context once so batched questions reach 5.7 ms amortized via an answer-supervised Qwen3-VL-4B LoRA.

name: jev-mcp
description: An eval-first MCP server for TypeSafe's Jev judgment model that provides `jev_ask` for prototyping questions against a single state, `jev_map` for batching question sets over many items without flooding agent context, and `jev_eval` for measuring variants against labeled data with accuracy, calibration, and threshold-sweep metrics so thresholds are evidence-based rather than guessed.

name: ulka
description: Ulka is an experimental local Chromium extension combining FX planning, Jev action selection, Vercel AI Gateway models, accessibility-tree observation, approvals, evidence capture, and Stagehand-style observe/act/extract primitives for supervised browser automation.

name: open-jev
description: A PyTorch reconstruction of a "system one" model that encodes JSON-like state once with a bidirectional transformer, then answers many typed questions in a single parallel forward pass via type-constrained readout heads (boolean, choice, ordinal score) plus evidential confidence and a calibration loss.

name: clearbook
description: Clearbook is an Express/React app that parses uploaded bank statements (CSV or PDF) and uses TypeSafe's Jev model to categorize every transaction, select beneficiary names from narration spans without generating them, account for VAT/EMTL/bank fees, and route low-confidence answers to a human review queue.

name: mnemon-memory-agent
description: Mnemon is a long-term memory agent for LLM assistants that keeps conversations as raw dated records and, per question, uses a fast System 1 decision model to judge retrieved records while a System 2 LLM plans searches and composes answers from minimal context.

name: toolgate-experiment
description: An experimental harness that separates tool selection from business execution, benchmarking direct MCP access against three designs (agent-initiated, host-first, and parallel binary suitability) using Go/Rust cores and a TypeScript SDK to measure end-to-end latency.

name: mysql-ailike
description: A native MySQL plugin that adds an `AILIKE` operator and `ailike()` function for filtering rows and comparing text columns against natural-language conditions, enabling semantic search and relationship-based joins evaluated via TypeSafe API calls.

name: Qwansh
description: Qwansh is a local discriminative Transformer decision model that encodes a shared state once, scores all caller-supplied answer candidates in a single batched pass, and returns schema-valid probability distributions for yes/no, multi-choice, and ordinal-score questions.

name: decision-index
description: Reproduction kit for the Decision Index benchmark that rebuilds the frozen 38-benchmark suite from public sources, runs typed decision engines locally or as a Hugging Face Job with checkpoint/resume, and scores results with the leaderboard's own chance-corrected scorers.

name: jev-reflex-autonomy-lab
description: An interactive multi-drone autonomy simulation where 1–15 drones steer via TypeSafe Jev System 1 reflexes that can asynchronously consult an optional OpenRouter System 2 planner when confidence drops, with seeded scenarios, per-drone telemetry, latency/confidence charts, and JSON export for comparing solo reflexes against guided flight.

name: ask-jev
description: Ask Jev provides an AskJev CLI, Dockerized stdio MCP server, and Astra skills that submit typed Noul, Choice, and Score checks to TypeSafe, letting agents validate interpretations, plans, edits, analyses, tool results, and completion claims against evidence during ongoing work.

name: privatemode-decisions-benchmark
description: A reproducible benchmark suite that compares three System One decision APIs (Privatemode's enclave-hosted GLM-5.3-Flash, TypeSafe Jev, and local Laya) on 29 labelled datasets, measuring accuracy, latency, billed cost, capability limits, and memorisation under controlled conditions with resumable runs.

name: jev-sdk-go
description: A zero-dependency Go client (Go 1.24+) for the TypeSafe AI "System One" API that submits content alongside named yes/no, multiple-choice, or rubric-scored questions and returns each answer with its underlying probabilities, offering typed generic answers, request validation, retries with backoff, configurable timeouts, logging, and support for alternate gateways like OpenRouter.

name: systemone-poc
description: POC wiring the System One classifier (hosted Jev or local Laya) as a preflight decision layer into coding-agent harnesses Pi, OpenCode, and DSH via MCP server and native plugin—deciding inspect/implement/test/clarify before the agent starts—with demo app and eval reports.

name: jev-cli
description: jev-cli is a Python-stdlib CLI and pi extension that turns program or business state descriptions into structured Jev decisions—binary probabilities, option choices, or scores—for routing, classification, urgency gating, and workflow gates via TypeSafe direct or OpenRouter.

name: toolJev
description: toolJev is an MCP gateway that collapses hundreds of upstream MCP servers into two tools — `search` to find the right tool and `execute` to run sandboxed Python calling tools plus Jev, a calibrated decision model that makes per-item judgements without LLM turns — cutting tokens, cost, and calls at scale.

name: jev-doom
description: jev-doom runs the Jev model in real Freedoom via ViZDoom, with a local dashboard showing game frames, choices, probabilities, navigation, latency and cost, editable standing orders, a persistent $15 spend cap, and TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway providers.

name: rot-guard
description: A Chrome extension that asks the TypeSafe Jev API whether each YouTube video, X post, or article serves your goals, then blocks or collapses what doesn't—with escalating time limits, per-item verdicts, creator reputation, one-shot appeals, and cached decisions, all without a server.

name: jev-digest
description: jev-digest is an MCP/Python/CLI tool that searches the web or reads local Markdown, text, HTML, and PDF files, returning verbatim, source-cited passages grouped by topic with gap and disagreement flags, cutting agent input tokens and tool rounds.

name: jarviscore-framework
description: JarvisCore is an Apache-2.0 Python runtime for multi-agent systems: agents discover each other over a SWIM gossip mesh, claim crash-durable workflow steps from Redis (surviving `kill -9`), and invoke 150+ services through a zero-trust credential vault — no central orchestrator.

name: laya-vs-jev
description: An Apple Silicon tool that races a local MLX typed-decision model (Laya) against TypeSafe's hosted API model (Jev) in Chrome's T-Rex game, with live latency charts, safety overrides, crash replays, and 1080p run export for comparing on-device versus cloud inference.

name: jev-search
description: jev-search is a macOS desktop app (Python + Electron) that finds files, documents, and code via ⌘⌥Space using fresh per-search local retrieval with no pre-indexing, optionally re-ranking top candidates with JEV through an OpenRouter key while working fully offline without one.

name: decide-mcp
description: A local stdio MCP server exposing a `decide` tool that delegates decisions to a configurable model—defaulting to TypeSafe AI Jev via AI Gateway—returning a recommended choice with percentage distributions, plus routable decision-policy profiles, per-profile tools, and multi-provider support.

name: jev-no-bullshit
description: A Stop-hook plugin for Claude Code and Codex that uses TypeSafe's Jev yes/no model to verify each assistant's final summary against its actual tool actions, flagging unverified claims, weasel words, empty rhetoric, and paltering, and forcing honest rewrites.

name: jev-mailroom
description: jev-mailroom is a local read-only mail-triage PoC: .eml fixtures feed a fake IMAP server, a listener gets 11 typed Jev answers per email in one call, Python rules assign kind/category or review, and a no-build dashboard polls results.jsonl.

name: jev-lint
description: jev-lint is a CLI/CI linter that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to catch meaning-dependent problems in HTML and JS/TS—like a "Postal code" field typed `number`—that pattern-matching linters miss, reporting each finding with evidence.

name: jev-clinical-trial-prototype
description: Local web app that screens ~500 synthetic clinical notes against editable trial criteria via TypeSafe's Jev model, streaming per-note results over SSE with hash-based caching, confidence-slider re-rolls, flip tracking, calibration eval, and Claude-compiled criteria.

name: jev-oas-sentinel
description: A CLI tool and GitHub Action that compares two OpenAPI documents to catch behavioral breaking changes—combining deterministic structural diff checks (removed operations, required parameters, enum narrowing) with probabilistic semantic evaluation of changed descriptions, defaults, retries, ordering, pagination, authorization, and error semantics, producing pass/review/block verdicts with SARIF, J

name: swenai-nansen
description: A Nansen API integration layer and runnable demo for the Swenai trading assistant on Hyperliquid, using six endpoints to split wallet cohorts, source divergence signals, veto trades against top-holder outflows, and disarm orders when smart money is positioned opposite.

name: progressgate
description: ProgressGate is a TypeScript SDK that supervises agent trajectories via TypeSafe Jev semantic signals and a deterministic policy, detecting when differing actions repeat the same contradicted assumption and returning CONTINUE/WARN/REPLAN/HALT decisions with fail-open defaults to stop wasteful spinning without naïve step counters.

name: jev-workflow
description: jev-workflow is a TypeScript library that drives iterative workflows by having the Jev model pick the next action from a described set, while the application owns state, supplies only decision-relevant facts, executes chosen actions, and calls `update()` to continue as state changes.

name: Jev-Calibration
description: A calibration guide showing how to make Jev's returned answer probabilities match observed accuracy — recommending isotonic regression over Platt scaling (ECE 0.117→0.008 on held-out data, effective with 20–100 labeled examples), with practical thresholds for trusting Noul and Choice outputs.

name: pi-jev-context
description: pi-jev-context is an opt-in, reversible Pi extension that sends session history to the TypeSafe Jev judgment service to score older messages for relevance, hiding low-scoring tool exchanges and assistant text from future model context—without deleting them—via configurable threshold, protected buffer, branch-aware caching, and `/jev` commands.

name: smart-switch
description: SmartSwitch is a macOS menu-bar window switcher that, on ⌘`, sends your recent app-switching history (dwell times, time of day, last 10 manual ⌘Tab switches) to TypeSafe's Jev model to predict and activate the most likely next window, falling back to the last-used app on failure or 1 s timeout.

name: jev-vampire-survivors
description: A local bridge that lets a TypeSafe Jev agent (or your own controller) play Vampire Survivors by exposing player state, enemies, pickups, inventory and menu actions over localhost, with bounded runs, cost/latency limits, and gameplay recordings annotated with inputs, action probabilities and token usage.

name: Canny
description: Canny is a hook-based warden for Claude Code and Codex CLI that records an append-only ledger of agent actions, blocks "done" claims until a test, build, lint, or type-check passes after the last code edit, denies secret-shaped writes and test-removal edits, and optionally asks Jev for calibrated judgments that can only relax—never harden—its deterministic gates.

name: decio
description: Decio is a Unix-friendly CLI that turns piped or configured context into typed choice, boolean, or score decisions via an API provider, optionally dispatching only pre-declared trusted actions so scripts, hooks, CI/CD, and agents can automate decisions without executing model-generated commands.

name: jev-pii-checker
description: jev-pii-checker is a CLI that scans stdin/files for PII using TypeSafe's Jev API, regexes, and Intl.Segmenter name-span assembly, emitting masked JSON or human reports with severity exit codes to gate sensitive text before LLM use—at the cost of sending scanned content to TypeSafe.

name: claude-herdr-jev-compaction
description: A single-file, stdlib-only Python Stop hook for Claude Code that auto-compacts at task boundaries: once context passes a token threshold, it asks TypeSafe's Jev model whether the task is done, then uses Herdr to type `/compact` into the correct pane, avoiding costly mid-task compaction.

name: jev-rs
description: jev-rs is a Rust engine that turns any LLM's next-token logprobs into calibrated probability answers for typed questions (yes/no, choice, score) in a single prefill—no generated text—serving them via the TypeSafe `/v1/systemone` wire format or an MCP `judge` tool for coding agents.

name: JevScout
description: JevScout is an open-source Node.js toolkit powered by TypeSafe's Jev that condenses oversized MCP responses for Claude Code via a PostToolUse hook—keeping verbatim, exactly recoverable segments—and lets Codex app-server hosts map routine requests to reviewed, authorized, verified fixed commands, cutting agent time and token cost.

name: jev-enforce
description: jev-enforce is a Claude Code plugin and CLI that checks every reply and file edit against CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules using TypeSafe's Jev, blocking violations via hooks and quoting broken rules back so Claude fixes them in the same turn.

name: nospace
description: nospace is a TypeScript library that restores word spacing and corrects typos in English text as the user types (e.g., `ilovecats` → `I love cats`), attaching to inputs/textareas via a DOM helper or headless API backed by server-side spacing (Jev) and spelling (Luna) endpoints, requiring Node 22.12+.

name: jevfilter
description: JevFilter is a zero-dependency Node.js library that converts natural-language search requests into typed, validated filter objects matching a developer-defined schema — with deterministic parsing for dates and numbers, LLM-driven field/value selection, clarification questions for ambiguity, and no generated SQL or permission changes.

name: convoai-jev-vad
description: Client-side turn detection for Agora ConvoAI that replaces server VAD: a ~110 ms acoustic SNR gate opens turns via manualSOS, while TypeSafe Jev judges streamed STT text for turn completion, addressee, and barge-in, issuing manualEOS/interrupt under live-tunable thresholds.

name: jevrealtimecodecheck
description: A VS Code/Cursor extension that checks your local git diff against Markdown-defined coding rules using TypeSafe AI's Jev model — sending only rules matching touched file types, flagging just new violations with severity scores and real line numbers — runnable on save, manually, or in CI on pull requests.

name: jauvex
description: Jauvex is a macOS Electron app that runs Claude Code, Codex, and Grok sessions side by side, adding voice control that steers agents and summarizes replies aloud, agent-to-agent messaging, and a built-in agent that manages and updates the app itself.

name: JevML
description: JevML is a dependency-free TypeScript toolkit of reusable ML primitives—PCA, MCMC sampling, text diffusion, and neural cellular automata—with a catalog/registry and matching/API harness that helps agents select and invoke the right primitive for a task.

name: auto-form-filler-plugin
description: A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that uses the Jev AI model to classify form fields and auto-fill locally stored profiles, handling split Japanese inputs (3-part phone, 2-part postal code, 3-select birthdates), select/radio label variations, and JSON profile import/export—while sending only field metadata (never personal values) to the API and never auto-submitting forms.

name: jev-little-airways
description: A runnable three.js air-traffic demo where every in-flight judgment—divert, hold, give way, declare emergencies, sequence landings—is made live by the Jev decision model as typed, calibrated probabilities in ~150 ms, with a monitor exposing raw API calls and costs.

name: rerank-bench-jev
description: An auditable benchmark that compares TypeSafe's Jev probability-returning model against the Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B cross-encoder as production rerankers on two BEIR datasets, measuring ranking quality, cost per query, and tail latency, with cached responses enabling full recomputation without API keys.

name: sift
description: A Chrome extension that labels every X post and reply as Substance, Humor, Chit-chat, Promo, or Junk plus AI-written and Off-topic flags, letting you hide chosen labels via presets, collapse hidden posts into count lines, and keep search native for ~$0.00003/post.

name: jev-dev
description: A local-first Tauri desktop workbench for experimenting with Jev, providing a JSON-editing playground with confidence results, a key-free Demo mode, Live API requests via a saved TypeSafe API key, an optional demo-only browser preview, and commands to run or bundle the app.

name: agentOS
description: agentOS is a Linux-based agent-first operating system prototype—a complete Debian ARM64 VM with tiling terminal, Rust runtime, Python services, and gateway-backed reasoning—whose validated action broker lets an agent inspect, plan, execute, and retain knowledge under explicit user authorization.

name: jev-ids
description: Jev IDS is a Python CLI that classifies network flows as attack/benign with a category label via one typed request to TypeSafe's Jev System One Model, and benchmarks it on NSL-KDD against LLM, Random Forest, and Isolation Forest baselines with paired statistics.

name: Jevmind
description: Jevmind is a zero-dependency Python CLI that turns agent decisions into typed, confidence-scored questions answered by an offline local brain or the Jev API, enforced by a code gate and logged to a hash-chained ledger that is graded and recalibrated from outcomes.

name: jev-banking77-experiment
description: Documents a reproducible experiment evaluating TypeSafe's general-purpose Jev decision model on the BANKING77 intent-labeling benchmark, showing 92.40% test accuracy—1.26 points below fine-tuned BERT—using only retrieved labeled examples and category definitions for $0.44.

name: jev-frontier-100
description: A 100-question four-choice benchmark comparing Jev against local Qwen3.5 models (0.8B–4B) under controlled thinking budgets, providing frozen questions, graded trial outcomes, paired bootstrap intervals, confidence diagnostics, and an offline harness to recompute all published scores.

name: fitstamp
description: A Chrome extension that stamps every LinkedIn job card and open posting with a resume-fit percentage and confidence score, computed in under a second by the Jev decision model through your own OpenRouter or TypeSafe API key (~$0.0001 per job, cached 7 days).

name: jev-dspy
description: jev-dspy is an experimental FastAPI service that converts a situation plus named typed questions into a dynamic DSPy signature, returning per-question JSON decisions with type-coerced values and confidence scores via any OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway.

name: jev-bookmarks
description: A cross-platform CLI that takes a purpose statement, has Jev pick a matching entry from your Chrome history, drives the browser to operate that page, re-observes the result, and saves only URLs judged useful into a per-Git-project JSON "phonebook" — reusable later without history search and callable as a skill from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Grok Build.

name: jev-shell-history
description: A zsh plugin that provides fish-style autosuggestions ranked by the Jev (TypeSafe) model over your last 100 distinct history entries, showing the top match in grey after the cursor (accept with → or ^E) via non-blocking per-keystroke requests with prefix/fuzzy modes and tunable score thresholds.

name: libtypesafe
description: libtypesafe is an unofficial C++17 client for the TypeSafe AI API that provides non-blocking `Pending<T>` calls driven by `client.pump()`, exception-free `Result<T>` error handling, compile-time-checked answer types, pluggable HTTP transport (libcurl by default), and byte-identical requests to the official Python SDK.

name: jev-revenue-forecaset
description: A Python demo tool that builds a bottoms-up revenue forecast for 1,000 simulated clients, querying Jev at each contract roll date to decide renewals, bucketed ACV changes, and termination reasons, producing lazy Orcaset Series forecasts rollable into cohort revenue tables and churn-by-cause breakdowns.

name: jev-form-filler
description: A Chrome/Edge browser extension that imports your LinkedIn, X, GitHub, and portfolio pages into a reviewed local profile, then uses your own TypeSafe API key to automatically fill web forms — including embedded application forms and file uploads — with source-backed, confidence-scored answers you can inspect and undo before submitting yourself.

name: openai-scala-client
description: An async Scala client exposing OpenAI and other LLM providers (Anthropic, Gemini/Vertex, Groq, Bedrock, more) through one OpenAIService covering typed streaming, chat and Responses APIs, tools/MCP, vision, batching, audio, embeddings, fine-tuning, vector stores, and graders.

name: open-jev-laya
description: open-jev-laya is a Vite/Transformers.js project that runs the multilingual Laya ONNX model entirely in-browser (WebGPU with WASM fallback, ~647 MB fp16 weights fetched from Hugging Face) to power four deployable demos—Chinese decision playground, Gomoku, Big Two, and 3D maze—without any inference server.

name: erabi
