description: Erabi is a Python library providing a local, GLiClass-based (~438M-parameter) decision engine that takes a situation `context`, a `question`, and 2–16 `choices` and returns a probability distribution over all candidates—useful for tool selection, NPC behavior, or command-risk classification—running on PyTorch or ONNX (CPU FP32/GPU FP16) with a 512-token input limit, without generating text o

name: jev-stars
description: jev-stars is a local-first Rust CLI and MCP server that syncs your GitHub stars into a SQLite database with FTS5 full-text search, BGE vector similarity, deterministic repo health scoring (archived/alive/license), cached AI tags, and personal notes, giving coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor bounded, offline context about which starred repos are worth using.

name: jevmod
description: jevmod scores messages for spam, scam, harassment, NSFW, off-topic, self-harm, doxxing, and CSAM plus custom plain-English rules, applying tunable thresholds with logged decisions via CLI, Python/npm SDKs, HTTP API, MCP server, or Discord/Telegram/Reddit/Twitch/YouTube bots.

name: jev-fault-diagnosis-poc
description: A read-only PoC that replays real compressor telemetry through an emulated Modbus device, flags suspect behaviour in code, then asks a pluggable backend (Jev, Claude, or rules) for the manual-grounded fault, severity, and confidence, opening tickets on a live dashboard.

name: software-factory
description: A local software factory CLI that moves queued requests through YAML-defined pipelines of stages run by your installed coding-agent CLIs, shell commands, or typed judgments, each in an isolated git worktree, in parallel, with human-review gates and replayable runs.

name: jev-benchmark
description: A reproducible benchmark that evaluates TypeSafe AI's Jev on classifying agent tool calls as readonly/destructive/privileged/exfiltration using 60 labelled cases, showing 91.7% accuracy, ~400ms latency, and—most importantly—well-calibrated confidence where every error came hedged below 1.000.

name: x-jev-gate
description: x-jev-gate is a Python CLI that pass/fail-gates X post drafts by first hard-blocking secret-like strings (API keys, passwords, local paths) locally, then scoring the text against thresholded yes/no "Noul" questions via TypeSafe Jev's System One — on cloud or a local Ollaya backend — and exiting 0/1/2 so scripts and CI can enforce publish-readiness without auto-posting or LLM critique.

name: jev-feels
description: A Ruby gem that binds declarative LLM-powered predicates (`feels?`), classifications (`decide`), and ordinal ratings (`score`) to model fields via named, reusable definitions, with calibrated probabilities, confidence thresholds, batching, pattern matching, and stub/record/replay test support.

name: jev-experiments
description: A compact Windows PowerShell/WPF demo that turns a folder into a semantic search surface: it sends bounded file metadata to the TypeSafe Jev API for typed decisions, fuses them with deterministic local relevance scoring to rank results, and keeps raw contents private with an offline fallback.

name: typesafe-image-diffusion
description: Generates 16x16 pixel art from text prompts by asking a multiple-choice classifier 256 parallel questions—one per pixel choosing among 16 colors—with optional local-neighborhood refinement passes, served via a FastAPI web UI and API with animated history and token usage.

name: system-one-benchmark
description: A benchmarking suite that compares TypeSafe Jev's cloud "System One" decision model against local MLX parallel constrained decoding and autoregressive Qwen baselines on adversarial and intent prompts, measuring latency, accuracy, safety precision/recall, calibration, and schema-error rates.

name: jev-llm
description: jev-llm coerces TypeSafe Jev — a judgment/classification engine — into an autoregressive language model by decoding token-by-token through multiple-choice candidate selection, offering word, char, hybrid, and syntax-aware code generation modes with temperature sampling, planning, and interactive chat.

name: jevpipe
description: A CLI that pipes lines or files through a calibrated decision model, answering yes/no or typed questions per record in parallel, so agents can semantically filter, classify, and score thousands of items cheaply with confidence scores and cost caps.

name: jev-mail-filter
description: A single Google Apps Script file that auto-filters Gmail using plain-English rules judged by the Jev API every 10 minutes—labeling threads that score above a configurable threshold and optionally archiving them—without requiring a server or OAuth app.

name: typesafe-jev-workflow
description: An async LangGraph demo that classifies mocked emails via TypeSafe's Jev model into a typed `invoice`/`general` Choice and routes them to stub handlers, letting you exercise real intent-detection API calls and verify routing without sending email or payments.

name: decision-lab
description: Decision Lab is a local visual playground for System One decision APIs that lets you build Yes/No, Choice, and Score experiments with evidence, inspect answers and probabilities, compare multiple models on the same input, and run what-if variants — with two key-free simulated demos included and optional connections to hosted Jev/OpenJEV or local Laya endpoints.

name: bagel
description: Bagel is a Dockerized MCP server that lets LLMs answer plain-English questions about robotics, drone, and IoT data (ROS bags, MCAP, PX4, ArduPilot, MQTT, and more) via auditable DuckDB SQL, and turns sentences into edge pipelines that keep only the windows around real events.

name: jev-vs-rerankers
description: A benchmarking tool that evaluates whether TypeSafe's jev (in pointwise, single-call listwise, and batched multi-question arms) can replace dedicated rerankers like bge, Voyage, Cohere, and zerank in a RAG pipeline, comparing nDCG@10, Recall@5, MRR, latency, cost, and calibration-threshold precision on BEIR nfcorpus.

name: commentlint
description: commentlint is a command-line linter that extracts comments across many languages with tree-sitter, evaluates them against configurable TypeSafe.ai yes/no rules such as active voice, and reports file/line failures for CLI, pre-commit, and CI workflows.

name: 15-min-BTC-JAP
description: A live Kalshi BTC 15-minute YES/NO trading desk that streams Coinbase BTC-USD into a TypeSafe "Jev" paper judge and fires at most one $2 order per window via `live_spin.py`, with odds/flow dashboards on ports 3000–3002 and a file-based arm/kill switch.

name: langgraph-jev
description: `langgraph-jev` is a LangGraph/LangChain integration for TypeSafe's Jev probabilistic decision API, providing `JevNode`, `JevRunnable`, `JevClient`, typed question helpers (`choice`, `boolean`, `score`), confidence thresholds, and a `route_by_decision` helper so agent graphs can branch deterministically on typed decisions with probabilities rather than parsed LLM text.

name: open-jev-fast
description: A drop-in local server for Open-Jev-27B that replaces the PyTorch forward pass with custom CUDA kernels, a shared-prefix tree, tuned GEMMs, and per-shape CUDA Graphs, running bf16 inference ~6× faster on a single NVIDIA B300 with unchanged JevBench accuracy.

name: jev-voice
description: jev-voice is a macOS voice-control tool that converts speech into local app launching, typing, site searches, scrolling, shortcuts, media/system actions, and guarded multi-step browser or Accessibility-tree automation for fast hands-free desktop control.

name: jevies
description: A Python toolkit built on the TypeSafe Jev SDK whose helper "Jevs" design and review evaluation setups—recommending question types and instruction structure, checking instruction wording, option overlap, rubric ordering, and answer-space coverage, and validating inputs and test cases against preset rules.

name: browser-use-clef-flash
description: An independent browser-use/jev-ultrafast fork where Cloudflare-hosted Clef picks an operation and indexed DOM target in one request per cycle and GPT-OSS 20B fills text fields—verified to run a Google Flights search in 30.4 seconds.

name: typed_evals
description: A Python library and CLI that judges LLM responses, RAG datasets, and agent traces with Jev models, supporting preset and custom metrics, calibration against human labels, pluggable judge backends, and pre-execution tool guards for LangChain, CrewAI, and Microsoft Agent Framework.

name: open-jev
description: An inference harness that uses DiffusionGemma to produce typed JSON decisions by denoising a fixed token canvas and selecting the highest-logit allowed tokens, enabling training-free, schema-valid structured judgments with batched, cost-measured benchmarking.

name: site-judge
description: A CI check that audits marketing site copy for unsupported claims, combining deterministic regex checks with a probability-returning judgment model validated per-run by known-good/known-bad controls, and reports each flagged claim's sentence and score as an advisory, never-blocking PR comment.

name: jev-trade-cc
description: A point-in-time backtest of an O'Neil momentum strategy where a stateless decision model makes entry/exit calls, with reproducible pipelines, jackknife tests against mechanical rules, and timing/provenance safeguards that honestly measure whether the model adds any edge.

name: mobile-jev
description: A standalone mobile agent that drives a real Android phone through the Mobilerun API using TypeSafe's Jev model for per-step decisions—no ADB—bundling a live React streaming studio, a CLI with preview/execute modes, verified demos, JSONL execution traces, and request-level latency breakdowns for reproducible evaluation.

name: jev-chat-jarvis-mac
description: A macOS floating panel that watches WeChat via Vision OCR and a local 2B model to classify each incoming message's intent and risk, generate tone-tagged reply candidates, and fill them into the input box—read-only, no injection, hooking, or auto-send.

name: jev-emotional-avatar
description: jev-emotional-avatar renders a live Bluesky feed where the character Jev adopts avatars and outfits from user profiles and changes expressions based on post text, served locally in English or Japanese with only Node.js 22+ and a TypeSafe API key.

name: jev-assist
description: jev-assist is a CLI/agent skill that uses TypeSafe Jev to rank tracked files against a task, audit files against repo conventions, gate risky diffs, and validate ranking accuracy, making whole-repo triage cheap enough to catch relevant files grep misses.

name: jcm-router
description: A local Claude Code–Anthropic proxy, jcm-router asks TypeSafe’s Jev for model and effort per request, preserving subscription auth while always routing cold subagents and switching main chats only when cache-rewrite costs justify it, with failover, overrides, logs, and a cost dashboard.

name: jev-guard
description: A real-time risk triage gateway for crypto exchange deposits and withdrawals that uses the Jev decision model to score risk while deterministic Java hard rules, thresholds, and a direction-aware routing matrix make the final auto-pass, manual-review, or freeze decision.

name: decisions-judge-mcp
description: An MCP server exposing a `judge` tool that answers typed questions—yes/no probability, multi-option choice, or ordered-level scoring—about arbitrary JSON state in one request, returning structured, branchable answers (with a guaranteed failure-safe fallback) via TypeSafe's Jev model.

name: jev-commit
description: A commit-msg hook that sends the staged diff and message to TypeSafe's Jev decision model, which scores five checks—filler message, diff contradiction, debug leftovers, unmentioned work, secrets—and blocks only credentials (or findings under --strict), failing open on errors.

name: grev
description: grev is a suite of Unix-style stream filters that uses TypeSafe Jev models to select, label, rank, split, cut, deduplicate, bisect, and probe input by meaning while preserving input as output and exposing calibrated probabilities, budgets, and confirmation controls.

name: tiny-decision
description: Tiny Decision is a Windows desktop platform for running System One decision models in-process at sub-50ms latency, providing confidence calibration (ECE, recalibration), visual DAG pipelines, a vendor-neutral SOMI interface, and one-click export as MCP tools or a REST API.

name: Bud-Decision-Engine
description: Bud Decision Studio runs eleven open decision models locally, returning calibrated probabilities for six typed question kinds over text, images, audio and video, with hardware-aware install, model management, evaluation tools, and a TypeSafe Jev-compatible local API.

name: jev-opus
description: jev-opus drives Claude Code on Opus 5.5 with effort re-picked before each API call — raised when checks fail, lowered when they pass — via per-message effort statements that keep the prompt cache intact, in gateway or headless driver mode.

name: hotel-reviews
description: A dependency-free Python 3.9+ script that collects hotel reviews via Apify, classifies Wi-Fi and noise sentiment with Jev, escalates uncertain or failed cases to GPT-5-mini via OpenRouter, ranks hotels on a smoothed 50/50 score, and prints a GPT-explained verdict with reusable saved results.

name: jev-auto-ime
description: A macOS CLI that watches romaji keystrokes, asks TypeSafe's Jev whether the text is Japanese or English, then auto-switches the input source and retypes pending characters, skipping password fields and excluded apps with a tunable confidence threshold.

name: model-picker
description: A hook plugin for Codex and Claude Code that periodically sends a bounded snapshot of your session to TypeSafe's JEV model and displays recommendations for which model and effort level fit your task—without ever changing settings itself, since no host allows hooks to switch models.

name: jev-snake
description: Jev Snake is a FastAPI real-time Snake game pairing a TypeSafe Jev decision model (latency-immune strategist with natural-language coaching and calibrated probabilities) with a deterministic BFS pathing executor, plus token telemetry, rate limiting, and graceful fallback.

name: semcrawl
description: Semcrawl is a Go CLI tool for browser-based scraping that loads URLs in headless Chrome/Chromium, keeps reusable browser sessions via a local daemon, and extracts structured fields from page elements using natural-language descriptions powered by the TypeSafe Jev API.

name: jev-code
description: jev-code is a coding-agent CLI and TypeScript SDK built on the decision-only Jev model: it constructs programs as syntax trees one grammar rule at a time (Python, TS/JS, C, Rust, Go, Lua, Ruby, Bash) with compiler validation, executes them with key-press approval, and exposes a scriptable `decide` command that turns stdin questions into labels, probabilities, or scores with exit-code branching.

name: djev
description: djev is a self-hosted, Jev-compatible `POST /v1/systemone` decision server that makes `noul`, `choice`, and `score` answers bit-for-bit reproducible across load, restarts, and same-model GPUs—via SGLang batch-invariant inference plus patched fp32-aligned linear-attention checkpoints—so routing, moderation, and guardrail branches can be replayed, pinned in tests, audited, and not defeated by re

name: jagged
description: A pre-registered ablation study measuring which of TypeSafe's recommended jaggedness mitigations actually change `jev-1.13`'s accuracy and calibration on Wikipedia Articles-for-Deletion verdict prediction, with committed trial data and scripts to reproduce every result.

name: OpenJev
description: OpenJev is a Windows desktop AI agent—a DeepSeek Harness fork—that consults TypeSafe's Jev decision model at every thinking step for calibrated-probability routing and verification, exposing `jev_*` tools, logging each call to a trace file, and bundling an optional Python CLI/MCP server.

name: Jev-For-Dummies
description: Jev-For-Dummies is a minimal FastAPI wrapper that exposes Jev's decision primitives—choice selection, yes/no boolean evaluation, and numeric scoring—plus a health check as plain HTTP GET endpoints returning JSON results with confidence and probabilities, requiring only a TypeSafe API key and no SDK or Jev knowledge.

name: Bud-Decision-Studio
description: Bud Decision Studio is a cross-platform desktop app that runs eleven open "System One" decision models locally, turning situations and typed questions (choice, scale, yes/no, multi-select, ranking, numeric estimates) into calibrated answer probabilities in milliseconds, with model management, versioned reusable templates, a decision history with labeling and review thresholds, model evaluation lea

name: Jevs-Garage
description: Jev's Garage is a Python 3.11+/uv workshop of 26 runnable demos and a local gallery showing how TypeSafe System One models turn realistic state into typed probabilistic judgments (Choice, Score, Noul) that deterministic policies convert into bounded actions or safe fallbacks across critical, orchestration, and casual scenarios.

name: jev-accessibility-tree
description: A Chrome extension and Bun-based eval harness that uses TypeSafe's Jev probability-returning model to rebuild a web page's accessibility tree (roles, names, landmarks, headings, decorative-image hiding) in ~0.66s per page at ~1/230th the cost of Claude Opus, recovering ~85% of stripped semantics by pairing typed Choice/Noul questions over page-derived candidates with code-enforced invariants and c

name: jev-harness
description: A TypeScript library that turns TypeSafe Jev's structured `choice`/`score`/`noul` answers into production actions via a policy layer, a confidence gate for low-certainty cases, shadow mode, reusable decision recipes, and an offline eval CLI that asserts on actions rather than free text.

name: jev-hooks
description: Lifecycle hooks for Google Antigravity that use TypeSafe's Jev System One model to gate destructive tool calls via blast-radius scoring, dynamically inject the right skill per prompt without token bloat, and compact trajectories verbatim — all at sub-120ms latency.

name: soter
description: Soter is an automated Discord moderation bot that scans every message for hate speech and spam, automatically times out repeat violators, and provides slash commands for configuring channel exemptions, the hate-speech filter, a mod-log channel, and timeout thresholds.

name: wince
description: wince is a CLI that triages any unified diff (branch, PR, or agent output) into a green/yellow/red review-attention verdict with a risk score, suggested reviewers, reasons, and experimental hunk reading order — combining non-overridable deterministic path/size rules with typed per-file model calls — so teams know where to route human review rather than having the tool review code itself.

name: decision-model-testing
description: A repository of reproducible experiments benchmarking TypeSafe Jev general-purpose decision models against LLMs, NLP models, and specialized rerankers for eval judging, RAG filtering, and passage ordering, including code, prompts, and aggregate measurements.

name: peaks-notes
description: A Bun CLI and Claude Code Stop hook that incrementally maintains a topic-organized, token-budgeted markdown summary of completed conversation turns—with source provenance, an append-only archive, and an audit journal—for downstream handoffs and context compaction.

name: jev-feed-filter
description: jev-feed-filter drops paywalled, slanted, opinion or unwanted-topic news stories and YouTube Shorts/livestreams via code checks plus cheap probabilistic Jev model judgments, outputting two HTML digest pages listing every hidden item and its reason.

name: Jev-To-Hackathon
description: A Next.js app that matches hackathon ideas to the best-fitting NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge via Jev's structured evaluations, scoring alignment against customizable weighted criteria to reveal what already fits, what to strengthen, and the official challenge link.

name: OpenRecurSearch
description: OpenRecurSearch is a Node.js web app that answers research questions by recursively searching the web, using a typed-decision model (Jev) to make all branching choices—source selection, deduplication, follow-up picking, coverage checks—while LLM agents only generate, streaming each decision's probabilities and latency to a live chat alongside a markdown report panel.

name: jev-reranking
description: Benchmarks JEV's zero-shot reranking against monoBERT, BM25, and published neural systems on MS MARCO passage/document and WSJ transfer tasks, reporting nDCG@10, MAP, P@10, MRR, per-query latency, and API cost with reproducible protocols and frozen input manifests.

name: typesafe-ai-benchmark
description: A Node.js benchmark harness that runs Qwen 3.8 27B on Cerebras, TypeSafe Jev, and local Needle 3 side-by-side across seven synthetic judgment workloads, recording validated outputs, fixture agreement, latency percentiles, token usage, and API cost via a comparison theater UI with raw exportable results.

name: jev-snake
description: A Snake game where a local server computes legal directions along the shortest reachable routes to the apple each turn, posts the board and candidate moves as a `Choice` question to Jev via the TypeSafe API, validates the returned direction, and advances the snake—keeping the API key server-side and sending no move history.

name: jev-design
description: A Next.js/shadcn logistics console and centrally governed token/family CSS engine that lets the typed Jev model turn a one-sentence brief into a coherent, catalog-constrained visual style across every component, enforced by build-time coverage gates and runtime layout audits.

name: azdaja
description: Azdaja is a recursive language-model layer that keeps full inputs in a persistent local Monty/Python evaluator, giving models a bounded surface for local computation and selective llm/llm_batch recursion—cutting tokens and steps—with optional TypeSafe typed judgments.

name: jev-file-library-organizer
description: A macOS workflow that scans folders for images, PDFs and MP4s, extracts text and video frames locally, renames files with descriptive titles and searchable metadata, verifies SHA-256 fingerprints on every move, and serves a local review dashboard with previews, editing and undo.

name: jev-vs-sovereign-benchmark
description: A benchmark suite comparing TypeSafe AI's Jev System One (`typesafe/jev-1.13` via OpenRouter) against a specialized sovereign RAG stack (DistilBERT, ColBERT-v2, DeBERTa-v3) on UK primary legislation, measuring latency, token cost, abstention, and governance reproducibility across three retrieval nodes, with dry-run and live modes producing percentile tables and SHA-256-sealed telemetry.

name: jev-ultralightspeed
description: A Python library that packs many independent text items into single TypeSafe Jev API requests to answer one judgement question per item, delivering ~32x throughput and ~41% lower cost at unchanged accuracy for batch triage, labeling, and classification queues.

name: kanari-decision-bench
description: Evaluates whether typed-decision models can judge if attack-probe answers from Polish customer-service chatbots are vulnerable, using a stdlib `run.py` that scores any `POST /v1/systemone` server for misses, false alarms and AUC on 189 labeled real answers.

name: jev-chat-jarvis
description: An Android accessibility-service chat copilot that reads on-screen WeChat/QQ/X/Feishu conversations (via UI nodes or offline OCR), uses a Jev judgment model to assess intent and risk in ~1s, and ranks three generated reply drafts it fills in but never sends—enriched by local knowledge-base, contact, and chat-history context.

name: jev-learning-lab
description: A self-contained, fully executed Jupyter course of 42 lessons on building auditable agents from typed decisions—covering extraction, games, planning, evaluation, and an incident-copilot capstone—runnable offline via fixtures or live with an optional API key.

name: worth-replying
description: Worth Replying is a Next.js demo that crawls a given domain, builds a customer profile, generates five X searches, and uses TypeSafe's jev model to score each tweet on five typed criteria—ICP fit, pain, reply value, needs-human, injection—routing conversations worth answering into a review queue, all via one AIsa API key.

name: similarity-ts-jev
description: A CLI and library that detects similar TypeScript functions, types, and classes with similarity-ts and fallow, then has TypeSafe's Jev model judge each pair like a code reviewer, reporting only the duplicates worth merging or refactoring.

name: jevlint
description: jevlint is a linter whose rules are plain-English yes/no questions—e.g., whether a logging call leaks a secret—judged by TypeSafe's Jev model, which returns calibrated probabilities, with fixture tests, mutation-based recall checks, caching, and baselines.

name: stfu
description: stfu is a UserPromptSubmit hook script that, on each prompt, queries an AI for an appropriate answer length and injects that as a limit, forcing terse replies (e.g. "The app listens on port 9090" instead of verbose narration), installable via a Claude settings.json hook and a TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

name: building-with-jev-skill
description: An agent skill for writing and improving programs that call Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, covering question design (Choice, Score, Noul), state structure, answer composition, confidence thresholds, and diagnosing wrong or low-confidence answers, targeting `jev-1.13` and installable via Claude Code plugin, skills CLI, or manual copy.

name: jev-demo
description: A Next.js demo dashboard that triages GitHub issues into five typed Jev-1.13 decisions—category, severity, urgency, team, and actionability—with calibrated confidence thresholds, live timing/cost metrics, and Kanban or action-based views for automatic routing versus human review.

name: jev-demofast
description: jev-demofast is a CLI that turns a single sentence into a narrated MP4/GIF product demo by driving a real browser with the Jev decision model, optionally guided by a source-code-generated map of your app, with dry-run safety guards, voiceover, and replay logs.

name: jev-seo
description: jev-seo runs a live SEO audit from one homepage URL, crawling the site against 52 Google Search Central rules, measuring Core Web Vitals, asking the Jev model typed questions about each page, and outputting ranked fixes as PDF, XLSX, and Markdown reports.

name: grok-bot-jev
description: A Python router that classifies Grok Bot requests via TypeSafe Jev's `system_one` call, returning explicit actions (reuse_cache, stop_retry, research_capped, ask_human) so shadow or active modes can skip needless browser, retry, research, or subagent work.

name: open-jev
description: open-jev is a browser-first TypeScript library that runs quantized Jev-style "System One" models on-device via Transformers.js (WebGPU or WASM), turning a text state plus typed choice/score/yes-no questions into calibrated probability distributions in a single non-generative forward pass.

name: finance-agent
description: finance-agent is a LangGraph multi-agent system that turns a stock ticker plus a natural-language query into an investment research report, using TypeSafe's Jev model to route only to relevant specialized agents (news, financial statements, analyst outlook, sector) that pull data from yfinance and Tavily in parallel before a single Gemini 2.5 Flash call synthesizes the findings—keeping research

name: edgejev
description: EdgeJev is a CLI/Python tool that converts open-source Jev "System One" decision-model checkpoints (laya, kev, nanojev, playjev) into quantized ONNX bundles for fully offline CPU inference — 15.6 ms per question on 4 cores, no torch or network at runtime — and can serve them via an official-protocol-compatible `/v1/systemone` endpoint.

name: dsh-crypto-workbench
description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin providing an AI-assisted OKX USDT-perpetual trading workbench with code-enforced risk gates, an opportunity radar, human-confirmed plan execution, Jev decision monitoring, Jin10 data feeds, and a sidebar dashboard.

name: jev-signal-scorer
description: A Python trading-signal scorer that pairs Jev's typed AI judgments (bullishness, clarity, freshness, setup type) with a deterministic rule engine that pre-computes market features and enforces hard vetoes on spread, staleness, and thresholds—producing calibrated buy/sell/skip signals plus a (state, decision, outcome) dataset for tuning confidence honesty.

name: fedjev-bench
description: A pre-registered evaluation harness that ranks FOMC chair press-conference openings for inflation hawkishness via TypeSafe/Jev pairwise comparisons, validating them against same-day funds-rate changes, published FedLock scores (Gate 7 Spearman rank agreement), a TrueSkill replica, and a seven-criterion multi-axis extension, with cached results, reproducible analysis scripts, and a live re-scoring

name: laya
description: Laya is a non-autoregressive decision engine that answers typed questions (choice, score, noul) over text or JSON states in a single ~33 ms forward pass, trained with RL on strictly proper scoring rules for calibrated confidence, with a router that dispatches to one of three checkpoints across 100+ languages.

name: xo-jev
description: A Bun-based browser tic-tac-toe game where you play X against "Jev," an AI opponent that picks O moves via TypeSafe Choice (`systemOne`) through a `POST /api/move` endpoint returning move source, confidence, and probabilities, with random-cell fallback on model failure.

name: LetJevDecide
description: LetJevDecide answers yes-or-no dilemmas by querying TypeSafe's probabilistic model for a verdict and importance rating, or flipping a cryptographically fair in-browser coin, applying a study finding that randomization counters excessive caution in life choices.

name: open-jev-typed-decision-engine
description: An open 150M ModernBERT encoder that answers arbitrary per-request typed questions (boolean, choice, score) about a state in one forward pass with calibrated confidences, trainable free on a Colab T4, scoring 0.697 accuracy vs TypeSafe Jev's 0.727 at ~60ms locally.

name: jgrep
description: jgrep is a Rust CLI that answers plain-English questions over piped logs, files, or directories—evaluating deduplicated context windows via the Jev SystemOne API to return yes/no probabilities, choices, or weighted scores with line-level source citations.

name: jev-review
description: A TypeSafe Jev–based code-review tool that orchestrates staged model judgments (file profiling, evidence selection, mechanism classification, severity scoring, conditional reviewer routing) over a Git diff or full codebase to flag correctness, security, reliability, compatibility, and test-coverage risks, presenting results in a localhost-only dashboard.

name: codex-typesafe-threads
description: Codex Threads is a macOS menu-bar and CLI tool that uses TypeSafe to search the 20 most recent local Codex threads within a 3,000-token input budget and open or save the closest match, making prior work easier to retrieve.

name: jev-gmail-ai-spam-filter-and-labeling
description: jevMail is a self-hosted Google Apps Script tool that uses the Jev AI model to label Gmail messages by meaning against custom natural-language criteria, with confidence-based second-pass review, optional auto-archiving, spend limits, and preview mode—no external backend required.

name: trenchscore
description: Unofficial Chrome/Edge extension that displays 1–5-star Jev AI scores beside GMGN trench coins using your own API key, scoring only public on-card fields, skipping tokens failing hard risk filters, with caching and adjustable concurrency—never trading or reading wallet keys.

name: codex-jev-router
description: A local MCP server for Codex that searches a workspace via `search_workspace_evidence` and `read_selected_evidence`, returning deterministic, cited code/log excerpts instead of large raw output—cutting measured API costs up to ~41% on noisy-log investigations, with optional Laya reordering and workspace-bounded, sensitive-path-excluding file access.

name: demo-mcp
description: DEMO MCP is a Cloudflare Workers-hosted MCP server giving clients a persistent real browser (open, click, type, scroll, screenshot, media/video inspection, CAPTCHA human handoff) plus optional Roblox OAuth account access, with SSRF guards and structured capability errors.

name: jev-vtuber-ime-core
description: jev-vtuber-ime-core is a TypeScript resolver/CLI that turns a Japanese reading into a canonical VTuber name by searching the web for evidence, extracting name candidates, and using Jev’s probability-only judgments to select a threshold-passing match—without bundling a dictionary or returning non-VTubers.

name: kev
description: kev is a local decision-model server — a LoRA adapter plus pointer readout head on a Qwen base (0.5B–8B) — that answers many typed questions (yes/no, multi-choice, ordinal score) about a document in one decode-free prefill pass, returning calibrated softmax probabilities through a TypeSafe System One–compatible API.

name: jeff-cli
description: jeff-cli is a Go/cobra command-line tool (and dependency-free Go client) that queries TypeSafe's Jev model to return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, multi-choice, and ordered-scale questions, plus weighted multi-dimensional item ranking, with JSON output, exit-code gates, and pipe-friendly input for shell scripts, CI jobs, and agents.

name: jot
description: Jot is a Node.js/TypeScript agent that runs the tool-calling loop for the Jev model — Jev picks tools and arguments while Jot executes calls, feeds results back into context, and iterates until a reply — shipping a chat UI with visible tool-call traces, a provider-independent core, and a loopback server that keeps credentials server-side and chats in the browser.

name: jev-traps
description: jev-traps is an Apache-2.0 TypeScript toolkit that inspects untrusted text, HTML, browser content, and images for injection risks, enforcing host-side allow/sanitize/review/block decisions through deterministic policy, optional semantic checks, and destination preflight.

name: JEV-EFMW-Syncretic-Layer
description: Reproducible synthetic testbed simulating a Jev-like typed decision layer with an EFMW-style recursive coherence monitor, providing three controlled experiments—calibration degradation, closed-loop trajectory instability, and an equal-information anti-circularity comparison—run via pip, Python scripts, and pytest under frozen null-calibrated thresholds.

name: omnia-laya
description: A local decision layer that runs pinned-checkpoint inference on typed question sets, validates answers against configurable probability policies, and stores durable, replayable decision records with full evidence lineage, review reasons, and calibration metrics in a SQLite ledger.

name: jev-codex-plugin
description: An open-source Codex plugin that provides TypeSafe Jev decision consultation, failure diagnosis, and completion-evidence review through MCP tools, lifecycle hooks, and standalone CLI skills, returning recommendations or abstentions without acting automatically.

name: cyprid
description: cyprid installs and runs local decision models on Apple Silicon Macs behind a single Jev-compatible API and web UI, so you can ask fixed-answer questions (yes/no, pick-one, rating) about text and compare or swap models without changing your code.

name: jev-physical-ai
description: A reproducible benchmark repo applying TypeSafe's Jev "System One" model to physical-AI workloads — 300 real API triage decisions for a 10,000-robot fleet ($24.57/M decisions, 0.53s p50) plus a Jev-vs-self-hosted-ModernBERT cost crossover (~977K decisions/month) — with runnable scripts, measured data, and stated limitations.

name: questions
description: A TypeScript library for typed semantic decisions: validate LLM answers against Zod 4 schemas or native question batches, get inferred types back via async/await or Web Streams, and swap between TypeSafe AI, Vercel AI Gateway, or generative Gemini/Claude/GPT models with retries, deadlines, and observability.

name: hellow-jev
description: hellow-jev is a Python benchmark suite that evaluates four classification models—Jev (TypeSafe AI API), Laya (local open weight), Claude Haiku 4.5, and Qwen3 4B—zero-shot on log classification and jevbench tasks (SST-2, AG News, Banking77), measuring accuracy, Macro-F1, latency percentiles, API cost, and output stability via config-driven runners and a Markdown report generator.

name: jev-arena
description: jev-arena is a real-time bot-fighting arena where plain-English YAML strategies are piloted live by LLM brains (Jev, System One endpoints, or chat models), featuring deterministic replays, a PR-based Elo ladder, and offline mock mode.

name: jet-revenue-forecaset
description: A bottom-up revenue forecast tool for 1,000 in-place clients that calls Jev inline at each contract roll date to decide renewals, bucketed ACV changes, and termination reasons, exposing results as lazy Orcaset Series that roll up into per-contract, cohort, and churn-by-cause revenue tables.

name: grok-jev-reflex
description: A CLI router that gates each step of a Grok-powered agent through a cheap ~239ms Jev model—deciding whether to proceed, cap research, reuse cache, skip, ask a human, or prune the per-call tool list—cutting token spend while never approving irreversible actions.

name: Jev-router
description: An in-process Rust request router that classifies prompts through a five-tier deterministic fallback cascade—regex rules, FastText, quantized ONNX transformers, a heavy model, then a frontier LLM—to choose discriminative or generative execution within a sub-5ms p99 SLA.

name: POK-Agent
description: POK-Agent is a Windows 10/11 computer-use agent that pairs a large LLM planner with a small fast action model, grounding screens via UI Automation and OCR, replaying verified task runs as "muscle memory" motor programs, and enforcing Rust-level safety policies for autonomous desktop control and coding.

name: HA-Jev
description: A Home Assistant integration that turns typed questions for the TypeSafe Jev decision model into sensors and automation actions returning probabilities, choices, or scores, plus an Assist conversation agent, with daily token budgets and cost tracking.

name: radixing-traffic-engine
description: TypeScript decision engine evaluating versioned ordered rules over host-supplied request signals (probes, User-Agent, geography) to select explicit block/allow/redirect/route actions, plus an optional bounded Jev model step and deterministic rule-proposal replay/review.

name: IntentSQL
description: IntentSQL is a local playground that turns plain-English requests into SQLite queries and confirmed inserts/updates/deletes via bounded Jev decisions—exposing each typed plan, generated SQL, result, and preview so you can inspect exactly how every answer was built.

name: jev-as-judge
description: An auditable tutorial project that evaluates refund-support traces via the Jev LLM-as-judge API—scoring groundedness, action honesty, and helpfulness—and logs verdicts to Opik experiments, with deterministic pre-checks, an offline demo mode, and JSONL audit output.

name: agent-router
description: A local-first, quota-aware CLI that filters your AI coding-agent subscriptions with deterministic eligibility rules, has TypeSafe rank eligible models and pick reasoning effort, then launches the chosen agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode) in a Herdr pane.

name: jev_escalation
description: A HumanEval/HumanEval+ benchmark toolkit demonstrating that verifying a Qwen3-4B answer with Jev and conditionally escalating to a cold Qwen3-32B restart (plus first-line stub retry) reaches 84.1% pass@1 at 3.49× cost, beating always-4B, always-32B, and prompt-only routing, with cached data, bootstrap stats, charts, and an interactive demo.

name: ai-backends
description: AIBackends is a self-hostable API server that exposes ready-to-use AI endpoints for text, vision, and data tasks plus autonomous tool-using agents with multi-turn sessions and SSE streaming, backed by local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, LlamaCpp) or cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Google, Baseten, ZAI, LLM Gateway), with an admin dashboard for custom agents, HTTP tools, MCP servers,

name: zev-rs
description: zev-rs is a zero-token Rust LLM decision engine (library, CLI, and REST server) that scores structured choices in ~5.8 µs with calibrated confidence, abstention guardrails, and order-invariant SIMD scoring, cascading to on-device Apple Intelligence or Candle neural backends for ambiguous inputs.

name: open-spark-jev
description: Open Spark Jev is an open-source local decision model (spark-s1, Qwen3+LoRA) for NVIDIA DGX Spark that answers typed Choice/Score/Noul questions about a state with probabilities and confidence in ~30–66 ms, serving use cases like tool-call gating and routing.

name: tenet
description: tenet is a CLI review gate that lints agent-written diffs against plain-language rules in .tenet/config.yml, drafted from AGENTS.md-style instruction files or built-in presets, enforcing a calibrated pass/fail cutoff via git hooks so agents fix violations before review.

name: jev-design-test
description: Turns a one-line prompt into a batch of distinct, live full-page UI screens on an infinite canvas by sampling Jev's probability distributions over a fixed vocabulary of real shadcn/Base UI layout blocks — fast (~1-2s) with no generated JSX.

name: Jevbridge
description: Jevbridge is a zero-dependency Node 22 library and MCP/ACP stdio adapter that pairs any LLM with TypeSafe Jev's typed System One decisions (noul, choice, score), confidence-gating tool calls and closed-set computer-use actions so software can branch on probabilistic answers.

name: typesafe-sdk-dotnet
description: An unofficial .NET client for the TypeSafe AI API that ports the JavaScript SDK's SystemOne question primitives (Choice, Score, Noul), retry/timeout configuration, DI integration, and exception hierarchy, targeting net10.0 and netstandard2.0.

name: jev-profanity
description: A Czech-first benchmark lab that detects and star-censors unsafe review text—vulgar, rude, or coded attacks—comparing Jev (TypeSafe System One) against lexicon and token_scorer baselines, with v3.0.0 coverage of algospeak, short codes, semantic weapons, and coded hate, runnable via Node scripts with a TypeSafe API key.

name: everett
description: A branching-container harness that forks agent worlds at each architectural split, runs every choice to completion in copy-on-write snapshots, scores leaves with a frozen Arbiter, and collapses sibling rankings into calibrated counterfactual target distributions for RLCD finetuning.

name: jev-retrieval-eval
description: An evaluation harness measuring Jev as a second-stage passage filter after BM25 retrieval and as a GPT-agent retrieval tool, reporting evidence recall, latency, token usage, and per-provider API cost across controlled ranking and agent-workflow experiments on an 8-question technical corpus.

name: zcode-router
description: This kit renders one roster into ZCode's router, provider picker, workflow library, and keepalive service — tiered routing with fallbacks, pay-per-token safeguards, router-chosen delegation (call, mixture-of-agents, or swarm), quota-aware failover, and usage dashboard.

name: FeedGate
description: A Chrome extension that reduces noise across six social feeds via an explicit, reversible rule set—AI-based semantic filtering, time-limited topic mutes, author allow/mute lists, optional duplicate grouping, cosmetic filters, and honest API-usage controls—while keeping merely promotional posts visible and requiring no external server.

name: OpenRyoko
description: OpenRyoko is a Slack-first, Japanese-first resident AI gateway that gives you an AI colleague which reads the room via Haiku triage (silent/react/reply), autonomously finishes tasks using natural-language /goal stop hooks, and live-syncs all session states to a Slack Canvas.

name: ego-jev
description: ego-jev automates multi-step ego lite browser tasks by having TypeSafe's Jev model return the next operation and target element in one request, while code owns observation, execution, fail-closed guards, and exit conditions—about 2x faster than per-step LLM loops.

name: jev-ercot
description: jev-ercot ranks every Texas retail electricity plan in your utility area by projected 12-month cost from a ZIP and one past bill, then shows each plan's EFL price components, cost-model verification, and contract-term details, plus live analysis of pasted EFL text.

name: jev-integration-evaluator
description: A read-only, offline-by-default Python CLI/agent skill that scans repositories, scores bounded decision-point opportunities, generates reviewable integration and experiment plans plus disabled adapters, and gates adoption on explicit approval and measured evidence.

name: vllm-jev
description: vLLM-Jev serves Jev-style decision checkpoints through native vLLM, exposing an HTTP API that returns labels and probabilities for candidate answers—Choice, yes/no, and ordered-score decisions over text and images—with batching, KV cache, and multi-fold latency and throughput gains.

name: laterhook
description: Laterhook is a self-hosted webhook inbox that captures every request sent to zero-setup endpoints, then lets you inspect, search, replay, tag, secure, and permanently forward matching traffic through regex routes before your real backend is ready.

name: typesafe-profiler
description: A CLI that scores each message in a single-person chat log against 35 fixed psychological dimensions using TypeSafe's typed decision model, then aggregates, schema-validates, and emits a Markdown report plus JSON record for humans and code.

name: spring-ai-typesafe
description: Spring AI TypeSafe is a Java 17+ client and Spring AI integration for TypeSafe AI’s System One API that turns a state plus typed questions into parallel structured answers for LLM judges, guardrails, RAG filtering/reranking, and tool selection without brittle generated JSON.

name: jevdexer
description: Jevdexer is a free, local-first Windows search tool (Win+Alt+Space) that finds apps, games, folders, and files by name, optionally understands natural-language descriptions through your own Vercel AI Gateway key, and can index document text, OCR, and photo contents inside chosen folders entirely on-device.

name: Jev-Radar
description: Jev-Radar is a local, CPU-based research workspace that turns a prompt into an auditable web investigation, combining hosted Jev decisions, Brave Search, page collection, and optional text models to produce evidence-linked comparisons, uncertainty tracking, replays, spend controls, and exports.

name: jdl-results-downloader
description: A Python CLI that scans the JAPAN DRONE LEAGUE site, uses the TypeSafe Jev API to select completed rounds and classify their linked Google Drive PDFs (qualifiers, finals, pairings, course info), then downloads, verifies, and organizes them with HTML/CSV/JSON indexes and caching for fast reruns.

name: Jev
description: Jev is a PowerShell module that turns unstructured input into structured, actionable decisions by invoking TypeSafe AI’s Jev model with typed yes/no, choice, and score questions, returning named answers as top-level properties while preserving the full API response and supporting pipeline input.

name: medula
description: Médula is a reproducible Python lab and coordination kernel that intercepts concurrent coding agents' writes, uses a fast probabilistic decider (escalating to stronger models when uncertain) to detect semantic conflicts git misses, and benchmarks six collision-prone tasks across six coordination modes with fully published evidence.

name: a3m-router
description: A self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible proxy that routes each prompt to the cheapest capable provider among 80+ LLMs—with semantic caching, provider fallbacks, and ensemble calls—cutting API costs by up to ~90% without changing existing client code.

name: laya-server
description: LAYA SERVER is a self-hosted Docker service exposing Laya's System One structured decision-model inference through a TypeSafe Jev–compatible REST API and web console, with API key auth, a playground, readiness checks, and a bundled multilingual model.

name: ts-browser-agent
description: A Playwright-based browser agent that runs LangChain's `create_agent` loop with TypeSafe's classifier returning per-step probabilities over browser operations and element targets—exposing a `browse_fast` tool for deep agents and a compiled `build_browser_agent()` graph, without any third-party browser-agent package.

name: jev-for-finance
description: A RAG pipeline for financial research that answers analyst questions from SEC 10-K/10-Q filings by using Jev to pick the two best passages from a hybrid BM25+e5 top-30 for a single LLM call—achieving 50/50 accuracy with ~100x fewer tokens than agentic RAG—plus reproducible benchmark scripts and logs.

name: jev-buildathon
description: A buildathon toolkit for making four deliberately unsafe AI agents behave: run their practice and sealed tasks, diagnose failures with Jev evaluations on FailproofAI Cloud, and enforce real-time syntactic and semantic policies that block or redirect harmful tool calls.

name: jev-second-brain
description: jev-second-brain is an MIT-licensed, local-first CLI that indexes a Markdown or Obsidian vault into SQLite/FTS, searches it, shortlists notes related to a new note, and optionally asks Jev to judge pairs or rerank results—always citing source paths, caching by content revision, gating private text behind a zero-data-retention canary, and leaving all edits to human review.

name: laravel-jev-ai
description: A typed PHP SDK and Laravel adapter for Jev decision requests, offering an injectable client contract, facade, fluent typed questions (boolean/string/number/enum), configurable retries, safe exceptions, and a network-free fake for testing.

name: jevbrief
description: jevbrief is a Python CLI and library that condenses web pages, JSON, OpenTelemetry logs, or NES memory into compact, reason-coded facts for TypeSafe's Jev decision engine, cutting input tokens and logging replayable per-decision traces viewable in one offline HTML file.

name: jev-browser-use
description: A Codex browser Skill that offloads clicks, navigation, toggles, and scrolling to TypeSafe's low-cost Jev model over the existing Computer Use connection—delivering ~5–10× faster browser operations—while Codex retains text input, visual judgment, and final verification.

name: jev-rag-pipeline
description: A real RAG system for testing rag-guard as an external pip-installed dependency: a streaming web app for uploading documents and inspecting per-stage relevance, sufficiency, and grounding traces, plus a terminal REPL and golden-set evaluation scripts.

name: jev-childspeak
description: A terminal Python chat that turns TypeSafe Jev — a typed decision model rather than a chat LLM — into a constrained speaker by asking it to pick one token per API call from a fixed ~255-token vocabulary until emitting END, with transcript save/load and tunable limits.

name: salomon
description: Salomón is a Node CLI experiment that normalizes EPUB/text books, has an LLM write sectionwise reading notes, samples passages for Jev’s probabilistic questions, then turns answers into reproducible valuations benchmarked against external literary standing.

name: jev-robotics-demo
description: A MuJoCo simulation demo where a Franka arm with an Allegro hand stacks cubes, comparing an LLM agent that reasons step-by-step via low-level tools against Jev, a fast typed-probability model that picks pre-simulated moves — achieving the same result ~8x faster at ~1/1000th the cost.

name: schemasift
description: SchemaSift is a provider-neutral Python library and service that turns a natural-language question and a large database schema into a compact, high-recall working schema via batched two-stage table/column selection, with key/relationship preservation, budgets, and tracing.

name: pg_typesafe
description: PostgreSQL extension exposing TypeSafe AI's Noul, Choice, and Score primitives as SQL functions for yes/no probabilities, category assignment, and rubric scoring, with batched requests, retries, cancellable queries, and offline mocking.

name: typesafe-guardrails
description: A runnable demo that rebuilds the Chevrolet dealership chatbot so you can reproduce the famous $1 Tahoe jailbreak, then watch TypeSafe's Jev guardrail block it at inbound, tool-argument, and draft-reply boundaries—with OpenAI Agents SDK, Arize tracing, and a Jev-vs-LLM-as-judge latency/cost comparison.

name: n8n-nodes-jev-classification
description: An n8n community node that classifies, scores, and checks workflow items with TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model, returning typed answers with calibrated probabilities and routing items to category, yes/no, or Needs Review outputs via batched parallel requests for high-volume workflows.

name: jev-context
description: A Pi extension that replaces attention-based context management with a cheap scored judge: it routes only relevant skills, surfaces only needed tool namespaces, and prunes unhelpful tool outputs, cutting billed context ~33–37% without breaking prefix caching.

name: jev_project_context
description: An agent skill that maintains evidence-first research memory for AI coding agents, providing ten operations (init, start, frame, plan, record, end, correct, synthesize, claim-audit, doctor) with provenance gates, controlled validity vocabulary, and read-only audits so every claim stays traceable and sessions resumable.

name: dsh-jev-plugin
description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds a separately configured TypeSafe Jev decision layer for skill/file ranking, supervision, corrections, log filtering, single-operation approvals, and stage review—12 individually gated, default-off features integrated through public extension points.

name: doc-router

description: BrowserClaw is a Chrome MV3 extension plus local MCP server that lets AI agents operate your everyday Chrome—preserving logins, cookies, and extensions—through 50 tools spanning pruned indexed DOM reading, trusted-input batch pipelines, and a local perceive-decide-act micro-loop for autonomous goals.

name: jevspeak
description: JevSpeak is a chat system where a decision model (Jev) answers ~13 parallel questions about each user message to produce a typed semantic IR that a deterministic compiler renders into English (or other locale packs) with confidence-calibrated hedging—demonstrating natural conversation without any generative LLM in the runtime pipeline.

name: JevPlaysPokemon
description: A demo harness that lets the Jev model play real Pokémon FireRed fights on mGBA (reading battle state from RAM) and Pokémon Showdown matches by feeding it per-turn JSON snapshots of HP, stats, and legal moves/switches, executing its typed choices, and exposing a live dashboard with replays.

name: typesafe-sdk-go
description: An unofficial Go SDK for the TypeSafe AI API that provides a configurable client, typed SystemOne questions and choice/score/noul answers, model listing, structured API errors, and runnable live-API examples.

name: Jevsus
description: An open dataset and stdlib-Python runner that asks TypeSafe's Jev model forced true/false picks on 3,608 templated statements across rewordings, accusation batteries, stances, and languages, storing every raw response with mechanical publishability gating for reproducible, traceable results.

name: jev-news
description: jev-news is a daily pipeline that collects RSS articles from Malaysian outlets, uses JEV and DeepSeek LLMs to extract core facts and strip emotive or political packaging language, and presents neutral tabulated summaries so readers can judge events for themselves.

name: changelog-bot
description: changelog-bot is a CLI/GitHub Action that generates polished changelog entries—and optionally opens a PR with compare links and release notes—from commit history, PR titles, and release notes, using OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini for tone-aware summaries or a deterministic heuristic fallback, with optional "WHY" rationale extraction, multi-language output, and dry-run diagnostics.

name: jev_vs_oss
description: Benchmark material comparing TypeSafe AI's jev decision model against open alternatives — a Modal-hosted Qwen3.5-4B decoder, local encoders (Laya, jeff), and specialised tools (lingua, tesseract OSD) — across five generated, labelled document-pipeline tasks (language/orientation detection, classification, bundle splitting, parse-tier triage), with liteparse-based CLIs for PDF rendering and OCR

name: obekt-terminal
description: An open-source autonomous crypto trader that scans ~270 EUR pairs every 5 minutes, filters them via deterministic gates, consults a typed decision model, and enforces risk in code with OCO and trailing stops, plus a read-only Bloomberg-style terminal streaming every decision.

name: jev-map
description: jev-map is a Python CLI and MCP server that statically maps each function in a repository to the tests that call it, optionally adding model-inferred links from TypeSafe's Jev that are labeled by provenance, threshold-scored, and backed by replayable request receipts, helping coding agents prioritize which tests to run.

name: jev-nethack
description: Public source, live gameplay viewer, archived recordings, and research artifacts for Jev, an AI agent persistently playing NetHack — including the runner, crash-recovery background service, BC/PPO training pilots, sanitized transition datasets, and rigorously documented negative-result experiments.

name: Dutygate
description: Dutygate is a chatbot-agnostic screening gate that scans inbound support messages for legal triggers (opt-outs, privacy requests, legal threats) using TypeSafe Jev plus versioned YAML policy packs, returning continue/route/review decisions—never acting itself—with fail-safe error handling, a Python library, CLI, HTTP sidecar, TypeScript client, and evaluation harness.

name: jev-trade
description: A Bun trading bot that reads the Hyperliquid book every tick, lets the Jev model call long/short and open/close/hold across five isolated coin wallets, sends post-only maker entries and Ioc exits, and streams fills and positions to a live Next dashboard, with dry-run and testnet modes.

name: code-compact-jev
description: An npm library, CLI, and Claude Code plugin that uses a calibrated classifier to score comments in JS/TS/Rust/Go/Python as drop, shorten, extend, or keep, then applies LLM rewrites only to survivors while guaranteeing code is never modified.

name: ask-jev-ai
description: An open-source Convex app where visitors submit short questions that TypeSafe's Jev judgment model scores into typed yes/no/it-depends verdicts in ~100ms, while signed-in users get model-routed answers, threads, and history on a realtime public wall.

name: jev-runway
description: A local proxy between Codex and your model provider that uses the Jev decision model to trim stale tool output from each resent conversation history—cutting input tokens 66–76%—while archiving trimmed output locally for re-reads and passing requests through untouched if Jev is unavailable.

name: llama-index-jev
description: Drop-in LlamaIndex reranker (`JevRerank`) and router selectors (`JevSingleSelector`, `JevMultiSelector`) powered by TypeSafe Jev's typed Score/Choice decision API — ~$0.0003/query, fail-open rerank/fail-closed select, and measured BEIR nDCG gains over MiniLM.

name: ai-cli
description: A terminal tool for generating text, images, video, and audio and evaluating typed Boolean/Choice/Score questions via composable commands, stdin piping, file/URL inputs, batching, and JSON output on the Vercel AI SDK and AI Gateway's hundreds of models.

name: Failproof-Buildathon
description: A Codex CLI hook-based tool where a separate reviewer agent turns completed worker message pairs into reusable advisory policies that Jev applies as one combined check on later turns, catching repeated mistakes without changing model weights.

name: five-lines
description: five-lines is a cross-platform CLI that reviews pull-request diffs against the ten *Five Lines of Code* refactoring rules, combining deterministic tree-sitter checks in ten languages with optional probabilistic Jev judgments, suppression controls, JSON output, thresholds, and CI failure gates.

name: daf-jev
description: daf-jev is a modular Python client and decision toolkit for the TypeSafe Jev (System One) API that batches typed noul/choice/score questions into one call and layers on pure-logic composition gates, concurrent corpus evaluation, calibration metrics, a circuit breaker, a decider loop, Bayes-net elicitation, a CLI, and an MCP server.

name: jevmem
description: jevmem is an npm CLI that gives Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex persistent project memory—automatically capturing decisions, constraints, bugs, and todos from chats into a `JEVMEM.md` file with superseding history, then injecting relevant lines into future sessions, using secret scrubbing, probability-thresholded save/skip decisions, and MCP hooks.

name: mario-never-dies
description: A demo that uses microsandbox VM snapshots to checkpoint a running Mario game every 150 frames and, on each death, branches the last checkpoint into four VM copies racing different recoveries so the survivor becomes the run, while the Jev API picks moves from parsed RAM state and a browser visualizes the branching timelines.

name: safer-with-jev
description: Safer with Jev is a live demo site and API exposing TypeSafe Jev endpoints that inspect request bodies for prompt injections or unsafe replies and optionally forward the same bytes to a caller-chosen HTTPS target only when the judgment passes.

name: watfile
description: watfile is a Python CLI that sorts files (incl. PDFs) into category folders via symlink, copy, or move by sending each document's text extract to a typed decision model—batched TypeSafe Jev API calls or a local offline Laya backend—with confidence gating and a dry-run mode.

name: MinusPodJev
description: MinusPodJev is a FastAPI proxy exposing TypeSafe Jev to MinusPod as an OpenAI-compatible ad-detection model, scoring transcript segments into classified, sponsor-matched spans with runtime thresholds and a status UI, plus an offline benchmark comparing Jev to 84 chat models.

name: jev-mcp
description: MCP server exposing ten fast, low-cost judgment tools (verify, screen, find, rerank, classify, decide, compare, extract, review, gate) that return typed probabilities and confidence scores so agents can fact-check claims, detect prompt injection, rank candidates, and validate diffs without a frontier model.

name: jev-code
description: jev-code is a TypeScript SDK and CLI that lets the decision-only Jev model pick among finite alternatives to build validated AST programs in many languages, run coding sessions, and power a `decide` command whose exit codes let scripts branch on labels, probabilities, or scores.

name: jev-finance-heist
description: A FailproofAI buildathon submission whose nine Jev-backed policies let the Ledger finance agent process invoices while blocking approval circumvention—like splitting a ₹1,450,000 payment below its ₹500,000 authority—verified across 26/26 replayable runs.

name: jev-prune-kit
description: jev-prune-kit provides a capability-aware context-pruning installer, a bounded Jev assessment engine, and experimental request-projection adapters for harness integration, enabling controlled context reduction and evaluation workflows that remain experimental and untested on live hosts.

name: jev-reranker
description: jev-reranker is a Node.js CLI that pipes JSON search candidates through TypeSafe's Jev API to rerank them by query relevance, filter out results lacking usable evidence, or compress them into query-specific passages, so downstream LLMs receive only the context worth reading.

name: twitter-timeline-analyzer
description: A Chrome extension that filters your Twitter/X timeline by natural-language topics—an LLM generates regex patterns and decision rules, TypeSafe's Jev or any OpenAI-compatible API scores each tweet in real time, and matches get tagged, highlighted, or hidden with feedback-driven refinement.

name: jevons
description: Jevons is a local, embeddable System One server exposing `POST /v1/systemone` per the TypeSafe HTTP contract, scoring allowed outcomes from LFM2.5 logits and assembling the response JSON in code, with failover routing to an optional Laya encoder or official TypeSafe cloud.

name: resurface
description: Resurface is a Next.js resume-screening tool that turns an existing candidate database into evidence-backed shortlists: an LLM drafts 6–8 atomic questions per job once, then a TypeSafe JEV model answers them per resume with calibrated probabilities and verbatim quote citations, achieving ~99% agreement with LLM verdicts at a fraction of the cost.

name: jev-terminal-browser-driver
description: A CLI driver that runs an autonomous observe→choose→act loop on terminal-browser (terminal-rendered Chromium), using Jev typed-decision calls via OpenRouter instead of screenshots or DOM dumps—~$0.0001/decision, ~200-byte JSON ticks, code-enforced tab-lease safety.

name: SlowDialog
description: SlowDialog is a framework-free, retro Game Boy–styled web chat app for OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs that delivers AI responses slowly in timed chunks (with manual advance, pause, and mid-response interruption) to restore human-paced, reflective conversation, adding quick replies, intent tagging, mode tags, a "text call" mode, VOICEVOX speech synthesis, themes, and history export.

name: ailang-packages
description: A monorepo of tested, reusable AILANG packages extracted from production projects, providing modules for GCP auth, HTTP helpers, logging, config, Firestore, billing/Stripe, contract reasoning, and typed decisions, installable via registry, path, or git-subdir dependencies.

name: switchboard
description: Switchboard is an open-source local proxy that automatically selects the model and reasoning effort for Claude Code and Codex tasks using the Jev classifier and a customizable routing policy, pinning that pair for the whole conversation to preserve provider prompt caching.

name: react-ts-form
description: @ts-react/form is a ~3kb headless React library that auto-generates fully typesafe forms from zod schemas via a schema-to-component mapping, eliminating react-hook-form boilerplate while preserving per-field prop control and custom component rendering.

name: ask-jev
description: A zero-dependency Python CLI for bounded advisory judgments—choice, evidence checks, ordinal scoring, batches, verbatim passage extraction—via TypeSafe's System One model, returning confidence-gated answers, escalation signals, and evidence receipts inside a 280ms budget.

name: feedwall
description: Feedwall is a dependency-free Manifest V3 browser extension for Chrome-based browsers that filters feeds on X, YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, and Hacker News by sending each post to a fast yes/no-probability model (TypeSafe's Jev) under your own API key, letting you define custom plain-English topics with Keep/Hide/Dim/Highlight actions, per-site focus mode, a test-on-recent-posts preview, mistake fee

name: Jevest
description: Jevest is a GitHub Action for automated pull-request review that gates an LLM reviewer with fast calibrated Jev decisions—triaging hunks, filtering findings, enforcing budgets, and publishing comments, labels, and merge-gate checks with fail-closed defaults.

name: jev-tree
description: JevTree is a typed Python planner runtime that composes Jev's fast local action distributions into executable probability trees or merged graphs over finite multi-step tasks, tracking unresolved mass and selecting Pareto actions by downstream success rather than one-step greediness.

name: jev-permission-gate
description: A Claude Code mod that puts TypeSafe's Jev in front of the auto-mode permission classifier, answering seven yes/no questions per tool call to allow, deny, or defer — halving median permission wait where it decides with zero unsafe allows in testing.

name: jev-lint
description: jev-lint is a CLI tool that checks JavaScript/TypeScript files against project conventions written in plain English (inline or Markdown rules in `jev.config.json`), sending code to the Jev model via Vercel AI Gateway to report possible violations with configurable severity, cost/file/request limits, compact or JSON output, saved reports, and CI-friendly exit codes.

name: jevmail
description: Jevmail is an open-source, read-only Gmail triage app that sorts messages into five trays with 1–5 urgency scores using TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model via Vercel AI Gateway—about a minute and 3 cents per 1,000 emails—with all state in local SQLite.

name: jev
description: Jev (jevos-1b) is a free, locally-run yes/no decision server that loads a quantized GGUF model via llama.cpp and answers named yes/no questions about arbitrary text or JSON states in ~50–220 ms on CPU, returning P(yes) probabilities through a `/v1/systemone` HTTP API wire-compatible with TypeSafe Jev's SDK.

name: topiclens-for-youtube
description: TopicLens is a Chrome extension that continuously filters YouTube cards during infinite scroll and in-page navigation using Hide and Show-only topic lists, resolving matches locally or via the TypeSafe Jev API with reversible hiding, caching, and fail-open behavior.

name: jevtpp
description: A C++20 library that turns runtime text, JSON, or application objects into compile-time-typed routing, classification, and scoring decisions (enums, booleans, probabilities) via in-process ONNX/ggml inference, with abstention, batching, observability metrics, and runtime-loadable decision graphs.

name: pi-jev-wiki
description: pi-jev-wiki is an agent-managed wiki that maintains a project's conceptual space, using Jev to keep its accumulated knowledge legitimate, relevant, and robust as it scales.

name: meraline
description: Meraline is a tiny macOS utility that summons a floating AI window via ⌥Space for ephemeral streaming answers, supporting LLMs, CLI agents, and a decision model with selected-text/file/image context, prompt presets, answer rewrites, and word games while saving nothing to disk.

name: swift-jev
description: A dependency-free Swift 6.2 library and JSON-based CLI for TypeSafe AI's Jev model, evaluating typed Choice/Noul/Score questions in parallel against a state and returning type-safe answers with calibrated probabilities and confidence-based routing for apps, terminals, and coding agents.

name: relay_itsm
description: A FastAPI/SQLite IT service desk with React front end for a fictional food distributor, providing incident and service-request workflows where priority is derived from a live matrix, policy logic is pure and testable, and every decision logs its reason so a pluggable AI judgment layer can be measured rather than asserted.

name: open-typesafe-camoufox
description: A CLI that drives a headed Camoufox browser toward plain-English tasks at ~$0.0002/step via deterministic page reads, a confidence-gated Jev classifier over typesafe_sdk, a writer model only for free text, and a ranked CAPTCHA-solver chain with full audit trails.

name: typesafe-jev-traffic-demo
description: A local simulation that polls Hong Kong traffic sensors and asks TypeSafe’s Jev which conflicting phase gets green at a real junction, while deterministic timing enforces safety limits and a dashboard shows decisions with traffic injection and emergency preemption.

name: jeveryword
description: jeveryword is a dependency-free JavaScript library that uses TypeSafe's Jev to extract exact text spans, label words such as PII, and return offsets and probabilities for downstream confirmation or UI filtering.

name: ground-truth
description: A browser extension that automatically rates the political lean of the article in your current tab — painting an L/C/R/MIX toolbar badge and a side panel with bias shares, piece type, topic, and language loadedness — via a source-blind TypeSafe call proxied through a reading service, so no API key or host permissions ship in the build.

name: jev-dns-filter
description: A dependency-free Go sidecar that pairs with Knot Resolver to filter DNS: it scores each queried domain via TypeSafe's jev AI model, returns NODATA for domains exceeding per-category thresholds, forwards the rest upstream, and fails open on errors.

name: typesafe-ai-playground
description: `typesafe-ai` is a Rust CLI playground for TypeSafe's Jev model that scores text files for HIPAA-style PHI metrics, rates code comments on accuracy and usefulness, ranks per-line runtime importance into a JSONL heat map viewable in a local browser, and provides live interactive tone analysis.

name: jev-skill-router
description: A Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook that sends each prompt plus your full skill roster to TypeSafe's Jev probability model, logs which single skill it would pick, and optionally injects that name as a one-line hint—useful for auditing whether a nudge would change skill selection.

name: jev-browser
description: Headless browser agent (MCP, CLI, or library) in which TypeSafe's Jev model chooses one action per step from a page's interactive elements and scores goal/stuck probability, returning the final page, step trace, console errors, and screenshot at sub-cent cost.

name: chip
description: A minimal coding agent whose control loop runs on a decision model (Jev) that probabilistically picks the next tool and judges each step's result, while Claude only fills in tool arguments — providing a fast, judgment-driven alternative to prose-generating LLM loops.

name: jev-datafusion
description: A Rust crate that registers four SQL functions—`noul`, `choice`, `score`, and `ask`—on an Apache DataFusion `SessionContext`, letting LLM-style probabilistic judgments run across petabyte-scale rows against TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or compatible endpoints, with batching, retries, and per-row error handling.

name: compact-adviser
description: compact-adviser is a plugin for Pi, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Grok that scores each settled turn via TypeSafe's Jev model against a context-fill-adjusted threshold to hint—or, where supported and opted in, automatically run—/compact when the session reaches a safe boundary.

name: limpet
description: A Stop hook for Claude Code and Codex that scores each pending agent stop against plain-language rules with the jev model in ~0.7 s and sends the agent back to work when a rule is violated, with transcript tools that suggest rules and calibrate thresholds.

name: readybase-public
description: ReadyBase is a local-first CLI that maps repo dependencies, blast radius, ownership, and conventions to score AI-readiness, flag drift in AI-written code, guard risky edits, and certify the autonomy level (L0–L3) a codebase can safely support.

name: validator
description: Validator is a command-line tool that evaluates single-label and multi-label classifiers by comparing expected labels against generated predictions, surfacing missed labels, false alarms, and their underlying cases, and diffing report runs to reveal regressions or improvements hidden behind aggregate metrics like micro-F1.

name: Jev-StepPilot
description: A Windows-only Tauri desktop agent that autonomously carries out a typed goal by watching the active window and asking Jev for each next step—launching apps via Start-menu search, pausing on uncertain or hard-to-undo actions, and aborting when the mouse hits a screen corner.

name: jev-flight-combat
description: A 3D browser flight-combat game with manual keyboard controls, a deterministic local AI pilot, and live Jev model decisions via Vercel AI Gateway through a loopback Node server, featuring Three.js rendering, HUD/radar, telemetry export, and headless verification runs.

name: hermes-jev-approvals
description: A Hermes Agent plugin that routes smart command-approval decisions through TypeSafe's Jev model, replacing a chat LLM's one-token verdict with six parallel calibrated questions plus code-level policy rules for secret exfiltration, self-advocacy, blast radius, and operator allowlists—cutting approval latency ~10x while logging every decision.

name: jpp
description: J++ is an experimental programming language—implemented as a Rust-native CLI with a retained Python reference—that treats questions and methods as composable values, letting programs construct adaptive queries, accept and return methods, and execute semantic-judgment-driven algorithms offline.

name: jevymarket
description: A Polymarket trading bot that pairs TypeSafe's Jev calibrated-probability model with a web-searching researcher to price news-driven markets, placing Kelly-sized GTC limit orders where Jev's edge beats the order book, under hard exposure caps with SQLite logging.

name: jev-axi
description: jev-axi is a CLI for TypeSafe's Jev model, which answers typed questions with calibrated probabilities in ~400ms, giving agents a cheap second opinion: hooks that block risky commands, injection screening of fetched text, log triage, diff review, and file ranking.

name: armin
description: ARMIN is a per-project sidecar that passively captures agent sessions, distills durable decisions, rules, and open items into a queryable graph, and injects a compact reasoning-state brief each turn and after compaction so prior reasoning survives and prevents re-decision drift.

name: jev-telop-live
description: A macOS tool that turns live camera-and-microphone speech into automatic Japanese variety-show captions, sound-effect words, manga visual effects, and mood-driven sunglasses/voice changes, by sending transcripts to the Jev API with 30 typed questions and firing effects under code-controlled timing rules.

name: hermes-jev-router
description: An experimental opt-in Hermes plugin that previews and returns policy-constrained model routing plans—provider/model IDs plus an output cap—using TypeSafe Jev complexity assessment, explicit approval hashing, capability/cost/token/latency checks, and a configured fallback without dispatching requests.

name: jev-check
description: An open-source agent skill that drives an AI browser agent on your staging app as throw-away accounts in real plan states and confirms outcomes via SQL—exposing paywall, permission, and cross-tenant isolation bugs where the UI looks fine but the database disagrees.

name: jev-bois
description: Policy-layer defenses for the Jev Buildathon's unmodifiable Ledger finance agent: nine deterministic rails plus four Jev semantic checks that intercept every tool call to block or redirect fraud, with offline test suites, a 60-scenario harness, and a live trace viewer.

name: hip-jev
description: hipJev is a C++/HIP engine that answers typed questions—choice, yes/no (noul), and score—over unstructured text in one forward pass of Q6_K DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B on AMD gfx1201 GPUs, returning restricted-softmax probabilities through a Jev-compatible HTTP API at ~70ms latency.

name: jev-hanko
