description: Benchmark toolkit comparing TypeSafe AI's Jev model against fast, cheap LLMs on a 41-clause contract-page classification task over 500 CUAD pages, providing reproduction scripts, per-page latency/cost/recall/precision/F1 measurements, and replayable browser demos of the recorded runs.

name: filelathe
description: Filelathe is a web app that turns a dropped file or pasted URL into a floating window with the right tool—media player, editor, inspector, or an AI-invented mini-app for unknown formats—combining Jev's typed routing and composition with Haiku-generated UI Specs.

name: jev-extraction-marker-recovery
description: A Python script that recovers footnote and citation markers lost when OCR flattens superscripts, using a recall-heavy tokenizer to surface suspicious tokens and Jev (TypeSafe) to classify each as citation, footnote, section label, unit/exponent, or non-marker for reinsertion.

name: jev-magic-tower
description: A three-floor Magic Tower game for evaluating TypeSafe Jev's strategic judgment: Jev selects among enumerated legal moves without mutating deterministic game state, while the UI reports each decision's probabilities, confidence, model, and latency, plus an offline baseline.

name: la-ballot-match
description: A nonpartisan, open-source Next.js tool that quizzes Los Angeles County voters on issue positions, looks up their Nov 3, 2026 ballot contests by district, and scores weighted alignment against sourced candidate/measure ratings entirely in the browser.

name: fast-jev-opencode
description: An OpenCode v2 plugin that prunes stale tool calls and bulky results from outgoing model requests via TypeSafe's Jev through the `context` hook—leaving stored history untouched, failing open on errors, caching decisions across requests, and defaulting to observe-only dry-run mode.

name: jevals
description: jevals is a Python eval and guardrail library that checks agent traces — tool choice, groundedness, scope, relevancy, injection, PII — by packing all typed questions into one cheap, fast Jev-style decision-model request instead of an expensive nondeterministic LLM judge.

name: hermes-jev-skills
description: Eight agent-agnostic skills and a Hermes plugin that delegate per-turn decisions—model routing, memory filtering, compaction, skill selection, triage, GUI/browser actions—to TypeSafe's Jev decision model (~0.4 s, ~$0.00006), with redacted payloads and fail-open fallbacks.

name: speed-reading-app
description: SpeedRead is a macOS Tauri app that triages pasted AI coding-agent outputs using TypeSafe's Jev decision model via OpenRouter, highlighting sentences that need your decision or action, dimming informational text, and letting you delete it, jump between flagged items, and keep private local notes.

name: typesafe-sdk-rust
description: An async Rust client for the TypeSafe AI API that answers named questions (nouls, choices, scores) about a state via POST /v1/systemone and lists models, with derive-generated typed question sets, builder-configured requests, retries, and a structured error taxonomy.

name: jev-pokemon
description: jev-pokemon is a Node.js harness that lets the Jev decision model play Pokémon Red in a Game Boy emulator by reading RAM to list legal options with facts (type matchups, damage estimates, objectives) and pressing buttons, with no scripts, cheats, or memory writes.

name: jev-guard
description: jev-guard is a security hook that uses the Jev API to risk-score every tool call before execution, flag prompt injection in tool results, and audit skill/instruction files for covert behavior, working across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, Cursor, pi, OpenCode, and ACP.

name: goutoujunshi-jev-chat
description: A cross-platform (macOS/Windows/Android) chat copilot that screen-reads conversations like WeChat via local or cloud OCR, analyzes the other party's intent with Jev/DeepSeek strategy scoring, and generates ranked, tone-adjustable reply drafts—with transcript verification, relationship-trend K-line charts, and user-controlled sending.

name: Jev-Trades
description: Jev-Trades pairs a Next.js dashboard with a Python yfinance feed to stream one-minute crypto candles, compute indicators, request TypeSafe trading decisions, and apply them to a risk-limited simulated multi-asset portfolio for broker-free strategy testing.

name: pi-warden
description: pi-warden supervises Pi coding sessions by checking commands, edits, replies, and subagent reports for risky actions, rule violations, stuck loops, unverified “done” claims, secrets, runaway output, and noise, steering the agent to self-correct or holding irreversible steps.

name: zammad-jev-dispatcher
description: A Zammad integration that uses Jev (TypeSafe AI) to automatically triage incoming tickets, classifying each one and routing it to the appropriate service group so support teams can skip manual sorting and reach the right queue faster.

name: jev-bridge
description: A Rust tool (binary or library) that turns any OpenAI-compatible inference runtime (llama.cpp, vLLM, generic logprobs endpoints) into a Jev-style `direct-options-v1` decision scoring service, rendering fixed prompts via the runtime's chat template and softmaxing only over answer letters A–P to return typed choice/noul/score distributions without generating text.

name: jev-news-bench
description: Benchmark that injects five adversarial headline phrasings plus a benign control into a Polymarket news-classification task on Jev and Groq's gpt-oss-20b, measuring steering success and showing confidence gating admits attacks more readily than honest answers.

name: decision-query
description: decision-query adds SQL functions to SQLite and PostgreSQL that return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, multiple-choice, and rubric-scored questions over text columns, backed by a local laya.cpp checkpoint or an HTTP endpoint for in-database classification and filtering.

name: jev-vs-openai-dicision-api
description: A Bun-based benchmark comparing Japanese decision models (TypeSafe Jev, Cloudflare Clef, Clef-flash, plus a stub for OpenAI's unreleased Decisions API) on a fixed 260-case Japanese dataset, measuring accuracy, macro F1, Brier score, calibration (ECE), latency, token usage, and cost.

name: jev-curate
description: jev-curate is a Rust/Python CLI and library that streams Parquet/JSONL datasets through TypeSafe AI's Jev model to filter and score synthetic or pretraining rows at high throughput using typed decisions, calibrated probabilities, rubric presets, and adaptive rate limiting.

name: jevbrain
description: Jev Brain is a sub-millisecond local pre-execution firewall for AI agents and LLM apps that intercepts tool calls, shell commands, and commits to block destructive actions, secret leaks, and runaway loops via SDK wrappers, a GitHub Action, git hooks, CLI, and REST API.

name: firefox-jev-mcp
description: An MCP server that lets Claude drive Firefox, delegating per-click element selection to the fast non-generative Jev model so autonomous browsing loops (snapshots, clicks, typing, goal checks) complete with far fewer LLM round-trips, lower latency, token use, and cost.

name: jevchat
description: jevchat is a tool that turns Jev into a chatbot, providing a conversational interface layer so users can interact with Jev through chat-style prompts and responses rather than its default interface.

name: OpenDecision
description: OpenDecision is an open-source Python engine and FastAPI server that turns application state or documents into typed, code-ready decisions — Choice, Noul, Score, and Relation — via local ModernBERT zero-shot classification with evidence retrieval, offering a TypeSafe SDK-compatible endpoint for structured semantic answers.

name: lgtm
description: lgtm is a CLI that audits test files or diffs against their implementations with a bring-your-own-model reviewer to flag vacuous, mock-bound, or otherwise non-proving tests, estimate cost/runtime before running, and fit into terminal, CI, or agent workflows.

name: pr-sieve
description: pr-sieve is a GitHub Action that treats a base-ref `.jev.yml` of typed TypeSafe Jev questions as a semantic PR linter, failing, commenting, or passing check runs on scored answers plus code-level secret detection—never writing reviews or approving changes.

name: opencode-jev-router
description: An OpenCode plugin that routes each request through the Jev classifier to automatically pick per-step reasoning effort for wrapped GPT-6 or Claude models—injected via `configuration_update` or Anthropic effort messages—cutting token cost and latency without manual effort switching, with configurable fallback, retries, and metadata-only decision logging.

name: dsh-plugin-jev
description: A DSH Web GUI plugin exposing TypeSafe Jev calibrated judgment calls via a `jev_ask` tool, a `ctx.get('jev')` host service, and HTTP routes, plus a probabilistic command guard, per-chat usage chip, and settings tab for the API key and model.

name: jev-effort-router
description: A Claude Code plugin that sends each prompt to TypeSafe's Jev decision model to set per-turn reasoning effort (low/medium/high/xhigh), raising or lowering it with asymmetric confidence thresholds, forcing at least `high` for risky tasks, failing open on errors, and toggling via `/auto-effort`.

name: jevframe
description: jevframe adds a `.jev` accessor to pandas and Polars DataFrames for per-row AI text classification, sentiment analysis, and rubric scoring via natural-language questions, returning labels, confidences, and full probability distributions with bounded concurrency, caching, and null/error policies.

name: jevfire
description: JEVfire is a vLLM sidecar that scores verified single-token labels for finite-choice fields using a pretrained model's existing LM head—batching independent decisions over a shared cached prefix—to assemble typed JSON up to 10× faster than autoregressive constrained generation without retraining.

name: Jab
description: Jab is an unpackable browser extension that, on each Ctrl+Q press, uses a small in-browser int2-quantized model to focus the page control it predicts is wanted next, and ships a `train.py` script for retraining the model from JSONL data into ONNX.

name: jev-incall-assistance
description: Python reference implementation that re-scores a live call transcript against swappable question maps (MEDDPICC, BANT, sentiment) via Jev every two seconds, showing labels, probabilities, and coverage on a local dashboard with webhook, WebSocket, and Google Meet ingestion.

name: jev-demo
description: A demo repo showing Jev—a typed structured-decision model—powering a tool-call guard that sits between an AI agent's proposed action and execution, deciding allow/confirm/review/deny, with inbox-triage, support-agent, and Claude Code PreToolUse hook examples.

name: kite_population_simulator
description: Simulates million-agent behavioral populations on TypeSafe's Jev kernel by tabulating typed answer distributions per unique state, tilting treated rows with sparse paired flagship-LLM anchors, and propagating measured human–model discrepancy into calibrated uncertainty intervals.

name: jev-php
description: jev-php is a PHP 8.1+ Composer library that wraps the Jev API in typed value objects, letting you send text and receive structured answers—yes/no scores, labeled choices with probabilities, and rubric-based graded scores—each carrying input/output token usage metadata.

name: laya-jev-api
description: A FastAPI/uvicorn server for Apple Silicon that exposes the jev-compatible `POST /v1/systemone` endpoint—answering noul (yes/no), choice, and score questions against shared JSON state via local Laya Core ML inference—with optional bearer auth, health probes, request-ID tracing, and env/CLI configuration.

name: jev-grid-agent
description: A grid-world demo where Jev makes one batched decision per tick—action choice plus threat, goal-progress, stuck, and urgency judgments—to navigate an 8×8 map, illustrating a two-layer pattern that gives the model tactical judgment while code owns deterministic policy like anti-oscillation.

name: jev-riffs
description: jev-riffs tokenizes MIDI into transposition-invariant interval tokens, mines repeating units in code, grades each candidate's musical significance via batched Jev calls, and serves a web UI with piano-roll motif highlighting, passage playback, and WAV/JSON export.

name: discrimen
description: discrimen is a shell-based toolkit that lets a program ask a model for a judgment by offering named, actionable options, returning a typed JSON envelope the program validates against its list, state, and permission rules before acting, plus a decision log and calibration gate for checking whether those answers are worth trusting — all verifiable offline via a deterministic `--stub` mode.

name: jevsubrouter
description: JevSubRouter is a dependency-free Claude Code plugin whose hooks route each sub-agent dispatch to the cheapest sufficient model tier—without touching the orchestrator's cached prefix—with fail-open routing, worker background context, and /jev-why/jev-stats observability.

name: tab-jev
description: tab-jev pairs a jev-like backend that turns text into typed probabilistic judgments with a scikit-learn-style tabular foundation model, yielding calibrated predictions on mixed text-and-table data via in-context learning from few or zero labels, with pluggable local or hosted backends.

name: typesafe-go
description: Community-maintained, stdlib-only Go client for the TypeSafe AI API that returns typed structured answers (Noul probabilities, Choices, Scores) via `SystemOne`, with `errors.As`-compatible typed errors, configurable retries/backoff, context-aware concurrency safety, and per-call overrides for model, timeout, and headers.

name: jev-lm
description: jev-lm turns TypeSafe’s Jev option classifier into a character-level autoregressive language model that generates short answers over `a-z`, space, and a stop option, with calibrated probabilities, order averaging, greedy or beam decoding, CLI sessions, and a Python API.

name: jev-codex-token-saver
description: Jev Codex Token Saver is a Codex plugin whose local MCP server scans workspaces or large logs, sends bounded candidate excerpts to Jev for typed relevance scoring, and returns only selected excerpts—reducing tokens sent to Codex, with deterministic local fallback when its API key is unavailable.

name: ask-jev-skill
description: A Hermes skill that invokes TypeSafe Jev (`jev-latest`) as a typed decision tiebreaker, returning probabilistic Choice, Score, or Noul answers so agents can act confidently or escalate, with install, env-key, disable, and reliability-test scripts.

name: jev-acento
description: jev-acento is a reproducible audit quantifying how TypeSafe AI's Jev evaluation model loses accuracy, calibration, and automatable coverage on Spanish inputs, plus a CLI (`acento`) for running the same paired-language comparison on your own labelled data.

name: jev-trader
description: A Monad trading bot that queries a TypeSafe Jev model each ~300 ms block for a buy/sell call on Kuru's MON-USDC book and posts a post-only limit order one tick inside the touch—earning spread on taker fills—with dry-run mode, sub-block two-RPC-round-trip hot loop, and an SSE dashboard server streaming per-block quotes, fills, and P&L.

name: typesafeai-go
description: A Go client library for the TypeSafe AI API that sends typed questions—Noul (yes/no probability), Choice (options), and Score (ordered levels)—via a SystemOne client and returns answers in corresponding Go types, enabling type-safe model querying.

name: invalidate
description: invalidate is a Python library that continuously checks every stored agent memory against each new event—using the ~150 ms, $0.00006-per-check Jev yes/no model plus fixed rules—to mark stale facts superseded or contradicted without editing them, route uncertain cases to human review, and layer onto existing stores like Mem0, Chroma, or pgvector so agents stop answering from outdated memories.

name: pi-jev-reasoning-router-lite
description: A Pi Agent extension that routes each prompt through the Jev API to automatically pick the model's thinking level (none/low/high) — cutting reasoning cost on routine prompts while preserving depth on hard ones, with model gating, audit logging, and fail-safe fallback to high.

name: jevgate
description: JevGate is a CLI that reviews selected source files with TypeSafe Jev for organization, simplification, and shared-logic concerns, offering reports, JSON output, context controls, role assessment, caching, and upload limits for iterative or CI checks.

name: homing-pigeon
description: A local, read-only Gmail inventory tool that stores message metadata (senders, sizes, attachments) in SQLite and provides a browser UI to rank which senders and domains consume the most storage, plus CSV exports to guide mailbox cleanup.

name: piper-astra-jev
description: piper-astra-jev provides eight Jupyter-notebook demo runs that drive a real AgileX PiPER arm with large models, comparing Astra and Jev deciders across Grounding DINO, SAM 3, and STL-geometry perception for grasping, balanced carrying, and ~2 mm-clearance insertion.

name: demo-jev
description: Five runnable TypeScript samples demonstrating TypeSafe's Jev model returning typed, calibrated judgments (Choice, Score, Noul) that ordinary code composes—covering speculative fan-out triage, function calling, semantic find, multi-dimension ranking, and select-don't-generate extraction.

name: plotveil
description: PlotVeil is a Chrome extension that covers YouTube comments while checking them against the current and protected titles, keeps likely concrete plot disclosures hidden at a user-set threshold, fails closed, and requires explicit user action to reveal them.

name: pagegrade
description: A WXT Chrome extension that grades a page's content sections on ten weighted rubric metrics—clarity, concision, usefulness, readability, search intent—via TypeSafe AI Jev through your own Vercel AI Gateway key, showing per-section breakdowns, on-page A–E badges, and an overall page score.

name: KaLM-Jev
description: KaLM-Jev is a local PyTorch/Transformers service that wraps the KaLM-Reranker-V1-R2 reranker to return structured Choice/Score/Noul judgments (probabilities, expected scores, yes/no margins) via HTTP or Python, with an LRU document cache and no text generation.

name: jev-semgrep
description: jev-semgrep is a cross-language semantic grep that scores every line against a meaning you specify, letting you search English text in Japanese or vice versa and combine meanings with AND/OR/NOT logic for precise concept-based search.

name: jev-compare
description: jev-compare is a comparison utility that lets users evaluate differences between inputs, useful for quickly spotting discrepancies during development or review workflows.

name: jev-bot
description: jev-bot is a macOS-native MCP tool that lets Codex or ChatGPT desktop control native Mac apps through persistent JavaScript calls—offering app discovery, accessibility reads, screenshots, clicks, typing, and element-based or AI-driven (Jev) action selection via Cua Driver.

name: jev-align
description: jev-align is an experimental CLI that iteratively improves TypeSafe Jev AI Functions by surfacing uncertain dataset rows for human labeling, running GEPA optimization with configurable reflection models and providers (TypeSafe, Vercel, Cloudflare), and resumable runs that can keep learning from captured production examples.

name: tabjev
description: A Chrome extension that automatically sorts every newly opened tab into the right tab group by asking the Jev API a typed choice question with a calibrated probability, at roughly a cent per thousand tabs.

name: jev-pubmed-discovery
description: A Node.js toolkit that tests whether the Jev model can rediscover Swanson's 1986 fish oil–Raynaud's link by reading pre-1986 PubMed papers, extracting directional substance effects, and code-ranking candidates; includes checkpointed runs, a live dashboard, and a 50-disease benchmark.

name: kev
description: Kev is a local System One decision engine that turns unstructured state into typed probabilistic answers (Noul/Choice/Score) by scoring option-token logits instead of generating text, so invalid labels are impossible and applications get thresholdable distributions via Python, HTTP, or CLI.

name: skill-picker
description: A dependency-free CLI that sends a user request to TypeSafe's Jev model to rank an agent's skills and commands by fit probability, returning JSON suggestions with tunable thresholds and an eval harness so the agent can offer the right skill without ever invoking it.

name: JevImpact
description: JevImpact scores documented security findings via TypeSafe's Jev model, returning typed JSON (`is_vulnerability`, `impactful`, rubric-based `impact_score`, confidence, `needs_review`) from a CLI or importable Python API for threshold-tunable vulnerability triage.

name: jev-downloads-sorter
description: A macOS launchd agent that watches ~/Downloads and uses Jev decisions, with an offline extension-map fallback, to route each finished file or folder into your configured folders without overwrites using filename, type, size, source URL, and content hints.

name: jev-theme-designer
description: A web app that turns one aesthetic prompt into three ranked theme directions: Jev's systemOne scores options per design property, and the app maps top choices to curated colors, type, and spacing, compares them across sample pages, and exports versioned JSON with CSS variables.

name: llm-typesafe
description: An LLM plugin that exposes the TypeSafe `jev` model for probabilistic classification and scoring—yes/no ("noul") probabilities, multi-category choices with per-label probabilities, and fractional rubric scores—via CLI options or sync/async Python calls, with structured JSON input support.

name: jev-crash-course
description: An 11-level (~65 min) hands-on crash course on Jev, TypeSafe AI's fast "System One" decision model, with runnable real-API Python examples, a tested capstone project, and LiteLLM support for any provider—teaching cheap calibrated gating around LLM generation in agent loops.

name: second-thought
description: Second Thought is a terminal hook that AI-judges each shell command before it runs—allowing, warning, or blocking it—with a calibrated multiple-choice judge, pre-judging secret redaction, fail-open behavior, a typed `YES` override, a local audit log, and a free keyless mock mode for demos.

name: jev-accounting
description: A local Node.js prototype workbench that classifies pasted or synthetic bank transactions into illustrative account categories via the hosted TypeSafe Jev model through the Vercel AI Gateway, displaying per-category probabilities, flagging sub-threshold results as Unassigned for review, and exporting results—useful for evaluating Jev's classification accuracy before automating real bookkeeping.

name: simple-jev
description: Simple Jev is a local Hugging Face/PyTorch server that turns shared context plus choice, rubric-score, or truth questions into JSON answers by scoring next-token logits, reusing the common prompt’s KV cache to avoid generated completions and repeated prefill.

name: typedrank
description: TypedRank is an async Python reranking library that orders typed candidates for RAG, search, and agents via pluggable backends (hosted Jev, local/self-hosted Laya, or deterministic lexical fallback) plus routing, BM25, embeddings, fusion, diversity, caching, and metrics.

name: JevRev
description: JevRev is a Node.js CLI decision layer for LLM coding agents that sifts proposed approaches into bounded probes, audits evidence after each round, and watches long-running sessions for stalls or risk, returning typed next actions while preserving human control.

name: jev-bug-hunter
description: A bounded first-pass bug hunter that statically screens source files in overlapping windows, asking a hosted TypeSafe Jev judge validated true/false and multiple-choice questions to surface cited suspicious regions with honest "unknown"/"incomplete" statuses — without executing code, generating patches, or replacing tests and review.

name: jev-social
description: jev-social pairs Jev's decision loop with the socai CLI to drive your real Chrome through bounded read-only operations—search, open profiles/posts, read comments, optional TikTok downloads—across Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn, returning source-cited evidence and reports.

name: pi-ultracode
description: A Pi extension providing opt-in semantic analysis-depth modes (auto/focused/standard/deep) and deterministic multi-agent JavaScript workflows with parallel subagents, git worktree isolation, schema-validated output, durable resume, per-subtask effort routing, and live TUI observability.

name: QuantDinger
description: QuantDinger is an open-source, self-hosted AI trading platform that turns trading ideas into Python strategies with multi-provider AI research, server-side backtesting, paper and live execution across crypto exchanges and brokers, plus monitoring via web, mobile, API, and MCP interfaces backed by PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery workers.

name: MetaCog
description: MetaCog wraps any OpenAI-compatible or local LLM in an inference-time metacognition loop: a separate judge scores the model's answer and, if unsure, samples extra parallel thought paths, scores each path and distinct answer, and returns the best—lifting measured accuracy 76.7%→86.7% without training.

name: JevAny
description: JevAny is open-source infrastructure for training and deploying System 1 decision models whose API takes a state, question, and candidate options and returns a choice with calibrated probabilities, enabling ticket routing, tool selection, robot actions, and cheaper LLM agent loops.

name: jev-document-classification
description: Local-first app that sorts documents into configured folders via typesafe-ai/jev on Vercel AI Gateway, quarantining unreadable, low-confidence, or injection-suspect files, with bounded 4,500-char local profiles, batched requests, preview, undo, and cost audits.

name: jev-browser
description: Jev Browser is a Playwright-based browser automation SDK, CLI, and MCP tool that combines deterministic native operations with Jev semantic decisions for DOM-grounded act, observe, extract, assertions, and bounded multi-step workflows, preserving explicit verification provenance.

name: jev-skill-router
description: A Pi 0.87.1 extension that hides most skill metadata from the main model's prompt, then uses Jev matching and a Luna interpreter to select and inject only relevant SKILL.md instructions, automatically or via an on-demand search tool, keeping native /skill:name commands intact.

name: dragon-voice-control
description: Dragon is a macOS/Windows voice-control agent that turns speech into real OS actions—launching apps, dictating text, driving Chrome, media keys—using Deepgram STT and a decision model that only picks among code-extracted candidates, with a live dashboard showing its reasoning.

name: stylomail
description: StyloMail is a pre-release .NET two-way email security proxy that fronts back-end mail servers, durably owning the queue and catching compromised accounts, phishing, impersonation, and drift via twelve semantic evidence dimensions that only deterministic policy may act on.

name: abide
description: Abide is a CLI that hooks Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode to check every edit or turn against repository instruction rules via TypeSafe’s Jev decision model, catching violations linters miss, prompting in-turn repairs, and providing audit, calibration, cost, and reporting commands.

name: jevql
description: jevQL is a Postgres-facing semantic SQL engine that parses ordinary queries, evaluates `jev_*` predicates, probabilities, choices, and scores through TypeSafe’s Jev model, and exposes the results through a REPL/CLI, HTTP/MCP service, and Go/TypeScript/Python SDKs.

name: jev-proof-selector
description: Benchmarks TypeSafe Jev's lemma selection for Lean 4 proofs against Random, Overlap, BM25, normalized BM25, and OpenRouter rankers on a shared candidate pool, with kernel-checked results inspectable via a local web dashboard or CLI in dependency-free Python 3.9+.

name: jev-migrate
description: A CLI tool that scans TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python code for LLM calls that are just routing, scoring, or yes/no decisions, then reports confidence-scored detections, estimated cost/latency savings, and scaffolds for converting them to local TypeSafe Jev rules.

name: jwenv
description: jwenv is a WebGPU-based inference engine (Node.js and browser, no native dependencies) that runs Qwen3 GGUF models to return calibrated probability distributions over named answer options in a single forward pass, enabling cheap, batchable classification, scoring, and routing via a `/v1/systemone` API.

name: thoughtdag
description: ThoughtDAG is a local-first context-graph tool with a CLI and desktop app that indexes conversations across agents (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, Pi), recalls topic dossiers into prompts, and lets users edit graph wires to precisely control what context the model sees next.

name: laya-server
description: A local FastAPI server that runs the Laya decision model behind TypeSafe's Jev/System One wire API — a drop-in, keyless replacement returning calibrated probabilities for typed noul/choice/score questions in one forward pass, with three selectable checkpoints, a built-in /demo UI, and a CLI.

name: tattle
description: Tattle is an open-source macOS app that live-transcribes conversations from your microphone and system audio onto a labelled timeline, fact-checks claims as they're said via a System 1/System 2 model loop, and runs free on-device with Apple Speech on macOS 26+.

name: jev-claw
description: An OpenClaw plugin providing a `jev_route` tool that uses TypeSafe's Jev classifier to type incoming tasks by type, complexity, and risk, then maps them through a testable code-based routing policy — with escalation rules, sensitive-path guards, and an opt-in automatic routing hook — to pick the right model for each software-engineering task.

name: jevqa
description: jevqa runs plain-English Markdown checklists against your app in a real browser, turning the Jev model's probability answers about what's on screen into per-step Passed/Failed/Needs-review verdicts with evidence, framework-agnostic since it never reads source.

name: jev-last-safe-ms
description: A seeded Space Invaders ALE benchmark that uses cloned-state counterfactual rollouts to score whether model decisions arrive correctly before life loss, comparing JEV and LLM baselines on deadline-adjusted accuracy, latency, cost, and calibration, with mock validation.

name: ten-levels-of-jev
description: A runnable ten-level tutorial and live lab for TypeSafe's Jev — a ~300 ms JSON-in/typed-decisions-out API (noul/choice/score) that costs pennies per million calls — showing agentic engineers thirty concrete uses progressing from smart `if` statements in plain code to guardrail hooks, compaction triggers, cheap file judgments, and self-driven `ask_jev` tools inside the pi coding agent.

name: ha-gutcheck
description: A Home Assistant integration that runs weekly checkups—triaging unavailable entities, flagging possibly-breaking updates, suggesting areas and device classes, diagnosing stuck integrations—via the Jev decision model, queueing findings in Repairs without acting autonomously.

name: jev-legal-instrumentation-latam
description: A reproducible Spanish-language pilot benchmarking typed-decision classification on 30 public Argentine Supreme Court metadata records—comparing deterministic rules, a local 0.5B model, and the Jev SDK—to show that high model confidence does not equal legal correctness.

name: typesafe-cookie-consent
description: Chrome extension that replaces filter lists with TypeSafe's Jev decision model to read cookie banners and popups, pick and click the decline button (drilling into settings layers when needed), while hard-ignoring user-action dialogs; bring-your-own-key, no backend.

name: jevshield
description: jevshield is a Python middleware library that gates AI agent tool calls through single-pass, non-autoregressive security evaluations using TypeSafe's Jev models — combining risk-tier, destructiveness-probability, and blast-radius primitives to block dangerous actions in under 100ms, with decorator and LangChain integrations plus a zero-config local heuristic fallback.

name: jev-mcp
description: jev-mcp is a local stdio MCP server that gives hosts like Cursor and Codex nine typed TypeSafe Jev judgment tools — for routing steps, selecting prepared tool calls, reviewing patches, verifying claims, screening content, ranking candidates, and gating — returning Choice/Score/Noul answers with confidence and auto/review/escalate actions while the host executes tools itself.

name: jev-block-ad
description: An open-source Manifest V3 Chrome extension that blocks ads without filter lists by sending compact structural descriptions of suspicious page elements to TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model, which classifies each one so code-owned thresholds hide them—using your own API key, with caching, site rules, and a daily token budget.

name: astra-jev-new-vegas
description: Source for a supervised AI controller that completed Fallout: New Vegas's main story using read-only telemetry and bounded keyboard/mouse input, with navigation, dialogue, combat, watchdog, budget-ledger, recording, and post-production tooling for building game-playing agents.

name: jevgrep
description: jevgrep (`jg`) is a Node.js 22+ CLI that lets coding agents ask natural-language questions about a repository and returns relevant files, reading leads, and verbatim source excerpts in one stdout response, using the Jev model via Vercel AI Gateway to judge relevance.

name: say-hi
description: say-hi makes TypeSafe's option-picking JEV model chat by planning each reply's goal, tournament-selecting an answer word, then typing it one keystroke per API call, with a live keyboard UI, request inspection, cost caps, and evals — a starting point for canned-response chatbots.

name: typesafe-jev-drone-demo
description: A live Three.js drone demo with a typed FastAPI backend that lets TypeSafe's `jev-latest` pick each navigation action while exposing probabilities, confidence, latency, and model I/O, useful for inspecting typed decisions against deterministic collision-checked flight.

name: typesafe-cli
description: typesafe-cli is a `jev` shell command that pipes state plus typed questions (noul probabilities, multi-option choices, rubric scores) to the Jev API and returns typed answers, batching many questions into one ~0.3s request with key resolution, retries, and JSON output.

name: jev-security-prioritization
description: A reproducible Python benchmark that evaluates whether TypeSafe's Jev decision model (via OpenRouter's Decisions API) prioritizes SCA and SAST findings better than severity-only and context-points baselines, providing frozen synthetic datasets, a reference rubric, resumable experiment runners, and offline analysis scripts for metrics like accuracy, AUC, calibration, cost, and adversarial steerabil

name: dag-jev
description: A Rust tool (`cargo run`) that reads test input from `input.txt`, renders dependency graphs via `render.sh` into `core/out`, and lets you verify its Jev output against control dependencies generated by `generate_control.py` using a `dep_{}_{}: 0/1` format.

name: toxic-filter
description: A Chrome extension (MV3, Chrome 120+) that sends X post text to the TypeSafe Jev API using your own API token, classifies it into six toxicity categories (discrimination, trolling, hate, calls to attack, sneering, resignation), and hides posts above a configurable probability threshold (default 70%) behind a dismissible translucent overlay.

name: pi-jev
description: A Pi extension that pairs local coding models with hosted TypeSafe Jev judgments to cut end-to-end latency via ranked file-excerpt retrieval, large-tool-output focusing, optional skill hints and Qwen thinking control, plus caching and outage cooldowns.

name: fly-x-jev
description: A browser demo where a robot walks a road driven by real MaleCNS v1.0 fly connectome wiring—1,771 eye columns, LC/LPLC vision, dopamine-plastic mushroom-body memory, and descending motor neurons—with TypeSafe's Jev model picking each action, plus a 141,208-neuron three.js brain view.

name: jev-system-architect
description: A system-architecture skill that guides agents in decomposing TypeSafe Jev integrations—deciding where fuzzy semantic judgment should become bounded Choice, Score, or Noul questions while deterministic code keeps control flow, side effects, batching, and explicit uncertainty routing.

name: ComfyUI-SystemOne
description: A ComfyUI custom-node pack that routes workflows on natural-language judgments (choice, yes/no probability, score, each with confidence) through either the local Laya model or TypeSafe's hosted Jev API, enabling style routing, content gating, and real-person detection inside image-generation graphs.

name: typesafe-adblock
description: A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that heuristically collects ad-shaped DOM candidates on any page, sends compact JSON descriptions in batched requests to TypeSafe AI's Jev model (BYOK, no backend), and removes or highlights elements whose ad probability exceeds a configurable threshold.

name: jev-test-filter
description: CLI tool that scores every test in a repository against a git diff via TypeSafe's Jev model in one round trip, then emits or directly executes the correct selection arguments for vitest, jest, node --test, Playwright, cargo test, or go test so only plausibly affected tests run.

name: tmux-jev
description: A Python CLI-plus-skill that lets a shell-capable agent list, inspect, and capture local tmux worker panes, request read-only TypeSafe "Jev" judgments for pane selection or task-status assessment, and explicitly send input to a chosen pane.

name: JevVSPolymarket
description: JevVSPolymarket is a Node.js/pnpm toolkit that benchmarks the Jev model's probability forecasts on settled Polymarket sports/esports markets—scoring Brier and accuracy against historical market-price baselines via batch, repeat, and background-ablation experiments without trading.

name: jevcache
description: jevcache is a CLI that memoizes Jev-model decisions—deterministic functions of model, schema, and state—in a local, privacy-preserving ledger, cutting API spend and enabling offline recall, deterministic CI replay, and model-drift detection.

name: fastbrowse
description: fastbrowse is an experimental Python CLI browser agent that has a choice model pick each action from indexed page controls instead of generating selectors, while an LLM plans and reads, returning answers with verbatim-quoted citations under code-enforced authorization and secret scoping.

name: jev-frontend-qa
description: A Python CLI that performs evidence-driven frontend QA in real Chrome via Browser Harness, using the Jev model only to select bounded browser actions while deterministic code executes inputs, asserts DOM/HTTP/persistence evidence, enforces deny-default policies, and reports verdicts, screenshots, and usage costs.

name: jev-triage-gmail
description: A Chrome extension that runs inside your Gmail tab, uses your Jev API key to apply action, topic, urgency, and must-see labels, archive low-value mail, learn sender rules, and export native Gmail filters—keeping important email visible without a server or Gmail API project.

name: AnyJev
description: AnyJev turns any open LLM into a typed decision model that answers choice/bool/score questions from one prefill—no generation or fine-tuning—removing option-order bias with zero labels and calibrating probabilities with 100–500 labels for safe thresholded auto-decisions.

name: TypeLLM
description: TypeLLM is a client for type-safe constrained decoding on SGLang-served open LLMs, producing JSON Schema–typed outputs (enums, booleans, integers, numbers, text) with no out-of-schema values, prefix caching, sequential or batch execution, optional thinking, and sampling.

name: typesafe-chess
description: Local app that tests TypeSafe Jev as a chess decision-maker: chess.js lists the legal moves, Jev picks one, and Stockfish grades it, with configurable prompt setups, an adaptive Stockfish ladder, mock mode, a stats dashboard, and headless benchmarks.

name: jev-pages
description: jev-pages turns a few typed product notes into a fully designed landing page by picking the headline, look, layout, type, motion, color, and photos from fixed options via the Jev API or an offline preview, and re-designs around any clicked choice in ~0.2s.

name: arc-cua
description: arc-cua is a macOS action layer that lets any planner or LLM hand off bounded desktop subtasks (goal, inputs, verification, constraints) to a fast decision backend called JEV, which executes the observe–act UI loop over structured AX + OCR elements—eliminating expensive frontier-model reasoning for every click.

name: callee
description: Callee defines repeatable agent workflows as versioned YAML/Markdown resources that compose AI roles, shell scripts, human approvals, and typed model decisions via sequential, parallel, loop, and router control flow, validated pre-run and invocable from terminal or coding agents.

name: jev-highlight-cutter
description: jev-highlight-cutter is a Codex skill + Python CLI that scores transcript evidence via the Jev API and uses local FFmpeg to cut long interviews/podcasts into preference-matched, target-duration original-audio highlight reels with local review pages.

name: typesafe-jev-bridge
description: A zero-dependency Node.js bridge that exposes TypeSafe's Jev model—which answers typed yes/no, choice, and rubric-score questions with calibrated probabilities—as OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus a CLI, code-audit tool, and autofix loop usable from any OpenAI client.

name: Jev-Quantum
description: A Rust stochastic baseline server implementing the Jev System One protocol (`noul`/`choice`/`score`) that answers requests with sub-microsecond PRNG output instead of reading prompts, serving as a dummy/mock and lower bound for latency and agent-routing benchmarks.

name: OneVOneJev
description: OneVOneJev is a server-authoritative browser FPS where players queue to quickscope-duel an AI opponent ("Jev") in a 60 Hz WebSocket arena — first to 5 kills — with spectating, chat, killcam replays, and a TypeSafe-powered/heuristic AI.

name: jev-pr-quality
description: A GitHub Action and self-hosted dashboard that runs Jev AI reviews on full PR diffs across 19 typed quality dimensions, posting review comments, enforcing a minimum-score quality gate, and logging structured results to RawTree for multi-repository score tracking.

name: jev4k
description: jev4k is a Kotlin DSL and client library for TypeSafe's Jev model that lets you declare typed yes/no, multiple-choice, and ordinal-score questions about a given state, send them in one request, and receive calibrated typed answers—including enum-valued options—with probabilities and confidence your code can branch on.

name: jev-persona-memory
description: A Node.js tool that stores scoped, visibility-filtered long-term memories in SQLite FTS5, retrieves candidates via trigram index, and re-ranks them with the Jev LLM judge to drive two-persona dialogue generation, per-persona memory extraction, and roleplay experiments.

name: fin-benchmark-jev
description: Benchmarks TypeSafe's Jev 1.13 decisions model against Qwen 3.8 27B on Cerebras (plus controls) across four constrained-output finance tasks, reporting accuracy, macro-F1, latency, and cost from deterministic seeded samples, cached raw responses, and timestamped Excel reports.

name: JevUnreal
description: JevUnreal is an Unreal Engine 5.8 plugin that adds async Blueprint nodes (Yes/No, Choose, Probability, plus a raw request node) which send game-state descriptions to the TypeSafe Jev API and return AI decisions with confidence and latency, supporting direct API-key or proxied requests for packaged builds.

name: Jev-Mem
description: Jev-Mem is an agentic memory system for long-running AI agents: a lightweight System-One controller manages memory writing and retrieval over semantic, temporal, causal, and entity graph views, while a System-Two model synthesizes answers, improving quality and speed on LoCoMo.

name: jev-rag-bench
description: Benchmark harness that evaluates Jev (TypeSafe System One) as a RAG reranker and answerability judge over 258 TypeSafe-docs passages retrieved via BM25, reporting gold@1 improving 7→17 and 33/36 gating accuracy (vs BM25's tuned 30/36) at ~$0.00023 per query.

name: unclutter
description: WXT browser extension for Chrome/Chromium and Firefox that uses the Jev AI model (with your own Vercel AI Gateway or TypeSafe AI key) to hide nonessential page elements via reusable per-template rules cached locally, with manual or on-visit analysis and pause/resume controls.

name: dify-plugin-typesafe-ai
description: A Dify Tool plugin for TypeSafe AI that provides Yes/No binary judgments with a tunable threshold and an Evaluate action batching typed noul/choice/score questions, exposing decisions, probabilities, and token usage as workflow variables over HTTPS to api.typesafe.ai.

name: Kestrel-Agent
description: Kestrel is a terminal AI agent that connects to user-configured model providers (Codex, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and others) to run permission-gated tools for file editing, sandboxed shell commands, document reading, and web research, with reusable workflows, decision-service validation of plans and outputs, per-request budgets, and SQLite memory for sessions and evidence.

name: barrunto
description: A Chrome extension that asks the Jev model closed questions about each X post, profile, or Hacker News comment you browse, combines the returned probabilities into labels like Bait, Signal, or Insight, and fades or hides likely noise—entirely client-side with your own API key.

name: scribe-verify
description: Verifies AI-drafted clinical notes sentence-by-sentence against the encounter transcript using Jev's non-generative model, color-coding each statement as supported, contradicted, not found, or ambiguous, linking to source turns, and flagging omissions.

name: jevmetrics
description: `jevmetrics` is an experimental OpenTelemetry Collector connector that asynchronously calls TypeSafe's Jev model to score metric instruments' operational value from their metadata, then applies cached, threshold-based keep/drop policy to annotate or filter metrics before export.

name: comfyui-openrouter
description: A ComfyUI extension that exposes OpenRouter-hosted models as chat, image, video, audio, search, and decision nodes—supporting multimodal inputs, generation/editing, speech, embeddings/ranking, and probability-based branching—using your own API key with per-run billing.

name: jev-mcp
description: jev-mcp is a zero-dependency Go stdio MCP server that exposes TypeSafe's Jev System One model as four tools (ask, choose, score, noul), giving agents typed answers with probabilities and confidence for routing, classifying, ranking, and gating without spending reasoning tokens.

name: oxlint-plugin-jev
description: An oxlint plugin that turns plain-English yes/no questions about functions, calls, JSX elements, or whole files into lint rules—TypeSafe Jev returns a probability per match and reports an error at your configured cutoff, with per-file batching, answer caching, and CI fail/skip controls.

name: jev-trip
description: An explainable day-trip planner where an LLM drafts itineraries and the Jev model screens candidates, compares transport options, and reviews plans while deterministic code owns route facts, timing, validation, and repair — supporting single-day trips in mainland Chinese cities via Amap with replayable, streamed planning events.

name: system-one-sdk
description: System One SDK is a modular TypeScript toolkit for typed decisions over shared state, providing an evaluate client, choice/score/boolean question types, pluggable transports and hosted, LLM, local ONNX, and browser WebGPU adapters, plus batching, policies, and evaluation harnesses.

name: jev-superpowers
description: An agentic-skill framework gating coding agents' architecture decisions, dependency picks, shell commands, commits, and completion claims behind sub-second System One typed decisions (TypeSafe Jev cloud or offline Laya) to stop package hallucination and premature 'done'.

name: jev-ai-sdk-form-router
description: A Next.js 16/React 19 example app that uses Jev with AI SDK 7 to route three form types (leads, contact, issue reports) to the right team, falling back to openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast when Jev's confidence drops below 95%, plus editable samples, routing stats, and optional Resend email delivery.

name: JevControl
description: JevControl analyzes recorded AI-agent traces (LangSmith, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, or JSONL logs), flags bounded decision steps like tool routing and retries, and reruns them with a smaller model to measure latency, token, and cost savings plus decision fidelity—without touching the production agent.

name: jev-desktop
description: Jev Desktop is a Codex plugin that keeps a bounded decision loop inside the existing Computer Use runtime—selecting one operation and compatible UI target per scoped TypeSafe request—so browser tab and native macOS app automation avoids per-click round-trips while Codex retains control of scope, permissions, prepared values, and verification.

name: jev-slot-machine
description: A local Node/Python tool that runs Jev on a slot machine—autonomously betting, leaving to spend winnings, buying items, resuming statefully, exposing CLI controls and a browser view—and logs every decision with option probabilities to JSONL for analysis.

name: nautilus-compass
description: nautilus-compass is a local-first AI-agent memory and reliability layer that combines BGE-m3 hybrid long-term recall, pre-action drift detection, and cross-agent contract auditing via CLI, MCP, and A2A integrations.

name: joxide
description: joxide is a zsh plugin that layers TypeSafe Jev semantic ranking on top of zoxide's directory index, so `j` can jump to projects by natural-language description or visit date while exact name matching, `z` commands, and local-only mode still work.

name: sqlite-jev
description: sqlite-jev is a SQLite loadable extension and Python package adding natural-language predicates, classification, and scoring to SQL via TypeSafe Jev, including a batched `jev_rows` virtual table joinable by rowid, scalar functions, connection-local caching, and spend guards.

name: ai-elo-ranker
description: AI Elo Ranker is a FastAPI/asyncio tournament engine that ranks large text datasets via pairwise LLM-judged duels, using Swiss-system matchmaking to cut O(N²) comparisons to ~O(N log N), position-bias randomization, dynamic K-factor Elo scoring, SQLite persistence, and a real-time WebSocket dashboard with live leaderboards and match metrics.

name: youtube-sponsor-detection
description: A Chrome extension and companion web app that detect sponsor reads in YouTube videos using TypeSafe's Jev model over transcripts or live audio (via Deepgram), auto-skipping them with code-controlled timestamps and confidence thresholds so model uncertainty never cuts into actual content.

name: grill-with-jev
description: grill-with-jev is a three-skill fork that runs fully automated design interviews: invoking `/grill-with-docs` walks a design-tree frontier, sends typed questions to the Jev answerer via bundled scripts, applies answers as `CONTEXT.md` glossary updates and gated ADRs, and fails closed with no writes if the `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or API is unavailable.

name: jev-doc-search
description: jev-doc-search finds the pages answering a question in documents hundreds of pages long by pairing Jev's probabilistic `Choice` calls with PageIndex's hierarchical document tree, making one small choice per level with beam search and `Noul` verification — no vector DB or embeddings.

name: drift-guard
description: A Claude Code and Codex hook pair that treats a session's first prompt as its intent, has Jev judge each later prompt and agent reply for drift via an EMA score with warn/block thresholds, and supports `drift:` escape commands, feedback labels, and adherence reports.

name: jev-scout
description: An MCP stdio server whose guarded_search, guarded_fetch, and research_report tools score every web search result and fetched page with Jev decision-model judgments (relevance, credibility, steering risk), streaming each decision to a JSONL ledger and live local dashboard.

name: jev-search
description: A Chrome MV3 extension that performs semantic in-page search by natural-language description, using TypeSafe's Jev model via the Noul primitive to score each candidate word against page sentences and highlight only matching terms (e.g., "apple" for "food items") with Cmd+F-style navigation, keeping API keys in the background service worker.

name: jev-poker
description: jev-poker is a browser-based No-Limit Texas Hold'em game whose CPU opponents make typed probabilistic decisions via TypeSafe Jev, with bring-your-own-key gateway routing, personas, spectator mode, hand/equity-aware reasoning, benchmarks, and reusable npm engine/agent packages.

name: TheOnlyArtz.github.io
description: A Hebrew/RTL React single-page app that ranks the 17 Knesset-26 party lists against a user's free-text ideology via a Supabase Edge Function scoring their verbatim manifestos, backed by local axis-vector analysis and a live public aggregate-stats board refreshed every 30 seconds.

name: jev-autopilot
description: A Three.js 3D drone simulator where TypeSafe's Jev model autonomously pilots a drone from pad A to pad B across a procedurally generated city: code builds plain-language situation reports, Jev answers six typed stick/landing questions with calibrated probabilities, and code converts the answers into stick deflections.

name: mini-jev
description: mini-Jev is a reproducible Qwen3-4B benchmark and local demo that measures whether lettered multiple-choice logit reads can replace grammar-constrained JSON generation for closed schema fields, quantifying accuracy, speed, abstention, dependent-field, and KV-cache tradeoffs.

name: layajev
description: layajev is a CLI/server tool that runs a Jev-compatible decision API locally, serving a verified Laya model via HTTP endpoints (`GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/systemone`) that answer choice, score, and noul questions with fully in-process inference and an explicit fetch/convert/serve model lifecycle.

name: jev-form-filler-extension
description: A Chrome MV3 side-panel extension that scans web form fields, asks the Jev API to match each field against candidate values built from locally stored personal details, validates picks via confidence thresholds, then fills the page only when you click "Fill selected."

name: jevtok
description: jevtok is a Python library and CLI that bit-for-bit reproduces the undocumented tokenizer of TypeSafe's Jev decision model—an `o200k_base` variant producing more tokens than `tiktoken`—enabling exact token counting and pre-request cost prediction (verified with zero mismatches on 5.6M tokens and 403/403 requests) via a `tiktoken`-style `encode`/`decode`/`count` API plus `estimate_request_token

name: jimothy
description: Jimothy is a CLI plus Node.js and browser SDK that trains small, fast local classifiers from Jev-compatible task definitions and labeled or teacher-generated examples, offering calibrated predictions, evaluation, and offline inference via TF-IDF or MiniLM backends.

name: demo-expanso-jev
description: Demos pairing Expanso Edge pipelines with TypeSafe's Jev: routine log lines are fingerprinted and archived without model calls while ambiguous records get severity, team and routing judgments (with hold-and-release on outage), plus a live Kubernetes pod-label workflow.

name: jev-rlm
description: A minimal Recursive Language Models (RLM) experiment that runs the RLM architecture against the Jev model via `uv run python main.py`, reading input from `data/context.txt`, toggling Jev usage with `USE_JEV`, and appending results to `data/reslts.json` plus interaction traces to `data/traces.jsonl` for comparing runs.

name: AgentZeroLite
description: AgentZero Lite is a single-process Windows desktop IDE (WPF/Avalonia) offering multi-tab, multi-workspace ConPTY terminals plus a dockable chat pane that forwards text, keystrokes, and skill macros to whichever AI CLI is active—enabling side-by-side Claude/Codex sessions, cross-model AI↔AI dialogue via IPC, on-device voice/LLM orchestration, and scriptable remote control.

name: Gambler-Jev
description: A localhost Flask blackjack game where an AI companion, Jev, reads the table after each deal and shows HIT/STAND/DOUBLE percentages, exact bust chance, and a plain-language recommendation via a TypeSafe API call, falling back to math-only basic strategy without a key.

name: better-email-filter
description: A macOS Gmail triage tool that uses TypeSafe AI's Jev API and local SQLite state to label inbox messages as Spam, Ignore, Important, or Review, optionally archiving or trashing them, while reusing user-corrected labels as examples for future decisions.

name: jev-test
description: Benchmark harness and results for a pipeline where a dedicated judge model (TypeSafe's Jev) makes every decision a small local model is bad at, evaluated on 500 SimpleQA questions, plus `harness/audit.py` for auditing any judge's confidence scores via AUROC and gate mobility.

name: jev-align
description: A CLI/MCP/programmable verifier that scores every LLM response or agent plan on calibrated alignment heads (sycophancy, deception, overreach, sneaking, etc.) in ~800ms for ~$0.003, returning auditable probabilities and pass/flag/block verdicts enforceable via CI exit codes.

name: jev-plays-pokemon
description: jev-plays-pokemon is an autonomous Pokémon Red agent that feeds TypeSafe's text-only Jev model RAM-derived snapshots (dialog, walkability map, NPC positions, party/bag/battle state, injected short-term memory) each turn and converts its typed goal/button answers into PyBoy emulator inputs via A* pathfinding and deterministic safeguards, reliably completing the opening sequence through starter sel

name: jev-browser-wingman
description: Delegates one bounded browser action on the open, logged-in Chrome to a TypeSafe Jev decision (pick rows, fill forms, click wizards)—with values typed locally and never sent, irreversible actions gated by single-use confirm tokens, and an optional fail-closed sensitive-page policy—while the calling agent keeps planning.

name: LLM2Jev
description: LLM2Jev turns local language models into Jev-style structured decision models, extracting Choice/Score/Noul probabilities from prefill logits without token-by-token decoding, with order-independent candidate scoring, multimodal inputs, SGLang prefix-cache reuse, and a System One–compatible API.

name: jev-gpt
description: jev-gpt generates text using jev—a model that only answers typed questions with probabilities—by hierarchically querying word type, WordNet category, embedding-clustered word groups, then the word, plus a final ranking pass (~400 calls, ~90 seconds, ~2 cents per prompt).

name: minicpm5-jev
description: minicpm5-jev serves the 2.5 GB MiniCPM5-2B-8bit model locally on Apple Silicon as a Jev-compatible `/v1/systemone` decision API and reproduces official JevBench public-item results (0.580 vs hosted Jev's 0.866), enabling private, offline structured-decision evaluation.

name: chofusai-birdplayer
description: A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that auto-plays the Flappy-style minigame on chofusai.jp's map page by reading ball and obstacle positions from canvas pixels, sending numeric state to a configurable Jev-compatible `/v1/systemone` API, and executing its click/wait decisions.

name: imajev
description: imajev is a family of small open-weight (Apache-2.0, 2B–9B) vision-language models that compare up to two photos against a business's own records or text and return calibrated probabilities over caller-defined answer options with a trained explicit "can't tell" abstention, running locally in ~0.1–0.35 s per decision so systems can act automatically when confident and escalate to humans otherwi

name: is-jeven
description: is-jeven is a joke TypeScript/JavaScript package exposing an async `isEven(num, options?)` function that calls TypeSafe AI's Jev model to determine whether an integer is even, supporting API-key override and AbortSignal cancellation.

name: rspamd-jev
description: rspamd-jev is an experimental, disabled-by-default Rspamd plugin that asynchronously sends sampled eligible mail to TypeSafe's Jev API for zero-score shadow evaluation—optionally paired with GPT verdicts—so operators can compare spam-classification quality without affecting delivery decisions.

name: tarnlight
description: Tarnlight is a free, open-source Windows app that records every answer your apps get from TypeSafe's Jev AI model, shows decisions and confidence live, and lets you grade correctness and set confidence thresholds to measure how far to trust Jev on your own data.

name: mcp-jev
description: A minimal MCP server exposing a `jev_decide` tool that lets Cursor, Claude Code, and other MCP clients evaluate a `state` against typed yes/no, choice, and score questions via TypeSafe's Jev fast classifier, returning structured probabilities and answers over stdio or HTTP from a Docker container.

name: decision-desk
description: Decision Desk is an open-source Node.js support-triage demo that turns each incoming ticket into four typed, confidence-bearing decisions (queue, priority, handling risk, next action) with probabilities over app-supplied options plus real model, provider, latency, and cost.

name: jev-plays-starcraft-2
description: An experimental StarCraft II harness where the Jev LLM makes every probabilistic gameplay decision via the game API while Python handles observation, validation, and transport, with commit-triggered policy hot-reloads, mission sequencing, JSONL decision logging, and a soft dollar spending cap.

name: tetris-bench
description: Tetris-bench is a dependency-free Node.js benchmark that simulates every legal Tetris placement for local or OpenRouter-hosted brains, scores their choices in untimed IQ or real-time Blitz modes over fixed seeds, and saves hash-verified replays for reproducible model rankings.

name: Astra-Ares
description: Astra-Ares is an experimental patched Codex CLI where a Jev evaluator adjusts GPT-6 reasoning effort mid-task—preserving prompt-cache prefixes and leasing each choice across generations—to cut token use by matching thinking depth to the next step.

name: jev-filter
description: A Chrome extension that sends visible X post text through OpenRouter to the TypeSafe Jev 1.13 model, highlighting red or hiding posts matching up to five user-defined categories and logging per-category detection counts with hourly, daily, and weekly stats.

name: jev-mac-voice
description: Jev Mac Voice is a local macOS Electron app that lets you control your Mac through natural spoken English conversations using the OpenAI Realtime API, combining React UI, native accessibility automation, optional screen sharing, and approval-gated actions.

name: JEV-Paper-Radar
description: A serverless GitHub Actions tool that judges every new arXiv, bioRxiv, or RSS paper against plain-English interests via TypeSafe's Jev model, emitting calibrated probabilities with tunable thresholds to build a daily page, RSS feed, and optional digests for ~6¢/day.

name: jde
description: JDE (Jev Decision Engine) is a Node.js library that verifies AI agent claims—like whether a task was actually completed—by decomposing judgments into typed per-part questions answered by a swappable judge, returning calibrated probabilities governed by JSON policies, with every decision recorded in an auditable ledger.

name: jev-visual
description: A runnable Apple Silicon project for learning vision-language inference with Qwen3.5-0.8B via MLX, answering multiple questions per image by scoring candidate logits over shared multimodal context instead of autoregressive generation, with a local UI, CLI, HTTP API, demos, and benchmarks.

name: OpenWhisper
description: OpenWhisper is a cross-platform desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux that provides hotkey-driven dictation, audio-file transcription, and meeting capture with live dashboards using local speech models (Whisper, Parakeet, Qwen3-ASR, Moonshine) or the OpenAI API, plus AI text cleanup, searchable history, and export.

name: KaLM-Ultrafast
description: KaLM-Ultrafast is a local, CPU-runnable Chrome browser agent that loops observe-decide-act using the KaLM-Jev Nano reranker to choose grounded actions from indexed page elements, with a live inspector exposing every model decision plus freshness and occlusion guards that validate targets before execution.

name: SystemOneHarness
description: SystemOneHarness is a Python harness that turns a System One decision model into an agent loop by observing an environment, compiling its finite declared action space into typed questions, gating each model decision by confidence thresholds, executing the chosen action, and recording complete traces—with pluggable process, MCP, and browser environments plus a UHP-conformant server.

name: jev-skill-suggester
description: jev-skill-suggester is a Python CLI (also packaged as a Codex skill) that uses TypeSafe Jev to recommend relevant skills from those already installed, helping you pick the right capability for a task, with bilingual docs and live examples.

name: jev-file-search
description: jev-file-search is a Python CLI that finds local files by content: a model triages filenames, types, and short text previews, then reads deeper only into uncertain files, keeping natural-language searches like "find subscription receipts, not credit top-ups" fast and cheap.

name: greenwash-oss
description: A self-hosted GitHub App that scans each changed hunk in pull requests with TypeSafe structured-judgment models and code rules to catch AI agents gaming CI—skipped tests, weakened assertions, hard-coded answers—reporting probabilistic findings via check runs and annotations.

name: typesafe-ai-playground
description: A zero-install Python playground serving a local three-panel dashboard for running 110 editable example scenarios — games, dilemmas, reasoning challenges, and practical use cases — through the TypeSafe API, with A/B comparisons, matched bias checks, typed noul/choice/score results, and run export.

name: ReportJevBench
description: A JevBench-based benchmark of 90 real Roblox game reports with operator-labeled valid/invalid verdicts, used to measure and compare how accurately pre-screening models (e.g., Jev vs. Solar Decide) auto-reject false reports under production-identical prompts.

name: jev-x-spam-filter
description: A Chrome extension that collapses spam replies (crypto shilling, porn solicitation, copy-paste bot floods) under X/Twitter status pages into expandable notices, combining local pattern rules with the typesafe-ai/jev evaluation model on Vercel AI Gateway for uncertain cases, with adjustable sensitivity.

name: jev-drive
description: jev-drive is a top-level index for an autonomous driving research repo (VennIntelligence), mapping every document and directory—how-to docs, research topics, decision log, surveys, experiment plans, results, figures, scripts, and the `jevdrive` Python package—so any repo content is reachable from one place.

name: jev-skils
description: A Claude Code skill that teaches agents to integrate TypeSafe's Jev System One model into JS/TS projects via noul/choice/score typed-decision primitives, with SDK/API references, a copyable retry wrapper, a runnable ticket-router demo, and confidence-gated routing patterns.

name: browser-agent
description: A PHP library that drives a remote Chrome over CDP toward a plain-language goal on a URL, picking each action from on-page controls and returning what it did, evidence, console errors, and failed requests, with read-only-by-default runs, replayable scripts, and caller JavaScript DOM queries.

name: jev-engineering
description: Jev-gate screens every AI coding agent tool call through layered hard rules, an allowlist, and a fast decision model returning allow/ask/deny in ~400ms for ~$0.00002, with observe/guard/enforce modes, log-based calibration, a 300-call attack kit, and MCP support.

name: ClearToPay
description: ClearToPay is a headless Claude Code accounts-payable agent (MCP server over a mock ERP) that pays invoices, wires, and refunds while every money-adjacent tool call passes through a Failproof policy layer—hard code rules plus Jev verdicts—that blocks payment fraud with actionable steering and measures reliability via calibration, simulation, and pass^k matrix runs.

name: x-post-checker
description: AmplifyX is a Chrome/Firefox MV3 extension that scores X drafts' viral potential as you type, optionally blends in bring-your-own-key AI judgment, badges timeline posts with their main spread reason, suggests rewrites, and falls back to fully local, telemetry-free scoring.

name: TerraBlind
description: A tModLoader mod exposing Terraria perception, pathfinding, building, and combat primitives over 152 HTTP endpoints, wired into a `/start` pipeline that autonomously runs a fresh world to killing the Wall of Flesh, plus a Jev model-driven boss-fighting layer.

name: jul
description: JuL is an offline MLX drop-in for the TypeSafe (Jev) Python SDK that answers typed decisions (Choice, Noul, Score) on Apple Silicon by comparing embedding vectors instead of generating tokens, yielding calibrated classifications in 64–273 ms, plus contexts and autotune heads.

name: jev-belay
description: A Claude Code Stop hook that locally verifies whether checks actually ran after file changes, and—only when nothing passed—makes one cheap Jev call to detect unverified "done" claims, blocking the turn with a reason so the agent runs the suite instead of ending falsely.

name: jev-oasis
description: A fork of the CAMEL-AI OASIS social simulation engine that cuts LLM API costs by routing deterministic agent actions (liking, scrolling, following) through TypeSafe Jev's fast, low-cost System 1 router and invoking an LLM only for generative actions like posts and comments, reducing API calls ~67%.

name: jev-agent-skill-router
description: A Python CLI and library that routes a request to one skill in a catalogue—or abstains via no-skill or review—using batched TypeSafe Jev judgements, returning typed decisions with probabilities, confidence, latency and token usage for skill selection at scale without executing skills.

name: Typesafe_chess_eval
description: A tool evaluating typesafe AI chess performance, revealing that the model plays poorly — frequently calling draws in heavily unbalanced positions and assigning low loss probability even when a side is actually losing — suggesting it was not optimized for structured games like chess.

name: jev-ar
description: A 322M-parameter local model that routes Arabic queries (MSA, Gulf dialects, code-switched) over caller-supplied route lists in ~10 ms, returning the best route, calibrated per-route probabilities, and an escalation flag—achieving 83.4% accuracy on 60-way routing without retraining.

name: semble-jev
description: Semble + Jev (`sj`) is a Python CLI that semantically searches local code repositories via Semble's local embedding index, filters retrieved snippets for relevance using the Jev API, and returns ranked source with file/line locations and reading leads — reducing the token context coding agents consume by up to ~54–74% in tests, with `--local` offline mode, strict/fallback error handling, JSON

name: n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai
description: An n8n community node exposing the TypeSafe AI System One API as workflow operations—yes/no probabilities, one-of-N choices, ordered-level scores, batched multi-question evaluation, and model listing—returning calibrated probabilities that workflows can branch on without prompt engineering.

name: Jev-Desktop
description: Jev Desktop lets AI agents operate Windows applications through MCP or CLI, autonomously executing bounded tasks locally—observing windows, choosing controls, typing text—then returning the result or a help request instead of a model turn per click.

name: CLM
description: CLM serves CLM-8B, a contrastively trained System One model (frozen Qwen3-8B encoder + 20M projection heads), via a TypeSafe-compatible API and playground for typed decisions, candidate ranking, and agentic verification with cached embeddings at up to 9× lower latency.

name: JevGPT
description: JevGPT is a ChatGPT-style chat app that generates replies autoregressively with Jev, a multiple-choice model—each word sampled from a ~1,800-word vocabulary via grouped questions and top-12 continuation re-ranking, with a streaming UI showing word alternatives and confidence.

name: jev-linkedin-saved-classifier
description: Reads your LinkedIn Saved Posts from your own logged-in Chrome over CDP, assigns each post to categories you define via one Jev call per post, and outputs a searchable, filterable HTML board plus CSV and JSON, using human-paced scrolling to protect your account.

name: rekordbox-jev
description: Experimental macOS prototype that lets the Jev AI agent autonomously DJ in Rekordbox—reading decks via ScreenCaptureKit/Vision OCR and driving keyboard/pointer controls through a Swift bridge to select, sync, and mix tracks—useful for hands-off AI-controlled sets with a floating widget exposing its reasoning.

name: jev-reasoning-lab
description: jev-reasoning-lab packages the Jev reasoning API as offline-first Jupyter notebooks plus unit tests, demonstrating typed decisions, 18-lens routing, decision receipts, numeric recurrence findings, and an exact-tool adversarial peer, with paid live cells gated behind explicit opt-in env vars.

name: typesafe-mario
description: TypeSafe Mario is a Python harness that lets TypeSafe's Jev model play Super Mario Bros. by parsing emulator RAM into structured JSON describing Mario's motion, hazards, terrain, and timing, then translating the model's Choice/Noul/Score judgments into controller inputs, with a live telemetry dashboard and per-decision JSONL logging.

name: jev-loop-benchmark
description: A reproducible benchmark harness that runs five SWE-bench tasks under three coding-agent setups—cheap-only, JEV-routed hybrid, and strong-only—with official Docker grading, per-arm artifacts, and provider-priced cost tracking to compare resolution rates, cost, and agent time.

name: agentrun
description: AgentRun is a Node.js workflow DSL that lets existing agents execute repeatable, inspectable steps combining tool calls, Jev typed decisions with confidence thresholds, and agent invocations—supporting nested workflows, parallel mapping, bounded loops, and escalation paths while preserving the host app's tools, model access, permissions, and budgets.

name: subcortex
description: subcortex is a local daemon that adds a fast typed-decision layer to 29 terminal coding agents—via a hosted API (~250 ms) or a private local model (~10 ms)—to flag simple prompts, trim unneeded tool output, and preserve context across compaction.

name: skills
description: A collection of agent skills for building with TypeSafe's System One API, giving coding agents reusable guidance and workflows that make it easier to integrate and work with the API correctly.

name: jev-bot
description: Jev-bot is a public hosted web app and loopback CLI that evaluates a user-described idea against a complete exported library of 466 Jev use cases and findings, returning a proposed visual workflow, illustrative inputs with copyable Jev JSON, external evidence links, and per-stage token and cost estimates.

name: jevfill
description: Jevfill is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension that autofills web forms by sending field context plus locally stored plain-text notes to the Jev API to match fields against note lines with a configurable confidence threshold, highlighting results for review while never sending or filling password and payment fields.

name: Jev-MongoDB
description: Jev-MongoDB is a real-time customer-care triage demo where MongoDB change streams trigger TypeSafe's Jev model to return four typed judgments (category, sentiment, urgency, safety) in ~300 ms, then push verdicts to live dashboards via SSE with no polling.

name: logjev
description: LogJev is a Node.js/TypeScript server that turns any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint returning `top_logprobs` into a structured decision API, yielding full probability distributions for choice, score, and noul questions over text, image, and audio inputs.

name: dsh-jev-guard
description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that hard-intercepts every bash/pwsh command before execution via unoverridable offline rules, a read-only pre-screen, and a ~300ms Jev yes/no semantic check, returning allow/revise/block/escalate to prevent irreversible data loss.

name: jev-java
description: jev-java is an idiomatic Java SDK for integrating the TypeSafe AI Jev System One decision engine, letting Java applications invoke and manage AI-powered decisions through a natural, Java-native API.

name: syft-listening
description: Syft Listening is a database-free Rails web app that uses browser Web Speech API transcription and a server-side Jev proxy to turn finalized speech into live, toggleable insights for factual claims, specificity, complexity, grammar, emotion, and speech habits without storing API keys.

name: jev-as-a-judge
description: A reproducible benchmark that uses TypeSafe's Jev decision model as a non-autoregressive judge for agent evals, showing it matched human labels on frozen weather-agent runs with lower variance, cost, and latency than GPT-5.6 and Claude judges.

name: typed-decisions-shadow-layer
description: A shadow CRM decision layer that turns inbound WhatsApp/Telegram/email messages into typed, confidence-scored outputs (intent, division, urgency, human-handoff and lead probabilities) via TypeSafe's Jev or a JSON-forced local model, logging decisions without sending.

name: decisionpacks
description: DecisionPacks is a Node.js library and CLI that packages LLM judgments as versioned, testable JSON dependencies with declared inputs, pinned models, validated responses, deterministic gating rules, audit records, and policy replay that recomputes decisions from changed gates without re-running inference.

name: clojev
description: CloJev is an unofficial Clojure SDK for the TypeSafe System One API that sends state and typed questions (noul, choice, score), lists models, and returns validated data with retries, Retry-After support, structured errors, and JVM or Jolt HTTP backends on a portable .cljc core.

name: SemIf
description: SemIf adds semantic if-condition evaluation backed by open models running locally on a home NVIDIA RTX 3090, enabling meaning-based branching without depending on a hosted model service.

name: aayans-yc-indexor
