description: A search tool that matches free-text descriptions of a YC startup against all 6,241 companies via four vector signals — write-up embeddings, logo image vectors, OCR'd logo text, and tags — then returns calibrated probabilities rendered as a physics pile of logos on Apple Silicon Macs.

name: semif-go
description: A lightweight Go adapter that turns a compatible local GGUF LLM served by llama.cpp into a Jev-like decision API, returning typed Choice, Noul (yes/no), and Score answers over text, image, audio, or video by scoring next-token probabilities for labeled options.

name: wordle-beyond-the-list
description: A self-contained browser-based Wordle solver that converts color feedback into probability-ranked candidates and next-guess suggestions—using baked-in Jev word priors and NYT answer history, with no API key or server—to solve current games and update its history.

name: TypeSafeAI.Net
description: TypeSafeAI.Net is a community .NET SDK (net8.0/net10.0, AOT-safe) for the TypeSafe AI System One API, providing typed Noul/Choice/Score questions that return calibrated probabilities, plus Polly retries, DI, OpenTelemetry diagnostics, and Microsoft.Extensions.AI middleware for guardrails, intent routing, tool calls, and evaluation.

name: necro
description: Necro runs Qwen3.5-0.8B locally to score candidate answers, yes/no questions, and ordered choices directly with probabilities—no explanation or JSON parsing—served via CLI or a TypeSafe-compatible HTTP API, using base, LoRA, or exported merged weights.

name: jev-codex-router
description: A Codex Router plugin that classifies every turn with Jev and routes it to the cheapest capable model (luna/sol/astra) at adaptive reasoning depth—cutting cost ~60% vs all-frontier—with fail-open fallback, dry-mode substitutes, and local decision logs.

name: JevPixelArt
description: A Next.js tool that generates pixel art by asking the Jev model one Score question per channel per pixel through the TypeSafe API, sharpening the returned probability distributions into colors, and painting a live canvas via chunked, resumable browser-side requests with PNG/JSON export.

name: jev-bot
description: jev-bot is a zero-dependency Python CLI that streams simulated or live market states through TypeSafe's JEV decision model (or a transparent offline fallback) to get typed BUY/SELL/HOLD/AVOID verdicts with calibrated probabilities, then enforces a risk gate and executes only approved trades on paper.

name: typesafe-skill-router
description: An opt-in, stdlib-only skill router for Hermes Agent that uses TypeSafe (Jev) to name the single most relevant skill to load before each model call, costing roughly $0.001 per routed turn.

name: agent-chaperone
description: agent-chaperone is a calibrated screening layer for AI agent tool calls that proxies MCP servers and client hooks to judge calls before execution and results before the agent reads them, logging probability-scored decisions against policy thresholds in shadow, enforce, or strict modes.

name: plausible-rooms
description: A Node.js harness that deterministically generates one-room fantasy-industrial scenes with seeded faults, has the Jev model judge each as a place via fixed questions, buckets verdicts under pre-registered rules, and renders auditable runs in local galleries.

name: jev-use
description: jev-use is a macOS voice-and-typed computer-use agent that reads the Accessibility tree instead of screenshots, lets an LLM pick each on-screen action, executes presses, typing, menus, scrolling and window arrangement, and verifies real effects in a loop until done.

name: jev-precheck
description: jev-precheck is an MCP proxy that forwards reads untouched but, before each write, fetches affected records and computes comparisons in code so Jev can flow, warn, or hold well-formed but wrong calls like duplicate payments or oversized credit notes.

name: jev-judge-mcp
description: An MCP server giving coding agents eleven TypeSafe Jev-model tools that judge supplied evidence against enumerable questions—claim support, page safety, file selection, patch completion—returning sub-second typed probabilities a policy maps to auto, review, or escalate actions.

name: jev-cli
description: A composable Rust CLI that pipes stdin records through TypeSafe's Jev model primitives—choice, score, and noul—emitting ordered JSON verdicts with probabilities and token usage, plus concurrency, retries, pinned models, and keychain auth for scriptable probabilistic judgments.

name: system-one-adapter-python
description: Drop-in replacement for typesafe_sdk's `system_one` evaluation API backed by OpenAI/Anthropic LLMs instead of TypeSafe, enabling cost/speed/intelligence comparisons with sync/async clients, structured outputs, probability normalization, retries, and usage/debug telemetry.

name: jev-pr-judge
description: A web app, CLI, and GitHub Action that judges whether a pull request does what it claims, combining TypeSafe System One typed answers (scores, yes/no flags, verdict) with deterministic code facts and code-defined policy rules — cheap enough to gate every PR.

name: jev-korean-benchmark
description: A reproducible, frozen 100-question-per-cell evaluation measuring whether the TypeSafe Jev decision model degrades on Korean versus English across four public test sets (Belebele, PAWS-X, KorMedMCQA, MedQA), reporting accuracy with uncertainty intervals, input-order sensitivity, latency, cost, and a mainstream-LLM comparison.

name: jev-graph
description: jev-graph is a browser page plus PHP server for visually building and running composable-jev graphs—adding nodes, querying gates as truth tables or sweeps, and streaming answers through TypeSafe or OpenRouter, with a keyless simulated mode and host/CORS-checked JSON runs.

name: jev-buildathon
description: A policy layer for an autonomous customer-support agent: 11 PreToolUse guards inspect every tool call—code decides deterministic rules, Jev judges ambiguous cases—blocking unverified disclosure, refund diversion, prompt injection, and misrouted escalations before execution, with hosted evals.

name: webmcp-jev-experiment
description: A client-side Chrome extension that routes WebMCP tools exposed by the current page through Jev, a structured-decision model that picks tools and enumerable arguments as typed choices in parallel, falling back to a configured LLM for free-text parameters and looping until task completion.

name: jev-secrets
description: jev-secrets is a PHP, JavaScript, and Python library that pseudonymizes names, emails, API keys, card numbers, and other secrets in Jev requests with reversible, format-preserving stand-ins—via SDK wrappers or direct body rewriting—so sensitive data never reaches the service while responses restore the originals.

name: calibrate
description: Calibrate is a pure-Python-stdlib CLI that evaluates AI decision-model calibration from a local CSV or monitored production logs, reporting accuracy, ECE, Brier score, AUROC, false-accept/reject rates, drift, and threshold recommendations in self-contained HTML, entirely offline.

name: typesafe21
description: A terminal-based blackjack simulator pitting random, basic-strategy, and AI players against identical starting hands, using TypeSafe's System One Choice and Score primitives for autonomous decisions and balance-based bet sizing informed by full shoe and counting state.

name: FailProofAI_Hackaton
description: FailProofAI_Hackaton wraps an unmodified AI accounts-payable agent with Jev policy guardrails that judge every money-moving tool call against the agent's policy manual—blocking fraud like fake bank-change emails, split payments, and unverified authority—plus deterministic rule floors, a before/after demo dashboard, and offline tests.

name: JevGuard
description: JevGuard is a semantic policy engine plugin for OpenCode agents that evaluates each turn's attributed diff against versioned `.jev/rules.md` policies plus built-in scope-creep and complexity checks, returning PASS/WARN/FAIL verdicts and optional observe-only remediation proposals.

name: whistle
description: Whistle is a macOS 15+ Apple Silicon menu-bar app that recognizes whistled melodies (registered by blowing each tune three times) to launch or focus apps and run Apple Shortcuts, classifying pitch/rhythm features—never raw audio—via a remote Jev System One API.

name: spring-ai-model-router
description: A Spring Boot app that asks Jev via the Spring AI TypeSafe starter to classify each prompt into one of four capability tiers (luna to astra), then routes it to the cheapest sufficient OpenAI model and returns the answer with the routing decision and confidence.

name: jev-review
description: jev-review splits a diff into per-file chunks, triages each through Jev via the Vercel AI Gateway, and emits a JSON report — full diffs for flagged files, one-line verdicts for clean ones — so review agents spend tokens only on risky changes.

name: jevtown
description: Jevtown simulates a 10,000-persona social network that reacts to your post, listing, product, or headline in seconds—showing who scrolled past, liked, or got annoyed, what buyers would ask or pay, and why—so you can test variants before publishing via web, CLI, or MCP.

name: reaper
description: Reaper is a CLI semantic linter for coding agents that checks Git diffs or codebases and emits deterministic text/JSON diagnostics for semantic problems ordinary linters miss, like narrating comments, shallow abstractions, silent fallbacks, weakened assertions, and scope creep.

name: jev-rogue
description: jev-rogue is a top-down action roguelike where TypeSafe's Jev choice model directs each run—returning probability distributions over code-enumerated legal options for rooms, encounters, and rewards based on player context—while deterministic seeded generators build, validate, and simulate the playable result.

name: seems-lang
description: Seems is a Python superset language where `if` conditions can be plain-English judgments answered by the TypeSafe Jev API, with three-valued yes/no/unsure logic, lazy batched requests, caching, and line-preserving translation to ordinary Python.

name: kev-browser-use
description: A 0.6B decision model fine-tuned from Kev-0.6B that reads a goal plus candidate page elements and returns, in one forward pass, which element to act on and whether to click, type, or select — 32.2% Mind2Web step success at 80 ms per decision, runnable in-browser on WebGPU.

name: ai-hedge-fund
description: Educational CLI (`aihf`) simulating an AI hedge fund: define mandates of LLM investor agents and strategies, run simulated trading cycles over chosen tickers, and backtest equity curves with anonymized prompts that curb model recall—no real trades.

name: jev-notion
description: jev-notion is a macOS SwiftUI app and CLI that fills Notion database properties with calibrated AI judgments, detecting row edits in ≤2s at ~$0.00004/row, routing uncertain entries to a review queue, with 8-language UI and Keychain-secured credentials.

name: dotpals
description: dotpals is a floating desktop companion that watches coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, reporting in plain language which files changed, which commands ran and their results, whether tests cover the latest edits, and what needs approval, via a pal, notch, and dashboard.

name: purelink
description: A browser extension that scores LinkedIn posts for AI authorship using a lightweight decision model answering 17 weighted questions instead of an LLM, flags engagement/curiosity/rage bait, and offers an on-demand fact-checker that annotates claims in place with sourced verdicts.

name: dspy-system-one-agent-patterns
description: A six-file progressive tutorial for building a sandboxed DSPy coding agent, showing how Jev probabilities and Python thresholds add permission gates, ranked tools, history filtering, delegation, and measurable comparisons to a baseline.

name: jev-shogi
description: jev-shogi makes TypeSafe's judgment-only Jev model play shogi by passing all legal moves as probability-scored choices in one inference (no search engine), and ships v2/v3 lookahead variants, Fairy-Stockfish match results, KIF/mp4 game records, and calibration and replay-rendering scripts.

name: skillranker
description: SkillRanker is a standalone Rust CLI that uses TypeSafe.ai’s Jev to evaluate live agent context against available skills, recommend the most suitable next-step procedure, abstain when none fits, and provide inspectable explanations, safeguards, and local feedback.

name: tavily-jev-public
description: A local React/FastAPI competitor-monitoring app that uses Tavily to fetch recent news, product, and pricing pages for up to five competitors, then has jev classify each source against your company context as Alert, Watch, or Ignore with confidence scores.

name: jevis
description: Jevis is a Dart package for Flutter's integration_test framework that uses TypeSafe's Jev model to drive UI tests: you register available actions, state a goal and action budget, and the model observes the current screen, picks the next action, and evaluates whether the goal is reached.

name: typesafe-sdk-go
description: A zero-dependency Go client for the TypeSafe AI API that returns statically-typed answers (probabilities, classifications, rubric scores) to named questions in one request, with pre-network validation, typed errors, retries, and per-call overrides.

name: jevc
description: jevc compiles natural-language rules from agent instruction files into typed questions scored by a non-generative probability model plus a code reducer, turning prose agents may ignore into testable, diffable gates for hooks, routers, and verifiers.

name: JevNQL
description: JevNQL compiles natural-language data questions into typed JevIR plans that route deterministic arithmetic to Apache DataFusion and only meaning judgments to the Jev semantic model, ordering filters and top-k first so minimal rows reach costly model calls, cutting token cost.

name: jev-decision-layer
description: An open-source MCP decision layer that routes bounded agent choices through TypeSafe Jev or optional local Laya-MLX, applying reusable recipes, workspace controls, local act/verify/ignore gating, receipts, host adapters, and offline fixtures while preserving host execution authority.

name: jev-chatbot
description: An experimental chatbot harness that turns TypeSafe’s non-generative Jev choice model into a next-word or reply selector over 30k words, with browser and Node CLI interfaces, seven comparison modes, cached embedding-built trees, and measured speed, cost, and quality tradeoffs.

name: jevc
description: jevc is a Rust CLI that pipes JSON stdin to the JEV semantic-judgment API and returns JSON—supporting noul probability, choice, and score questions with local validation, sequential JSONL batching, self-describing schemas, stable error codes, and distinct exit statuses for coding agents and shell pipelines.

name: jev-llm-guard
description: A contextual LLM guardrail SDK, CLI, and demo server that sends text (user input, retrieved content, tool or model output) to the Jev API and returns versioned allow/review/block decisions with OWASP LLM Top-10 risk signals for routing unsafe content.

name: notiq
description: Notiq is a native Android 10+ notification filter that routes selected apps' notifications to a configured Jev or self-hosted FastJev LLM service, removing promotions based on plain-language per-app rules while offering observe mode, local decision history, and fallback reminders for uncertain results.

name: TypeAR
description: TypeAR is a constrained-decoding client for SGLang-served open autoregressive LLMs that yields type-safe outputs (single-token enum/boolean choices, bounded numeric values, free text) via sequential or prefix-cached batch execution, with optional thinking, sampling, and per-choice probabilities.

name: is-odd-jev
description: A zero-dependency Node.js library and CLI that checks whether a number is odd by querying the Jev "System One" model (via TypeSafe API or Vercel AI Gateway), returning the model's calibrated probability rather than a parsed string so callers can threshold confidence and escalate uncertain cases.

name: jev-for-all
description: jev-for-all wires TypeSafe's ~500 ms Jev decision model into OpenCode, Claude Code, Hermes, and pi via one shared contract, picking which skill to load, which tool subset each step needs, and every browser_task move at ~$0.0001 per decision with fail-open fallbacks.

name: jev-router
description: An open-source LiteLLM-based proxy that exposes an OpenAI-compatible `jev-router` model id and routes each request to an eligible pool model—filtered by vision, tool, and output-length requirements—using TypeSafe's Jev model when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set or a local cheapest-eligible fallback otherwise.

name: jev-collusion-monitor
description: A black-box monitoring tool that uses the Jev model to detect secretly colluding AI agents from public meeting transcripts alone—scoring AUROC 0.82 on NARCBench Transfer (vs 0.88 white-box probes) at ~$0.002/meeting—plus frozen question configs, baselines, reports, and reproduction scripts.

name: book-aurora
description: Book Aurora converts a plain-text novel into an "emotional weather" poster by sending each ~90-word passage to the Jev decision model for calibrated 0–3 scores across nine emotions, then rendering every passage as a feathered row of colour curtains.

name: openjev
description: OpenJev answers typed questions—an N-way choice, an ordered-rubric score, or a P(true) gate—about a state in one shared forward pass, returning calibrated probabilities from a self-trainable Qwen3-1.7B LoRA adapter or ModernBERT encoder with no text generation.

name: Armada
description: Armada is a control plane for orchestrating AI coding captains across git repositories with isolated worktrees, durable mission records, gated pipelines, tiered routing, and REST/MCP/WebSocket access to dispatch, monitor, review, and land parallel work.

name: jevkit
description: jevkit is a zero-dependency Python policy and evaluation framework for Jev/Kev System One decision models that compiles labeled data into evidence-bearing threshold lock files, maps typed probabilities to actions via declarative gates, and provides CLI tools for calibration, coverage analysis, permutation stability testing, and drift detection.

name: opencode-fast-jev-compaction
description: An opencode plugin that replaces lossy LLM-summary context compaction with Jev scoring: once session context occupancy crosses a configurable threshold, every tool call and result is individually kept verbatim, truncated, or deleted based on scored relevance.

name: pi-pair-programmer
description: A Pi/OMP extension that runs specialized background code reviewers after each write or edit, filters duplicate and inherited findings via a Jev filter, and requires the agent to accept or reject each finding before continuing.

name: onesie
description: onesie is a CLI that pipes text to TypeSafe Jev, OpenRouter, or Berget models to return scriptable yes/no probabilities, option picks, or scale ratings, enabling shell-command gates, batch triage, labeled-data calibration, caching, mocks, and CI assertions.

name: typesafe-sdk-js
description: JavaScript/TypeScript SDK for TypeSafe AI that provides a `TypeSafeClient` for sending state and structured questions (e.g., `choice`) to `systemOne` and receiving type-inferred answers, distributed as ESM, CommonJS, and TypeScript declarations for Node.js 20+.

name: typesafe-sdk-ruby
description: An unofficial Ruby SDK for the TypeSafe AI API that evaluates state against noul, choice, and score questions, returning typed answers with probabilities and confidence, with retries, timeouts, cancellation, and an error hierarchy for classification, ranking, and routing.

name: osso
description: Osso is a Chrome extension that sends every sentence of a page to the Jev yes/no model and strikes out the filler—still readable, never hidden—while you read, with Shift to restore, a strictness slider, keep/highlight rules, and per-site privacy controls.

name: jev-reflex
description: jev-reflex is a macOS interaction engine that combines local MediaPipe hand tracking, offline Vosk partial speech, and window geometry with confidence-gated Jev typed decisions via OpenRouter to target, snap, resize, and control windows through gestures and voice, visualized on a token-authenticated Next.js dashboard.

name: jev-chat-JARVIS-windows
description: A Windows overlay tool that captures your own WeChat 4.x window, reads conversations via local offline OCR, generates three intent/emotion-scored reply drafts ranked by a Jev judgment model, and pastes a chosen suggestion into the input box—sending always stays manual.

name: jev-tetris
description: A Node.js web app where TypeSafe's Jev model autonomously plays Tetris: each piece's reachable placements are enumerated with board metrics (lines cleared, holes, height, bumpiness), sent to Jev as a typed Choice question, and the picked move is animated with probabilities, confidence, latency, and API cost.

name: jev-weekend-shopping-chrome
description: A Chrome extension (v0.4.6, Chrome 137+, MIT, unpacked install) that overlays a "PASS" stamp on Taobao and JD.com product images whose items, shops, or brands are AI-guessed via a user-supplied TypeSafe API key to lack two-day weekends, with an on/off toggle and live stats.

name: jev-bench
description: jev-bench is a 42-claim benchmark that tests whether a cited passage actually supports a sentence as written, comparing a typed-answer model against frontier LLMs on accuracy, calibration, cost, and risk/coverage, with reproducible code, raw outputs, and pre-registered decision rules.

name: metis
description: Metis is a dependency-free Python 3.10+ library, CLI, and GitHub Action that uses TypeSafe’s Jev model to triage new GitHub issues, apply confident labels, request missing details, and safely skip uncertain or changed cases.

name: jev-luna-photo-lab
description: A self-hostable Node.js photo lab where Jev and GPT-5.6 Luna each translate a text "look" prompt plus aggregate image statistics into settings for the same local browser-worker renderer (exposure, white balance, curves, HSL, grading, grain, diffusion), enabling side-by-side model comparison via an animated before/after divider, while a SQLite budget ledger enforces per-model lifetime spending caps

name: jev-search
description: A self-hostable Cloudflare Workers app that turns plain-language requests into Search1API queries across web and vertical engines, then streams Jev-scored, URL-merged links and snippets with visible relevance, editable source/time filters, caching, and per-IP rate limits.

name: betterfeed
description: A Chrome Manifest V3 extension that automatically masks unwanted posts in your LinkedIn feed, collapsing them into labelled bars via TypeSafe's Jev model running on Cloudflare Workers AI, with filtering preferences configurable from the extension's settings page.

name: magi-system-on-jev
description: A web app recreating Neon Genesis Evangelion's MAGI system using TypeSafe AI's Jev "System One" model, where three independent sage agents evaluate a question and reach a verdict via majority vote over calibrated probabilities, with a live CloudFront deployment and bilingual docs.

name: furu-agent-bar
description: FlashBar AI is an open-source Salesforce Lightning `Cmd+K` command palette that enables natural-language, SOQL-free search, relational filtering, inline mass editing, CSV import, and AI-powered case triage and lead scoring via a stateless Cloudflare Workers JEV architecture delivering sub-400ms responses with FLS and sharing rules enforced.

name: typesafe-mod
description: A Claude Code function hook that routes AskUserQuestion dialogs and per-prompt skill ranking to TypeSafe's Jev model, returning typed answers with probabilities and confidence scores so the agent can advise, auto-answer, or inject skill hints while failing open on any error.

name: jev-touhou
description: A two-layer control stack that lets self-hosted Jev-pattern typed-decision models (Laya or Mica, HTTP question-answering engines, no text generation) play the open-source Touhou game Taisei: a patched headless sim layer exposes frame-exact seeded gameplay via a C API, a Python harness compiles game state into ~300-token snapshots and batches choice/score/boolean questions at ~3 Hz, and a 60 Hz ref

name: jev-firewall
description: jev-firewall is a tiny JavaScript coding-agent experiment that places TypeSafe AI’s Jev between a bounded tool loop and OpenAI, letting typed confidence thresholds handle routine actions, escalate generation or uncertainty, and produce comparable metrics on avoidable frontier-model calls.

name: youtube-focus
description: YouTube Focus is a Chrome extension that dims or hides YouTube homepage and watch-page recommendations that don't match a free-text description of your interests, using TypeSafe AI's Jev model with your own API key, adjustable visibility controls, and local API-usage tracking.

name: distill
description: Distill is a lightweight coding agent harness and TUI that cuts token costs by routing work across configurable Worker, Reasoning, and Utility model tiers, working with Grok and Codex subscriptions and any OpenAI-compatible model.

name: magic-8-ball
description: A Vite/TypeScript Magic 8 Ball whose Cloudflare Worker relays each question to TypeSafe's `systemone` Choice API, letting `jev-latest` pick one of twenty witty replies rendered in a CSS-only ball with true latency timing, rate limiting, and deploy tooling.

name: jev-rs
description: jev-rs is an async-first Rust SDK for the TypeSafe AI API that provides a typed System One question builder (Noul, Choice, Score), model discovery, configurable retries and timeouts, structured errors with raw-response diagnostics and tracing, and an optional blocking client.

name: autojev
description: AutoJev-27B is a Qwen3.8-27B–based multimodal decision model that returns calibrated probabilities over supplied choices in one forward pass per question, served via a TypeSafe-compatible API and browser playground, achieving 84.60% accuracy with lower ECE and Brier scores than its base model.

name: jev-risk-check-provider
description: An x402 risk-check provider that evaluates agent payment counterparties with Jev’s typed parallel risk questions, applies deterministic composite scoring and caps, and returns fail-closed ES256-signed attestations verifiable via JWKS without trusting the provider.

name: duckdb-jev
description: A DuckDB extension that lets SQL queries filter, rank, and classify table rows with natural-language conditions judged by TypeSafe's Jev model, which returns calibrated probabilities through batched, concurrent, cached API calls — no embeddings or indexes needed.

name: jev-audit
description: jev-audit is a zero-dependency, fully local CLI that scans a codebase for LLM call sites, flags those that are really decisions (classify, route, score, verify), and—via an installable agent skill—produces a JEV_AUDIT.md report tiering each call as Replace, Hybrid, Keep LLM, or Pure code with savings math, draft Jev question JSON, and a migration plan to TypeSafe AI's System One model.

name: jevlogs
description: jevlogs is a Node.js 22+ tool that runs a local OpenTelemetry HTTP/JSON log receiver which scores each OTLP log record for diagnostic value, priority, and actionable probability using TypeSafe's Jev via the Vercel AI SDK, annotating records with `jev.*` attributes or routing low-value events away from expensive LLM analysis while preserving your existing archive pipeline.

name: WorkflowEvals
description: A Python/uv toolkit for reproducing workflow evals: it benchmarks models from multiple LLM providers against reference-labeled cases across four workflows, supports resumable runs and custom references, reports per-case cost and time metrics, and generates comparison plots including published Hugging Face runs.

name: jevcal
description: jevcal calibrates confidence thresholds for typed decision models (e.g. TypeSafe's Jev) on your own data, reports accuracy-vs-coverage and cost tradeoffs, ships a cascade runtime that escalates uncertain rows to an LLM fallback, and fails CI on drift.

name: jev-dataops
description: JEV DataOps is a traceable pipeline that uploads JSONL/CSV datasets, screens records into keep/review/reject partitions via local rules or the JEV API, trains a configured model, and reports before/after loss and perplexity via a browser workbench, CLI, and Python/HTTP APIs.

name: jev-poly-crypto-demo
description: A Bun research tool for Polymarket's BTC 5-minute Up/Down markets that fetches live market and Binance perp data, scores each round with the Jev model, executes simulated or real-wallet FOK trades under fee-aware edge and risk gates, and shows decisions on a local dashboard.

name: typesafe-ai-bot
description: A self-hosted Discord moderation bot where AI supplies rule-violation probabilities and code owns every threshold and action — with spam/anti-nuke detection, votable member reports with staff veto, explainable case logs, a local dashboard, and a watch-first default.

name: ai-day-trader-agent
description: An intraday trading assistant where Claude analyzes and trades through Robinhood MCP tools, adding a fail-closed order guard hook, Jev-scored headline judgments, a scored trade journal, an autonomous Alpaca paper news bot with bracket orders, and a live web desk for monitoring all agent activity.

name: jev-tool-router
description: A Codex MCP router that hides hundreds of external tool schemas behind a small routing surface, using Jev to select tools by capability at ≥0.90 confidence or return bounded shortlists—shrinking agent context while keeping the full inventory reachable.

name: vision-jev
description: A browser-based driving demo where Florence-2 captions images users drop on a road and TypeSafe's Jev model, called through a Cloudflare Worker, decides whether the car should stop, slow down, or continue—about 330 ms median at ~$0.00004 per decision.

name: jev-skill-gate
description: jev-skill-gate is a Node 18+ CLI that installs a SessionStart hook for Claude Code which scores installed skills against project signals using TypeSafe's Jev decision model (or a free local TF-IDF scorer), then writes skillOverrides to demote irrelevant skills to name-only or hidden states—cutting skill manifest tokens by ~75% for roughly $0.0005 per session while never writing `off`.

name: jev-router.nvim
description: A Neovim plugin that uses Jev via OpenRouter’s Decisions API to route natural-language prompts to native file-opening, code-editing, command-running, or contextual-question workflows—with previews, fallbacks, conversation context, and swappable backends—so intent becomes safe editor action.

name: jev-heuristic-adapter
description: A Python adapter that compiles fixed decision questions into reusable LLM-generated heuristic programs upfront, then executes them locally for new input states — replacing repeated remote inference with microsecond-to-millisecond local rule evaluation.

name: postlens
description: PostLens is a Next.js tool that evaluates LinkedIn drafts against an explicit eight-dimension rubric via Jev judgment and deterministic scoring, compares draft versions, and generates verified OpenAI rewrites—without storing drafts or claiming to predict virality.

name: SwiftJev
description: SwiftJev is a thin SwiftDecision `DecisionBackend` adapter for the hosted System One API, sending typed Noul, Choice, and Score prompts and returning validated probability distributions with injectable HTTP transport, cancellation, order preservation, and credential-safe errors.

name: jev-readability
description: An ESM/TypeScript library for AI agents that partitions a rendered webpage's DOM, uses TypeSafe JEV (or an offline heuristic) to select semantically relevant blocks across documentation, forums, products, and listings, and reconstructs the chosen content as Markdown, text, or HTML from the original source—favoring high recall over Mozilla Readability's article-only precision at the cost of API l

name: Jev-cu
description: Jev-cu is an installable Codex skill plus scripts that delegate Computer Use's next-step choice to Jev, which selects element, action, completion, and risk from text-only UI candidates while Codex executes, behind a dry-run-first local policy gate requiring human confirmation for sensitive operations.

name: jev
description: Jevrb is a synchronous Ruby client (gem) for the TypeSafe System One API that sends content with typed questions (Noul, Choice, Score) and returns immutable typed answer objects with probabilities, confidence, and usage, offering configurable retries, timeouts, error classes, and RBS type signatures.

name: jev-piano
description: jev-piano turns a mood description into improvised piano music by asking a model that only answers questions with probabilities—per bar, about harmony, melody, texture and form—then sampling its distributions, so key choice, cadences and the ending are its decisions.

name: who-is-right
description: A live party demo that streams microphone audio over a secure WebSocket to Gemini Live, which transcribes arguments, extracts checkable claims, and moves a gauge via a fast classifier call per claim — entertainment-grade fact-checking with capped session and API-usage limits and no audio recording.

name: jev-ultrafast
description: A browser agent whose dynamic, indexed action space lets TypeSafe's Jev pick an operation and compatible DOM target in one speculative request per cycle, with a small LLM generating text only for TYPE_TEXT—completing a verified Google Flights search in 7.1 seconds.

name: typesafe-ai-ruby
description: A dependency-free Ruby client for the TypeSafe System One API that sends state plus typed questions (yes/no Nouls, multi-option Choices, ordinal Scores) to the Jev model and returns structured answers with probabilities and confidence scores, plus retries, instrumentation, and per-call configuration.

name: jev-effort
description: jev-effort is a local proxy that wraps Claude Code (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) so the small Jev decision model picks per-step reasoning effort via cache-safe effort-only system messages, and it quantifies the savings: −55% cost on a `max`-effort benchmark, ~1% at `high`, and a measured 4–9% in real long sessions where context re-reads dominate.

name: jev-x-kit
description: jev-x-kit is a TypeScript toolkit (Claude Code plugin, MCP server, CLI) giving agents a non-autoregressive decision layer — Choice/Score/Noul primitives, confidence gating, speculative fan-out, lossless compaction, red-teaming, RLVR memory — that runs free and fully offline.

name: lcc
description: lcc is a local-first CLI and Python/TypeScript library that deterministically optimizes LLM context—cleaning boilerplate, deduplicating, counting exact tokens, and relevance-compacting without summarizing—plus prompt intake triage, on-device LLM agents, and an MCP server.

name: cairn-jev-lab
description: An experimental, dependency-free Node.js tool that judges whether a proposed memory is faithfully supported by a source passage, scoring support, durability, and commitment via three typed AI judgments plus a versioned policy recommending save, skip, or defer with inspectable reports.

name: jev-sdk-java
description: A type-safe Java 21 client for the TypeSafe AI Jev decision API that models noul, choice, and score questions as records and sealed interfaces, moving malformed request shapes to compile time and returning calibrated probabilities as ordered, exhaustive answers.

name: jevry
description: Jevry is an open-source Electron desktop browser that turns natural-language tasks into typed actions chosen by TypeSafe's Jev model from observed page controls, with a text/vision model planning and deterministic code validating, executing, and recording each guarded step.

name: typesafe-chess
description: typesafe-chess is a Node.js/React demo where two instances of TypeSafe's Jev model play chess by answering typed Choice/Score/Noul questions—returning full probability distributions over legal moves generated by chess.js—optionally deepened by an AlphaZero-style MCTS using those distributions as policy and value, with code-side tactical facts and Stockfish-based benchmarking.

name: vector-graph-rag
description: Vector Graph RAG is a Python library that builds knowledge-graph RAG indexes by extracting triplets, embedding entities and relations in Milvus, and answering multi-hop queries through subgraph expansion plus single-pass LLM reranking—without a graph database.

name: jevscan
description: jevscan is a CLI, library, and MCP server that turns an EVM token contract address into typed `ape / watch / avoid` verdicts with calibrated probabilities plus `rug_risk`, `momentum`, `liquidity_health`, and `fdv_stress` scores — deterministic local engine by default, swappable to the TypeSafe jev endpoint with an API key, and grep-style exit codes make it a pipeable gate for buy scripts and scr

name: jev-hft-model-router
description: Confidence-gated router that maps a natural-language trading request, market state, and constraints to a typed selection or abstention from up to 254 user-registered strategy model cards, with deterministic filtering, fresh-data gates, evaluation tooling, and no execution.

name: codeloom.engine
description: A headless AI coding-agent backend that runs as a long-lived process per workspace, exposing an NDJSON protocol over a Unix socket so any client can drive LLM agents with tree-sitter and LSP-powered code tools, all writes funneled through staleness checks, syntax gating, atomic replaces, and undoable journaling.

name: effective-jev
description: Effect-based TypeScript SDK for the TypeSafe Jev API that asks choice, yes/no-probability, and scored-level questions over arbitrary state and returns fully typed, validated answers with configurable retries, timeouts, cancellation, and error handling on Node.js or Deno.

name: jev-and-cartesia-experiment
description: Hands-on tutorial running three Python demos that show when a voice agent should use the Jev decision model over an LLM—detecting caller intent mid-speech, replacing IVR menus, and benchmarking Jev vs Claude Sonnet 5 on 150 calls for speed, accuracy, and cost.

name: jev-benchmarks
description: Benchmark suite evaluating Jev 1.13.0 zero-shot inference via the TypeSafe API against frozen supervised checkpoints and a local NLI baseline on five pinned benchmarks (BANKING77, CLINC150, HWU64, SST-2, STS-B), with resumable runs and paired-bootstrap comparisons.

name: free-mac-voice
description: Free, fully on-device voice control for macOS Apple Silicon that routes whisper.cpp speech through a four-tier regex→decision-model→VLM→Gemini pipeline to open apps, tile windows, click UI via OCR, dictate text, control Samsung TVs, and answer questions — privately and near-instantly.

name: jev-decision-bench
description: A self-hosted, reproducible benchmark toolkit that evaluates conventional LLMs against TypeSafe JEV's bounded-decision interfaces (Noul, Choice, Score) on identical states, rubrics, and answer spaces, reporting accuracy, token usage, latency, and reliability for fair comparison.

name: system-one-on-snapdragon
description: A pinned, reproducible snapshot of scripts, Jev-compatible servers, and a benchmark harness for running System One typed-decision models (Laya on Hexagon NPU/Adreno GPU, Decider via llama.cpp, imajev via PyTorch) natively on Windows ARM64 Snapdragon X Elite hardware, with measured latency, accuracy findings, and upstream fix notes.

name: cancerjev
description: CancerJev is a research-only platform that runs deterministic, provenance-tracked analyses over open public cancer data, gating AI-proposed hypotheses and follow-up tests behind verified evidence while refusing any restricted or authenticated patient data.

name: graphlin
description: Graphlin renders live architecture diagrams of your repo while Claude Code or Codex explores and edits it—highlighting file reads and writes across Blocks, Code, C4, Changes, and Activity views—with fully local parsing for JS, TS, TSX, and Python.

name: security-sandbox-jev
description: security-sandbox-jev is a sandboxed testbed that puts a policy-enforcing gateway between AI agents and a fake 50-person company's API, using the Jev classifier to score every action (allow/block/hold) based on agent identity, verified initiator, and planted adversarial traps, with audit logging and a live bench UI.

name: dsh-plugin-jev-effort-selector
description: A DSH plugin that queries the lightweight Jev classifier—given a compact envelope of the previous turn's facts—to choose each message's reasoning effort once per turn, rewriting the model call, anchoring unfinished continued work, and degrading silently on failure.

name: jev_benchmark
description: A benchmark comparing the Jev routing model with open-source alternatives on 100 multi-turn enterprise RAG agent cases, scoring each turn's route, scope-change, mode, and restriction decisions plus latency to reveal accuracy and predictability tradeoffs.

name: jev-tool-search
description: A benchmark and experimental search engine for picking the right tool for an LLM agent, comparing BM25, embeddings, rerankers, and Jev on real MCP tool catalogs, with runnable runners, datasets, metrics, and research notes.

name: jevspin
description: Browser app that visualizes TypeSafe's Jev judgment model solving a Rubik's cube through menu-based choices, offering guided and discovery modes, a random-picker control, benchmark script, keyless mock backend, and Cloudflare Workers deployment.

name: laravel-jev-memory-ai
description: Jev Memory gives Laravel apps a durable conversation-context layer — idempotent raw turns, versioned auditable thread state, explicit pending actions, compacted history, scoped long-term memory, and budgeted context envelopes — so short replies like "Yes" resolve safely against authoritative application state.

name: jev-column-race
description: A zero-dependency Node.js live benchmark racing TypeSafe's Jev (80 typed questions per request) against Gemini 3.8 Flash over 1,000 real app reviews, reporting per-request latency, cost, and label agreement, with replayable recorded runs and instant client-side re-ranking.

name: jev-phishing-bench
description: A reproducible benchmark that pits Jev against Claude Haiku 4.5 on 2,000 PhishNChips emails for the click/no-click decision, measuring accuracy, AUROC, calibration, latency, cost, probability stability, and signal-decomposition controls with confidence intervals and paired statistical tests.

name: WindTunnel
description: WindTunnel is a benchmark harness that runs identical seeded tasks on self-hosted real web apps, comparing WebMCP against screenshot, DOM/accessibility-tree, and code-execution interfaces for browser agents via outcome-based scoring of success, time, tokens, and cost.

name: jev-lint
description: jev-lint is a Python CLI that audits Markdown knowledge bases for contradictions, stale claims, unresolved markers, and dangling wikilinks via local checks plus TypeSafe Jev semantic scoring, with budget caps, caching, and a self-contained HTML evidence report.

name: ghosthands
description: ghosthands is a USB-HID computer-control stack that uses a fast element-table decision model or vision/grounding models to observe any screen and drive a real mouse and keyboard, enabling undetectable, DOM-independent automation of web and native apps for pennies.

name: jev-bias-bench
description: A Laravel + Vue benchmark that tests whether the Jev model decides the same case differently when only a person's identity attribute changes, using counterfactual pairs, measured model noise, and negative controls across ten real-world decision scenarios.

name: muse-jev-playbook
description: Playbook for using TypeSafe AI's Jev as a cheap, fast decision layer in AI agent workflows: typed choice/score/noul questions with confidence-based policy, recipes, and a drop-in skill to triage and gate work before costly steps like research or subagents.

name: lossless-rewrite
description: Lossless Rewrite lets you flag details that must survive a rewrite—exact wording, preserved meaning, or extracted key ideas—then has your LLM summarize or restyle the document while it checks the output for omissions and repairs them via a local editor, CLI, or browser extension.

name: in-other-words
description: A Chrome extension that uses TypeSafe’s Jev model to detect verbose LinkedIn posts, cross them out in red pen, and overlay the single plain sentence they are actually saying—naming companies or amounts when present—while sparing substantive, uncertain, grief, or illness posts and letting you reveal originals.

name: hono-jev-router
description: An experimental router for Hono that replaces method-and-path matching with plain-language descriptions: it sends each request's method, URL, headers, and truncated body to TypeSafe's Jev model, evaluates all descriptions in parallel, and runs the first handler whose match probability reaches a configurable threshold.

name: jev-gem-scan
description: An offline, stdlib-only Python CLI that simulates token launches and scores each `GEM` or `RUG` through a mocked decision model behind a policy gate, with shadow/active modes, seeded determinism, and JSONL logging — useful for demoing and reviewing a decision-model routing workflow with zero real trades, keys, or network calls.

name: jev-vpn
description: Jev-VPN is a Windows privacy proxy that blocks ads, trackers, telemetry, and malvertising at the socket layer using static blocklists and AI domain triage, with one-click system-wide routing, an encrypted tunnel, and GUI/CLI live metrics.

name: ddskk-jev
description: An Emacs global minor mode that reranks ddskk Japanese conversion candidates by sending surrounding context, reading, and okurigana to TypeSafe AI's Jev evaluation model (via Vercel AI Gateway or the direct TypeSafe API) and ordering candidates by their returned probabilities.

name: reflex
description: Reflex is a Rust library for building constraint-enforcing control loops that turns observability data (e.g., Datadog metrics, Toto forecasts) into typed state, lets a judge (AI model or algorithm) recommend actions, and commits only transitions that pass declared guards and invariants—useful for circuit breaking, autoscaling, scheduling, and retries.

name: jev-sentinel
description: A per-action monitor for AI coding agents that hooks Claude Code or Codex and scores every proposed tool call against the project's one-sentence task scope—allow, ask a human, or block with a reason—while also screening tool results for prompt injection, tracking session drift, and caching verdicts.

name: ironbee-express
description: IronBee Express is a goal-driven browser agent that executes one-sentence tasks in a real browser via single TypeSafe Jev decisions over indexed page controls—LLM-free by default at ~300 ms per step—then verifies the run against page state, API responses, console errors, and backend logs to return a pass/fail verdict with root-cause evidence, while supporting cached replay, masked secrets, hum

name: modular-agent-jev
description: Modular Agent modules that query TypeSafe AI's System One model (Jev) for structured judgements — multi-question evaluations, yes/no strength (0–1), label selection with confidence, or ordered-scale scoring — without prompt engineering or free-text parsing, with automatic retries for rate limits and timeouts.

name: jev-mermaid
description: A local Node.js demo that executes a Mermaid flowchart subset as ticket-routing logic, requesting typed Choice and Score judgments from Jev via `@typesafe-ai/sdk` and highlighting the computed route in the browser, with a fixture-backed Preview mode that works without an API key.

name: jev-torneo-animales
description: A dependency-free Python game pitting up to 2,569 animals in a winner-stays-on tournament across land, water and air arenas, with every fight decided by TypeSafe's Jev model via speculative batched calls (~7.6 ms per decision, 1,999 fights in ~16 s) in a local web UI.

name: pelican-jev
description: A Python CLI that renders an MP4 of a Logo turtle drawing a pelican on a bicycle, where Codex proposes candidate Logo command sequences each round, Jev's typed API selects among them, and every decision is saved to a resumable trace for model-free replay.

name: jev-mcp
description: A Rust stdio MCP server exposing TypeSafe AI's Jev judgment model to Codex via four tools (noul, choice, score, batch) that return typed answers with probabilities and deterministic accept/verify/reevaluate policies for classification, selection, and scoring.

name: typesafe-sdk-java
description: A community Java 17+ client for the TypeSafe System One API that sends typed questions (noul, choice, score) over application state and returns calibrated probabilities in one round trip, with async, retries, Spring Boot support, and minimal dependencies.

name: guard-jev
description: Moderation demo whose POST /api/moderate runs one TypeSafe `systemOne` call scoring 7 Noul hazards plus a severity Score in parallel, then applies tunable strict/permissive policy thresholds, IP rate limits, and a keyword-heuristic mock fallback without TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

name: jev-word-lab
description: A local app that makes TypeSafe's jev-latest model converse by picking each word from an 87,776-word WordNet dictionary via real API calls, with a 36-dimension category map, resumable scans, live request monitoring, repetition filtering, and exports.

name: jev-lite
description: Jev-Lite is a FastAPI/PyTorch decision engine that resolves typed choice, score, and true/false questions against shared context in one non-autoregressive forward pass—returning calibrated probabilities in ~15–45 ms with zero output tokens or JSON parsing.

name: jev-engineering
description: A technical review and implementation framework for embedding Jev's typed decisions into agent workflows—separating observation, judgment, policy, action, and verification—with a 34-page paper, diagrams, recipes, an offline claim-checking demo, and a reusable integration prompt.

name: Caret
description: Caret is a native macOS assistant that offers Tab-accepted inline text completions and previewable action proposals — routed by a two-step judge (ABSTAIN/INLINE/ACTION, then workflow selection) over focused-field, clipboard, and Screenpipe history context — via a Python core bridge, requiring explicit user acceptance before any workflow executes.

name: hn-jev
description: A framework-free Chrome MV3 extension that uses TypeSafe's jev-latest model to score Hacker News stories on five factors—relevance, depth, durability, primary-source likelihood, and hype—then displays and sorts them inline with tunable weights and 14-day local caching.

name: openpoke-meets-jev
description: An OpenPoke fork that routes yes/no decisions—email triage, tool-call guardrails, search relevance—to TypeSafe's Jev model for batched calibrated probabilities, cutting per-decision latency ~6x and cost ~95x, while quarantining injected mail instead of silently dropping it.

name: cyber-breach-jev
description: A Three.js infinite 3D Tron arena shooter where TypeSafe AI's Jev sub-100ms decision model (Choice/Score/Noul primitives) powers tactical enemy AI, an adaptive encounter director, and a Doom-style autopilot bot, with a Cua-browser pipeline for autonomous build verification.

name: pg_jevplanner
description: A PostgreSQL extension that delegates join-order selection to the Jev model by exposing query SQL, block-local relations, join predicates, equivalence classes, and row estimates at `make_join_rel()`, enabling learned join ordering that can outperform the native planner.

name: jev-watch
description: jev-watch is a Node.js CLI that catches silent behavioral drift in TypeSafe's Jev model by replaying committed baseline test cases—choice and score questions with tolerance-based confidence checks—against the live API directly or via OpenRouter, exiting nonzero so CI flags changed answers before they reach users.

name: jev-agent-tools
description: TypeScript library whose `ask()` picks a Jev carrier (TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Vercel, or an injected transport) from env credentials, sends typed questions, and validates replies fail-closed before returning a never-throwing ok/error result.

name: typesafe-go
description: typesafe-go is an unofficial, dependency-free Go SDK (go 1.22+) for the typesafe AI API that evaluates text against typed choice/score/noul questions via `SystemOne` and lists models, offering configurable timeouts, retries, per-call options, typed answers with confidence scores, and structured `APIError` handling.

name: citation-verifier
description: A privacy-first browser tool that verifies whether cited papers actually support the sentences citing them: it extracts references from uploaded manuscripts, fetches each paper via PubMed/OpenAlex, uses Claude and TypeSafe's Jev model to propose verifiable verdicts with verbatim passages, and lets reviewers record accept/reject decisions — with no server-side storage of content.

name: hippo-memory
description: hippo-memory is a zero-dependency, SQLite-backed memory layer for AI agents: provenance-tagged memories that decay unless retrieved, imports from ChatGPT/Claude/Cursor/Slack, portability across MCP-compatible agents, and sleep-time consolidation so lessons stick and mistakes aren't repeated.

name: jevthoven
description: Jevthoven is a prompt-first symbolic-music studio: a natural-language prompt becomes an editable multitrack composition via sequential TypeSafe Jev decisions, with piano-roll editing, plain-English revisions, resumable jobs, Tone.js playback, and MIDI/JSON export.

name: jev-snake
description: A Snake benchmark environment where a deterministic Python game engine enforces rules while TypeSafe AI's Jev selects each move from structured state, with browser and pygame clients, seeded reproducible runs, logged latency/confidence/fallbacks, and comparable human baselines across versioned difficulty presets.

name: jev-webmcp-extension
description: A Chrome extension whose side panel uses TypeSafe's Jev System One model to convert a page's WebMCP tool schemas into typed questions, predicting tool calls with confidence and latency from user input, gated by per-site access and execution confirmations.

name: hatebu-veil
description: A Chrome extension that scores Hatena Bookmark entry-page comments for aggressiveness and usefulness (0–5) via the Jev-powered OpenCode Zen API and auto-folds them per a configurable 6×6 matrix, with cached scores, manual hiding, and fold-history views for tuning filters.

name: jev-chat-for-twitch
description: A Chrome extension that adds a second column beside Twitch chat, using your own TypeSafe key to LLM-filter live messages by chosen intent (Helpful, Questions, Funny, Feedback, or meaningful), showing unmodified messages with probability scores and a configurable hourly spend cap.

name: mina-terrarium
description: Mina's Terrarium is a Dockerized simulation of an artificial person whose unscripted daily life is driven by a two-system loop—TypeSafe Jev ticks every second to accumulate typed "feelings" (hunger, alarms, obligations), and an LLM is invoked only when a feeling crosses its threshold to decide her thoughts and actions—letting her react to time passing rather than only to prompts, at low cost,

name: system-one-security-triage
description: A reproducible 100-case recorded security-triage demo that runs TypeSafe's Jev decision model, OpenAI's Terra, and Anthropic's Opus on identical label-neutral TypeScript vulnerability evidence (injection, broken access control, SSRF) across five passes—1,500 scored decisions—and renders balanced accuracy, vulnerability recall, latency, and Brier score on a static, credential-free dashboard.

name: jev-relay
description: Jev Relay is a local-first advisory router for Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes/Jax that sends bounded decisions to a configured local model, optionally escalates important sanitized checks to hosted TypeSafe Jev, and returns responsibility to the calling assistant—never silently falling back to paid providers or executing actions.

name: fallow-verdict
description: fallow-verdict is a Node.js CLI that submits Fallow's JS/TS security findings to Jev for assessment, yielding survivor/dismissed/needs-human-review verdicts with reasons, Markdown/JSON reports, cost caps, cached reruns, and CI exit codes.

name: jev-apply
description: jev-apply is a CLI-agent skill that auto-fills hosted job application forms (Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever) from a stored résumé and posting, drafting grounded prose where permitted, leaving unsupported fields open rather than guessing, and asking only for missing facts or attestations.

name: jev-tetris
description: A dependency-free Node/browser Tetris played by a textless multiple-choice model: the engine enumerates every legal placement, describes each in prose, JEV returns per-option probabilities, and the board visualizes preference and confidence, with mock mode, tests, and benchmark controls included.

name: jev-decision-demos
description: Two local browser demos—comparing participant answers to Jev's A/B probabilities across 13 Moral Machine dilemmas and letting Jev pick the machine's final Tic Tac Toe move among minimax-legal squares—demonstrate structured `choice` answers, served via a Node.js loopback server that keeps provider API keys server-side.

name: jevtraces
description: jevtraces is an OpenTelemetry Collector trace processor that sends bounded operation metadata to Jev, caches the returned diagnostic-value, business-criticality, and keep probabilities, and annotates matching spans with those assessments—retaining every span—so tracing backends and experimental tail-sampling pipelines can leverage model-guided scoring without dropping data.

name: jev-prompt-enhancer
description: An agent skill that scores a coding-task prompt via the Jev API, iteratively tightens task, context, constraints, and expected output (default target 80/100, up to three attempts, best score kept) while preserving intent, then runs the sharpened instructions.

name: jev-dimabsa
description: Jev-dimabsa solves SemEval-2026 DimABSA Tasks 1–3 (valence/arousal scoring, aspect–opinion triplet extraction, category prediction) using Jev's Score/Choice/Noul primitives plus calibrated statistics—no text generation, fine-tuning, or GPU—achieving state-of-the-art micro RMSE.

name: jev-model-router
description: A CLI and Python library that picks the cheapest Claude model able to finish a request, combining one low-cost Jev judgment call (tier, reasoning, blast radius, ambiguity) with a pure policy of overrides and clamps, returning a routing decision without making the downstream call.

name: Forma
description: Forma is a local-first, JEV-AI-aided website and app-UI builder that turns text requests into editable multi-page designs—choosing palettes, typography, component variants, and section order—then lets you refine via canvas editing, locks, undo, and exports as standalone HTML.

name: btc-jev-signal
description: A non-trading BTC forecasting experiment that collects Kraken spot and Binance futures data at fixed UTC boundaries, has TypeSafe Jev issue probability distributions for 15m/1h/4h/day-close horizons, then scores frozen predictions against realized closes via Cloudflare Workers, D1, and a public dashboard.

name: jul
description: JuL is a local, zero-shot Python library (and CLI/HTTP server) that answers typed questions—multiple choice, yes/no, scored scales—by comparing hidden-state embedding vectors of text and option descriptions, returning calibrated probabilities in milliseconds without training, APIs, or task-specific weights.

name: claude-jev
description: A Claude Code plugin whose five MCP tools send code snippets and typed yes/no, choice, or rubric questions to the TypeSafe Jev model, giving agents a cheap probabilistic second opinion for filtering review findings, ranking hypotheses, comparing options, and triaging search hits.

name: jev-msw
description: jev-msw provides contract-aware MSW handlers that mock @typesafe-ai/sdk's Jev endpoint so tests can script deterministic choice/noul/score answers, match requests, replay failure/retry sequences, and inspect request history while the real SDK's validation and retry logic still runs.

name: jev-guardbench
description: A benchmark harness that tests whether fast System One models (hosted Jev or self-hosted Kev) can replace the LLM-as-judge in agent guardrail before/after-model callbacks, scoring F1, FPR, AUROC, ECE, and latency against Gemini/Claude judges via resumable JSONL runs and markdown reports.

name: clef-airy
description: Clef Airy Decisions API Tester is an open-source Laravel/NativePHP desktop app for macOS and Windows that sends configurable decision requests (yes/no, choice, or score questions) to Ollama System One and Jev APIs, with model selection, None/Basic/Bearer authentication, form-or-JSON editing, Easy/JSON response views, local SQLite bookmarks, and OS-encrypted credential storage.

name: jev-fraud
description: An open-source Next.js demo where Jev scores 100 real emails for fraud, sends predictions below a 95% confidence threshold to Kimi K3 for independent review, and reports accuracy and inference costs via live runs or replay.

name: jev-compactor
description: jev-compactor is an open-source TypeScript library, CLI, and MCP server that compacts AI agent context by dropping messages the Jev model rates irrelevant—keeping survivors byte-for-byte verbatim—and flagging destructive commands in the same ~300 ms pass.

name: localjev
description: LocalJev is a Bun/TypeScript server exposing a Jev-compatible `POST /v1/systemone` decision API that runs typed questions on DiffusionGemma through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. oMLX), prompting for JSON probabilities with validation, retries, normalization, and entropy-based confidence.

name: typesafe-mcp
description: `evaluate` is an MCP server (and pi extension) that lets AI agents submit state plus typed questions—boolean (`noul`), `choice`, or `score`—to TypeSafe's Jev model via the TypeSafe API or OpenRouter, returning structured JSON answers with probabilities that code can branch on, with one-command client registration, batched parallel questions, and automatic 429/529 retries.

name: Decis
description: Decis is a self-hostable server that implements TypeSafe's `/v1/systemone` API contract to serve lightweight open decision models—pluggable engines like Laya and kev that return calibrated probabilities for typed questions in one forward pass—so the official SDK works by only changing `base_url`.

name: jev-cli
description: jev-cli installs `jev` and `jev-mcp`—a CLI and stdio MCP server—that send text/JSON state to TypeSafe Jev and return machine-readable noul, choice, or score judgments, with batching, multi-provider auth, and script-friendly output for fast classification without generated prose.

name: Cmd-F
description: Cmd-F is a Chrome extension plus local Fastify backend that answers natural-language questions about the current site by finding and highlighting the original source passages rather than summarizing, keeping your AI keys on your own machine.

name: jev-drone
description: jev-drone provides a MuJoCo simulation of a camera-only autonomous drone with a small TypeSafe Jev judgment model in the loop at 2.5 Hz, useful for experimenting with vision-based autonomous flight and robotics control.

name: djev
description: A server fronting vLLM's DiffusionGemma that turns question schemas into seeded, pinned-canvas diffusion reads, returning calibrated answer distributions for yes/no, choice, and score questions with optional reasoning, dependencies, and image inputs.

name: pi-jev
description: A Pi coding-agent extension that uses TypeSafe Jev's typed probabilistic questions to gate bash/write/edit calls for destructiveness, exfiltration, scope, and impact, flag leaked secrets and classify failures in bash output, and expose typed judgements to the model via `jev_ask`.

name: perch
description: perch is a CLI for semantic code linting: `perch scan` reports defects ranked by severity and confidence, custom rules in `perch.yaml` enforce natural-language invariants per method, and `perch issues`/`check`, agent-skill setup, and CI gating support triage and verification.

name: jev-ndr
description: Jev-NDR is a Windows Blue Team NDR and DNS sentinel that monitors live sockets, maps them to processes, detects C2 beacon jitter and DGA or exfiltration domains via fast bulk triage, and can sinkhole domains or block IPs, with SOC GUI/CLI, simulator, and tests for tuning defenses.

name: blorb
description: Blorb is a single-binary CLI for experimenting with and running named AI agents defined in one blorb.json, with configurable models, executable/built-in/subagent tools, chat and scripted runs, streaming, logs, metrics, deciders, judges, and OpenAI-compatible or Ollama backends.

name: jev-reflex
description: jev-reflex is an MCP server whose `browse` tool hands an entire browser task to TypeSafe's fast System-1 model Jev — which picks each ~100 ms action from observed page elements — while Claude plans the goal, supplies the typed values, and verifies the result.

name: jev-dojo
description: A hands-on, kyu/dan-structured tutorial for learning Jev (TypeSafe AI’s System One model), with runnable Node.js examples, recorded API fixtures, tests, diagnostics, bilingual docs, and progressive chapters from first calls to production practices.

name: jev-learning-quest
description: Jev Learning Quest is a study web app where the judgment AI Jev picks one daily quest for Japan's Information Security Specialist exam prep and AI/cloud/security catch-up, scoring answers and flagging reviews, deployable on Vercel+Supabase with GitHub OAuth and RLS or locally via `npm start`.

name: jev-spring-boot-starter
description: A Spring Boot 4 starter that auto-configures TypeSafe Jev inside Spring MVC applications, wiring it together with RestClient so Jev can be used without manual setup.

name: deepeval
description: DeepEval is an open-source, Pytest-style framework for unit-testing LLM apps—agents, RAG pipelines, chatbots—via locally run LLM-as-a-judge metrics (G-Eval, hallucination, tool correctness), synthetic datasets, benchmarks, and CI/CD integration.

name: elixir-jev
description: An Elixir library for typed semantic classification and pattern matching over model judgments, offering a `semantic_case` DSL plus Choice/Noul/Score APIs backed by TypeSafe’s hosted Jev or a supervised local Laya worker, with strict validation, timeouts, bounded concurrency, retries, recording/replay, and telemetry.

name: typesafe_agent_gates
description: LangChain/Deep Agents middleware that gates an unattended coding agent's shell commands, issue triage, merge requests, status notes, and spec changes using TypeSafe's typed model judgments instead of regexes, word lists, or prompt lines.

name: jev-guard
description: jev-guard is a cross-agent PreToolUse hook (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity) that intercepts shell, file, and patch operations to enforce workspace boundaries and sensitive-file protection via a sub-1ms local fastpath plus TypeSafe AI's Jev model for semantic blast-radius/destructiveness evaluation, with enforcing and audit modes and fail-safe blocking under autonomous bypass flags.

name: looper
description: Looper is an experimental, provider-neutral evaluation harness that tests whether typed decision models improve coding-agent context selection, routing, and repair accuracy via deterministic scheduling, JSONL evidence, a bounded closed coding loop, and pluggable adapters for benchmarks like BugsInPy and SWE-bench.

name: agent-beacon
description: Open-source, local-first CLI that captures AI agent session history across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 20+ harnesses into a unified OpenTelemetry event model, turning workflows, corrections, and debugging patterns into reusable memory retrievable via MCP or Agent Skills.

name: scala-jev-sdk
description: A backend-agnostic Scala SDK for Jev that sends structured state and named noul/choice/score questions through any sttp backend, returning typed probabilities, distributions, confidence, and errors for routing, gating, ranking, and guardrails.

name: jevpilot
description: A demo simulator where the Jev LLM pilots a car Autopilot-style by selecting from compact tables of sampled paths, road boundaries, traffic, and signals, with visualization of candidate paths, collision predictions, and API payloads, runnable locally with your own key.

name: jev-wordle
description: A web app where the Jev model plays Wordle live—each turn a letter-frequency heuristic shortlists candidate words, Jev makes one choice call, and its probabilities and pick are shown before the tiles flip—with solo watch and head-to-head versus modes.

name: jevbench
description: JevBench is a benchmark and leaderboard for Jev-class decision models that return typed answers with option probabilities, combining fresh sealed decisions with public measurements to score intelligence, calibration, speed, and cost for reproducible system comparisons.

name: agent-handoff-gate
description: An experimental protocol and offline evaluation kit that checks the evidence behind a delegated worker's PASS or BLOCKED report—via schemas, examples, and a semantic evaluator contract—before issuing a review-ready packet or authorizing one bounded continuation for the lead agent.

name: jevocks
description: A Bloomberg-style terminal that retrieves live market, news, analyst, and macro evidence through five parallel Valyu searches, then uses TypeSafe AI's Jev System One evaluation model to estimate the probability a stock trades higher in 30 days, reporting category signals, sources, and timing.

name: feedkeeper
description: FeedKeeper is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension that uses AI classification via OpenRouter to filter unwanted categories of videos from YouTube's home feed and "Up next" recommendations, offering Preview, Hide (blur), and Auto remove modes—plus channel lists, custom categories, a free Shorts blocker, and privacy-preserving local processing.

name: jev-hierarchy
description: jev-hierarchy is a Python library that recursively evaluates state through a Node tree with TypeSafe Jev forced choices, propagating path mass, pruning descent by sibling-probability cutoff, optionally adding “none”, and yielding absorbed/covered mass for hierarchical scoring.

name: jeval
description: jeval is a CLI tool that measures classifier calibration against labeled decision records on disk, then recommends a cost-based confidence threshold for deciding when to automate versus escalate to a human—producing an offline HTML report, a deployable thresholds.yaml, and label-harvesting guidance without any server, database, or network calls.

name: jev-subtitle-translator
description: An open-source SRT subtitle translator with local web and CLI interfaces that uses OpenRouter LLMs to preserve cue numbers, order, and timestamps, retries missing translations, and runs deterministic checks plus Jev review to flag lines needing human inspection.

name: jev-shadow
description: A Claude Code plugin that shadows every tool call, asks TypeSafe's Jev model five hazard questions in a background hook, and reports agreement, over-refusals, latency, and token cost versus the built-in classifier so you can judge whether Jev is worth trusting for gating.

name: RoboJev
description: RoboJev is a PyBullet Panda tabletop simulation that runs an observe→choose→execute→verify→recover loop from simulator state through one bounded action interface shared by rule-based, local Qwen, and credential-gated official Jev backends for seeded, comparable evaluation.

name: system1-jev-laya-agent
description: An open-source System 1 cognitive agent harness that solves a 3D Rubik's cube in real time using local Laya ModernBERT 421M (or TypeSafe Jev) non-autoregressive inference over a strictly causal sense-decide-actuate loop with a Three.js WebGL studio, temporal memory, calibrated softmax probabilities, and full test coverage.

name: jevelry
description: jevelry is a Node.js CLI/TUI and library that asks TypeSafe’s Jev model typed questions defined in reusable jevels, returning confidence-based act/mark/fall_back decisions, logging outcomes for review, and safely running selected commands.

name: chess-jev
description: ChessJev scores chess moves by keeping legal-move generation in python-chess and ranking UCI candidates with a one-pass MiniLM or byte-level model, served through a local FastAPI app with selectable scorers and scripts to finetune on Stockfish-labeled positions.

name: dinostomp
description: dinostomp is a local-first verification layer for AI evals that audits datasets and eval pods—recomputing summaries from records—to catch leakage, biased keys, scorer defects, seed noise, and unsupported claims, emitting a scoped verdict and CI-gateable report.

name: bes-kelime-jev
description: A dependency-light Turkish chat demo where any message gets one of five fixed phrases picked by TypeSafe AI's Jev evaluation model via `experimental_evaluate`'s typed choice/score/boolean outputs—a compact example of enforcing structured output through the type system rather than prompting.

name: jev-laya-local-daemon
description: A loopback-only HTTP daemon exposing one `/v1/decide` API for typed `noul`/`choice`/`score` decisions, routing each request to either a fully offline local Laya checkpoint or the hosted Jev model (key held server-side), with health/readiness probes and port fallback.

name: jevify
description: A paste-ready agent prompt for rigorously investigating how Jev's typed decision primitives could cut LLM cost and latency, replace brittle rules, and enable new semantic-judgment capabilities in a project, producing a ranked, evidence-backed recommendation.

name: jev-cookbook
description: Fifteen tested, runnable Node.js recipes with labelled datasets and measured results for TypeSafe's Jev decision model on OpenRouter, covering tasks like support triage, dedupe, PII scanning, moderation, and Gmail labeling with typed, confidence-scored answers.

name: ThinkLess
description: ThinkLess is an open-source decision plane that answers agents' routine judgments—intent, extraction, yes/no—via rules and small calibrated models, escalating to an LLM only below tunable confidence thresholds, with per-decision traces of provider, confidence, latency, and cost.

name: jev-spec
description: jev-spec is a CLI tool that gates pre-commit hooks and CI builds by sending each Markdown spec requirement plus its implementation to TypeSafe AI's Jev model as a focused yes/no, choice, or score question, then failing with exit codes when returned probabilities breach configured thresholds to catch spec drift cheaply.

name: jev-libero
description: jev-libero is a Python CLI that controls LIBERO/robosuite robot tasks through Jev's layered intent-family-input decisions over 27 atomic controls, using reversible MuJoCo physics previews to evaluate candidates before execution, with JSON-configurable tasks and replayable run records.

name: jev-clerk
description: jev-clerk is a macOS bookkeeping agent that reads supplier invoice PDFs via screen OCR and types them into Frappe Books: a ~$0.0002-per-decision model picks each action while a deep model periodically rewrites its playbook, with results verified against the accounting database.

name: jev-chess-bench
description: A chess benchmark that plays Jev (via Vercel AI Gateway) against Stockfish 16 with frozen protocols, durable cost caps, retained raw responses, PGN export/replay, a public match viewer, provisional relative ratings, and scripts for local validation, hosted workers, and video recording.

name: Jev-Moderation-Bot
description: A Python Discord moderation bot powered by TypeSafe AI that deletes spam and scam links in real time, applies progressive discipline (warning DMs escalating to timeouts), profiles members via `/profile` with scam/spam/toxicity scores, posts mod-log alerts with pardon/ban buttons, and learns from pardoned false positives to prevent repeat false flags.

name: jev_model
description: A Jupyter notebook project demonstrating cost-saving LLM routing with Jev (TypeSafe AI's System One classifier) and LangChain: it builds a `ModelRouterMiddleware` agent that sends each request to a fast or powerful model based on typed question probabilities, plus a labeled eval set with confusion matrix, cost/latency benchmarks, and a `wrap_model_call`-based custom router for per-turn re-classifi

name: trade-jev
description: trade-jev is a backtesting harness that evaluates the Jev (TypeSafe) model as a BUY/SELL/HOLD trader on 15 days of Databento NQ L10 order-book data, supporting paid live runs against baselines, free re-scoring of stored answers under new parameters, a local web app for interactive replay, and result publishing with licensed data stripped.

name: captaincore
description: CaptainCore is a Go CLI for hosting professionals that manages WordPress sites at scale via SSH and WP-CLI, providing incremental Restic backups to B2, Git-based change tracking, uptime monitoring, bulk updates, Kinsta/GridPane APIs, malware scanning, and a REST/WebSocket server.

name: jevlike
description: Jevlike is a research starter for training a small one-pass model that scores N text options against a context via per-option attention queries and softmax, with train/eval/predict CLIs, a byte or frozen Hugging Face encoder, JSONL data, and Doom, chess, and Wikispeedia examples.

name: ruby_decision_model
description: Ruby gem that answers typed questions (noul, choice, score) about a state with calibrated probabilities via one Client backed by OpenRouter or Typesafe, with retries, model aliases, pluggable transports, and typed errors—no runtime dependencies.

name: kev-model-router
description: An OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible proxy that routes each request to a configured provider endpoint based on a local kev decision model's classification of the last user message, with fail-open defaults, per-conversation decision caching, complexity-based upgrades, and passthrough auth at zero cost.

name: jev-skills
description: Seven installable skills and a CLI that let Claude Code and Codex delegate bounded choices—picking skills, models, context, first tests, triage targets, or plans—to the TypeSafe Jev decision model, with offline dry-runs, explicit live calls, and opt-in automation.

name: jev-browser-local
description: A fully local engine for jev-browser that replaces TypeSafe's hosted Jev model with Qwen2.5-1.5B/0.5B on CUDA behind a bridge speaking the /v1/systemone and typing contracts, enabling zero-cost browser automation with pruned action spaces and ~1-second decisions.

name: kev-onnx
description: Self-hosted, CPU-only API server running a quantized ONNX build of the KEV decision model in one Docker container, exposing a TypeSafe-compatible /v1/systemone endpoint that returns calibrated probabilities for choice, yes/no, and scored questions in a single forward pass.

name: laya-needle
