description: A local, offline-capable Chrome extension and Python server that uses the 322M-parameter Laya model to semantically search any webpage in natural language, highlighting matching passages and their key sentence via a single batched forward pass—no API key, cloud, or cost required.

name: jev-chess-algo
description: Extracted decision core of jevchess.com: offers every legal move as typed choice options so JEV, a textless probability-returning model, cannot produce illegal moves, and precomputes exchanges and hanging pieces in TypeScript because the model is bad at arithmetic.

name: dspy-typesafeify
description: A proof-of-concept DSPy fork providing a `@typesafeify` decorator that routes typed signature outputs (booleans, Literals, scored fields) through Typesafe's inference path while freeform fields stay on the DSPy LM—yielding 15.9% faster and 30.1% cheaper calls with no API changes.

name: duckdb-dual-cognition
description: A native DuckDB extension that composes cheap, batched System One judgments (classification, scoring, probability) with selective System Two LLM reasoning in a single SQL pipeline, escalating only low-confidence rows while preserving final results, decision provenance, caching, and per-system concurrency controls inside the relation.

name: laya-php
description: A PHP 8.4+ SDK for the self-hosted Laya decision engine that answers typed choice, score, and yes/no questions about text in 100+ languages, returning calibrated results as enums, ints, and bools over any PSR-18 client, with Laravel support and a test fake.

name: jevs-kitchen-chaos
description: Jev's Kitchen Chaos is a live Overcooked-style 3D benchmark arena where four AI chefs make streamed API decisions, letting users swap decision models/LLMs and compare score, latency, policy, confidence, token cost, and downloadable decision logs.

name: jev-cvss
description: Python scripts that score vulnerability descriptions by having TypeSafe's Jev model select CVSS v3.0/v3.1/v4.0 metric values via the System One API while computing scores deterministically in code per official FIRST specifications, outputting scores, vector strings, and per-metric probability spreads for calibration auditing.

name: laya
description: Laya is a non-autoregressive decision model that answers typed choice, score, and boolean questions about a given text or JSON state with calibrated probabilities in a single ~33ms forward pass across 100+ languages.

name: avalanche
description: Avalanche is a Python framework for building typed data pipelines that mix deterministic transformation steps with LLM-backed agent and classifier steps in a single DAG, executed by an operator with web, TUI, and CLI interfaces for running and inspecting workflows.

name: FlyJev2048
description: A toolkit that simulates all 166,700 fruit fly brain neurons as a spiking network to play 2048, benchmarks it against the Jev AI model on identical seeded games, and ships the game engine, expectimax teacher bot, readout trainer, controls, and video renderer.

name: bside
description: bside is a CLI/MCP tool that drives the Aside browser with TypeSafe Jev's typed System One decisions — picking actions and elements only from enumerated candidates in ~0.3–1s — so it cannot hallucinate tool calls and runs faster and cheaper than LLM-driven loops.

name: jev-recall
description: jev-recall is a retrieval tool that filters an AI assistant's memories by semantic relevance rather than surface resemblance, using TypeSafe's Jev with embeddings and RAG techniques to surface pertinent context for LLM-powered agents, with a Next.js implementation.

name: Jev-Flywheel
description: A runnable offline demo of an interpretable text-scoring loop: a frozen model answers typed questions, a small readable model weighs them into verdicts, and human disagreement re-weights answers or adds plain-English questions—exposing hidden label bias without retraining.

name: jev-agent-chess
description: A Next.js/TypeScript chess web app where you play against TypeSafe AI's Jev (with six personalities, difficulty levels, and confidence/candidate-move panels), browser-based Stockfish 19 Lite, or a hybrid mode—featuring evaluation bars, clocks, draw offers, game review, keyboard play, FEN/PGN support, and server-side rate-limited API key handling.

name: jevscan-evm
description: A Python CLI that scans Solidity/EVM repos via TypeSafe's Jev, running 343 detectors across 14 vulnerability categories to output a color-coded HEATMAP.md scoring each file's bug likelihood and flagging suspect functions with confidence percentages for fast, cheap pre-audit triage.

name: jev-chess
description: A UCI chess engine that delegates move selection to TypeSafe's Jev "System One" decision model via API calls, featuring TOML prompt templates with move-analysis placeholders, configurable temperature sampling, and a tournament harness for benchmarking prompt variants against anchors like Maia and Stockfish to estimate its ~940 Elo.

name: deci-serv
description: DeciServ is a local PyTorch HTTP server that hosts small non-autoregressive classifier models resident on GPU, answering typed decision questions (tool-call gating, routing, injection checks) with calibrated probabilities in a single ~13–40 ms forward pass via a `/decide` endpoint, serving as a hallucination-free System-1 decision gate alongside agent LLM stacks.

name: jev-svg-recognition
description: A research pipeline that classifies sanitized SVG code by feeding ~100 yes/no questions about it to the Jev language model and training logistic regression on the answer log-odds, achieving 93.8% accuracy on LLM-drawn object SVGs—beating pixel, n-gram, and element-count classifiers and generalizing across unseen model families and emoji styles.

name: jev-router
description: jev-router is a local pass-through proxy for Claude Code and Codex CLI that asks the Jev decision model which tier each human-written turn needs, then routes the session to a fast, balanced, frontier, or max model—escalating only upward within a session to preserve prompt cache and output quality.

name: jevclassifier
description: Classify is a local SvelteKit web app that runs the Jev model over Telegram Desktop JSON exports, labeling channel or chat posts with custom choice/score/boolean questions, token/cost meters, per-speaker tone summaries, and a dictionary-walking LLM chat mode.

name: open-jev-approvals
description: A per-project hook-based approval gate for Claude Code that sends intercepted tool calls to TypeSafe Jev for review and applies a local allow/deny policy—defaulting to allow on review failure—for third-party API setups that cannot use the harness's own approval flow.

name: jev-effort
description: jev-effort is a Claude Code plugin that routes each prompt through the Jev classifier on OpenRouter to automatically adjust per-turn reasoning effort (low/medium/high/xhigh) from your `/effort` baseline, with confidence thresholds, shadow-mode preview, decision logging, and fallbacks on classifier failure.

name: jevgraph
description: JevGraph is a schema-guided pipeline that converts PDF/DOCX/PPTX/text into evidence-backed candidate knowledge graphs via local parsing, bounded candidate blocking, closed-set relation decisions, and schema checks sorting edges into proposed/review/rejected states.

name: djev-spark
description: A Docker deployment running DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B (NVFP4) on a DGX Spark via patched vLLM, serving Jev's POST /v1/systemone API with probabilistic answers to batched structured questions, dependency-staged reads, image inputs, and seeded sampling.

name: memsearch
description: memsearch is a cross-platform plugin that gives AI coding agents persistent semantic memory — automatically capturing conversations as editable Markdown, indexing them in Milvus with hybrid dense+BM25 retrieval, and distilling repeated workflows into reusable skills.

name: jev-code-reviewer
description: A local CLI and Chrome extension that reviews agent-generated GitHub PRs, classifying each diff into configurable P0/P1/P2 priorities (P0 shown by default) with natural-language explanations a toggle away from the original code, posting nothing to GitHub.

name: openjev-multimodal
description: openjev-multimodal is a local, open-source Jev-compatible SystemOne API that turns text and images into typed decisions—yes probabilities, up-to-255-option choices with full distributions, and rubric scores—in one output token via Qwen on llama.cpp/Metal.

name: tax-doc-classifier
description: An open-source TypeScript library that classifies each PDF page of a tax document into 261 IRS form IDs and 7 page kinds with calibrated confidence scores—via one call to TypeSafe's Jev decision model against a generated JSON form registry—at $0.001/page, 34× cheaper and 6× faster than an LLM pipeline.

name: better-call-jev
description: A zero-dependency Node 18+ client for TypeSafe AI's Jev evaluation model, packaged as a Claude Code plugin that exposes a CLI and ES module for boolean, choice, and score judgments, with an optional SessionStart hook delegating every judgment call to Jev.

name: jev-lens
description: A Chrome extension that badges X and LinkedIn posts READ/MAYBE/SKIP using TypeSafe's Jev decision model against a plain-English interest profile you write, highlighting reads and dimming skips in ~300 ms for about 3 cents per 1,000 posts under your own API key.

name: jevalyzer
description: Jevalyzer is a Bun CLI that grades locally stored coding-agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity) by scoring every exchange with the Jev model, revealing failure modes and which model you actually prefer, in an HTML report or terminal dashboard.

name: JevChatHud
description: A desktop HUD for livestreamers that ingests Twitch, Discord, YouTube, and Facebook chat, scores each message for relevancy and kind via TypeSafe's Jev model, filters the feed by threshold or tags, and tracks per-user stats and API cost.

name: duckdb-jev
description: duckdb-jev is a native C++ DuckDB extension for semantic predicates, classification, and rubric scoring via the TypeSafe/Jev API, batching and streaming inference directly in SQL with caching, retries, and scoped credentials—no Python UDFs or separate server required.

name: jeverifier
description: JeVerifier is a CLI/MCP harness that places the Jev classifier under a Claude coding session to cut re-reading—generating token-budgeted doc reading lists, session handover digests, and incremental doc-contradiction and code-rule checks—while recording reviews so unchanged work is never audited twice.

name: yoshi
description: Yoshi is an experimental local proxy for Claude Code and Codex that prunes eligible completed tool spans from resent conversation history via Jev judgments, preserves protocol/tool identity with explicit omission markers, forwards to Anthropic/OpenAI, and streams responses unchanged.

name: docjev
description: DocJev is a Python library, CLI, and local app that categorizes PDF/DOCX/PPTX documents against natural-language rules and splits multi-document packets into per-document PDFs, using local LiteParse text extraction, the hosted Jev decision engine, and optional LlamaParse OCR.

name: sokudan
description: sokudan is a Japanese-native 310M-parameter decision model that answers typed choice, score, and bool questions about input text in a single forward pass via decision-head logits—no generation or parsing—returning calibrated probabilities, with MLX/torch backends and a `/v1/systemone`-compatible server.

name: jeq
description: jeq is a composable CLI that lets scripts and agents ask the Jev model typed questions — mapping, rating, ranking, and reducing piped NDJSON records, then gating or validating results locally — directly in the terminal with no boilerplate, state, or side effects.

name: minecraft-ai-bot
description: A Mineflayer-based Minecraft server bot that combines Gemini for chat conversations and Jev for rate-limited explicit instructions (e.g., `Jev: come here`), supporting `!` commands for movement, building, and safe autonomous actions, plus an independent Cloudflare Worker that pings the server every 30 minutes and optionally sends Discord webhook alerts when it comes back online.

name: jev-adblocker
description: jev-adblocker is an ad-blocking tool that filters or suppresses advertisements, helping users reduce unwanted ad content during browsing or related workflows.

name: jevdemo
description: A standalone TypeSafe API test suite providing a local FastAPI web demo and CLI script that call the Jev model via the official Python SDK to return structured Noul (yes/no probability), Choice (routing), and Score answers—displaying probabilities, confidence, model version, token usage, and raw JSON for customer-service-style evaluations.

name: pijev
description: pijev is a drop-in Python SDK extension that expands Jev Choice questions into sampled or exhaustive option-order permutations in one `system_one` request, then averages label-aligned probabilities to reduce order sensitivity with guaranteed no-worse mean Brier score or log loss.

name: jev-latam-lead-triage
description: A fail-closed lead-triage tool that routes WhatsApp/CRM messages to auto-handle, review queue, or human based on Jev model confidence, providing a dependency-free Python/JS client, an n8n workflow template with auth/rate-limit/circuit-breaker, and a 60-row Spanish (MX/LATAM) benchmark for threshold calibration.

name: yc-jev-bench
description: A Next.js app benchmarking whether TypeSafe's Jev can replace an LLM reranker on natural-language search over all 6,245 YC companies, shipping a live BM25+embedding search demo, resumable benchmark scripts, an Opus-graded results report, and Vercel deployment guidance for bundling ONNX model weights.

name: laya
description: Node.js/TypeScript package that runs the Laya System 1 decision model via ONNX Runtime (no Python or PyTorch needed), returning calibrated probabilities for choice, rubric-score, and yes/no questions about a given state in one batched forward pass.

name: JevGram
description: JevGram is a FastAPI app that judges each sentence, paragraph and full text of an uploaded PDF research paper as human-written, AI-assisted or AI-generated via TypeSafe's Jev model, drawing confidence-scaled highlights and an overall verdict directly on the pages.

name: jev-skill-router
description: A Claude Code plugin that routes every prompt by scoring each skill's relevance via Jev before the model sees it, auto-invoking skills above a configurable threshold, suggesting borderline ones, and gating the rest — replacing manual per-skill switches with parallel, per-turn judgments that stay fast at any catalog size.

name: Augustus
description: Agent skill for deciding where and how to place typed probabilistic judgment (Jev-class System One decision models like TypeSafe Jev's Choice/Score/Noul) via classical decision methods, composition algebra, question design, and a validation gate.

name: jev-compact
description: A Codex CLI plugin that hooks session compaction to score every tool call with the TypeSafe Jev model for continued relevance, then re-injects verbatim into the next model request any still-critical outputs that Codex's built-in summary dropped.

name: sf-lean-automation-bench
description: Benchmark comparing Lean proof automation—waterfall, aesop, induction/case-split search, and the jev-lean harness ranked by TypeSafe's Jev model or alternatives—on 590 Software Foundations exercises and 1,448 theorems, reporting strict proof success, timings, and per-arm costs.

name: jev-adventure-game
description: A browser-based Next.js dark-fantasy adventure where TypeSafe Jev evaluates every turn’s outcome, consequence, danger, chaos, and action risk, while GPT-4o-mini narrates those rulings without overriding them.

name: oxlint-plugin-laya
description: An oxlint plugin that turns plain-English yes/no questions about functions, calls, JSX elements, or whole files into lint rules, sending each match to a Laya model server and reporting an error when its yes-probability meets a configurable cutoff.

name: jev-sales-radar
description: A Rust-native, sub-25ms in-call teleprompter that detects hidden objections, predicts prospects' next statements, and serves verbatim counter-scripts with delivery-tone cues from pre-indexed sales playbooks—avoiding the multi-second LLM lag that stalls live deals.

name: jev-code-review-benchmark
description: A benchmark repo testing whether TypeSafe's Jev model performs rule-based Python code reviews cheaper and faster than Gemini Flash and Claude Fable—finding ~45–274× lower cost and 0.75s median latency at 98% correctness—with reproducible protocol, data, and runner.

name: claude-jev
description: A Claude Code plugin that routes cheap per-turn judgments to TypeSafe's Jev model—blocking edits that break instruction-file rules, sub-second compaction keeping key rows verbatim, subagent tier selection and brief checks, and prompt routing hints—failing open on errors.

name: jev-vs-llm-tb-amr
description: A reproducible benchmark comparing Jev's typed-decision API (27 questions in one ~0.4s call) versus Qwen3.8-27B's 27 sequential calls (~100–230s/isolate) for WHO-catalogue-grounded tuberculosis drug-resistance prediction, with code, data, and scripts showing ~98% agreement.

name: jev-fund
description: An open-source Next.js paper hedge fund where Jev (TypeSafe via Vercel AI SDK) or a keyless deterministic mock makes buy/sell/hold calls on a $100k long-only book marked to delayed Yahoo Finance prices, publishing a public tape of holdings, buys, and realized losses.

name: jevgrep
description: jevgrep is a grep-like CLI that filters lines, JSON records, or whole files by asking the Jev model a natural-language yes/no predicate, returning grep-compatible matches, counts, exit codes, probabilities, and confidence scores for semantic filtering in pipelines.

name: ghost-ops-jev-buildathon
description: A drop-in rules module that pre-checks every Ledger finance-agent tool call, blocking bank-detail diversions, over-limit or split payments, sanctioned payees, duplicates, bad refunds/write-offs and unearned revenue—while redirecting the agent so legitimate invoices still get paid.

name: killmyidea
description: Kill My Idea evaluates startup ideas by asking TypeSafe Jev 10 parallel questions—eight scored 0–4, weighted by goal (money, open source, or fun) into a 0–100 score gated by understandability—to return a KILL/FIX/SHIP verdict, deployable locally or on Vercel with opt-out SQLite analytics archiving.

name: decision-gate
description: A drop-in agent skill/CLI that batches candidate pages, search results, and snippets into single typed yes/no-probability calls to a cheap decision model (Jev), ingesting only items that pass—measured to keep ~85K tokens out of context (~70% page-read cut) for ~$0.007.

name: jevtok-ts
description: jevtok-ts is a dependency-free TypeScript/Node.js port of the jevtok tokenizer that provides offline Jev token counting, encoding/decoding, and structured request token estimation with configurable context-budget checks, for preflight accounting of TypeSafe Jev API calls without Python, network access, or API keys.

name: cmd-mod-jev-nudge
description: A Command Code mod that calls the typesafe/jev model whenever an agent stops to decide whether unfinished work merits a nudge, continuing the run (up to 8 nudges, configurable) unless it is waiting on the user or making no progress.

name: JevPR
description: JevPR is a GitHub App that ingests pull-request webhooks, sends normalized PR context to the Jev decision engine, and deterministically maps its LOW/NORMAL/SPECIALIST verdicts to actions such as auto-approval, reviewer requests, or check-run updates via a YAML policy.

name: jev_model_routers
description: A zero-dependency Python tool that wraps Claude Code with a local proxy which asks TypeSafe's Jev decision model, per new turn, which Claude model (Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus) best fits the task—rewriting only the request's model while preserving the UI, tools, streaming, manual overrides, and failing open on errors.

name: jev_stock
description: A TypeSafe JEV forecasting pipeline that fetches a Hong Kong stock plus HSI and HSTECH via AKShare, builds a leakage-free market state from technical, monthly, weekly, and financial context, requests structured up/flat/down probabilities for trading days and a 30-day endpoint, validates responses, renders HTML reports, and supports dated backtests.

name: jev-ra
description: jev-ra is a fast browser-automation layer for CLI coding agents that drives Chrome via the DevTools Protocol through MCP tools or CLI commands, using a System One decision model to pick each step's operation and target element in one round trip—benchmarked 4–8.5× faster than browser-use—while the calling agent supplies text values, reads results, and handles escalations.

name: JevMC
description: JevMC is an unofficial, dependency-free Java SDK for PaperMC plugins that wraps the TypeSafe.ai `POST /v1/systemone` endpoint, letting plugins send state plus typed questions (Noul, Choice, Score) and receive structured decisions with probabilities and confidence via asynchronous `CompletableFuture` calls with automatic retries.

name: jiffy
description: Jiffy runs typed yes/no, multiple-choice, and scored questions over documents and images using a frozen DiffusionGemma model, returning bounded answers with full probability distributions—no task-specific training—via a Jev-compatible API or a batched shared-prefill local SDK.

name: jev-build-sentinel
description: A GitHub Action that picks the minimum safe CI scope per pull request—skip, targeted, or full tests—using diff analysis and an AI risk engine whose deterministic safety policy forces full runs on low confidence, failures, or risky changes.

name: JevTools
description: JevTools is a toolkit and reference implementation for building AI apps with the Jev sub-second typed decision model, combining an interactive web cockpit, zero-dependency Python REST server with SQLite request-history storage, CLI demos featuring speculative fan-out and offline mock mode, and an Obsidian-compatible knowledge vault.

name: tool-routing-experiment-with-jev
description: A benchmarking harness that compares how Kimi K3, GPT-6 Astra, and the Jev router select the next tool as catalog size grows from 50 to 200 real MCP tools, recording golden-check pass/fail, hops, prompt tokens, and per-condition cost to quantify routing accuracy and expense at scale.

name: llm-skills
description: Agent skills (SKILL.md + templates) for Cursor/Claude Code/Antigravity/Codex covering benchmark-verified local LLM selection with VRAM checks and Jev deterministic-model design—candidate detection, TCO estimation, typed schemas, fallbacks, eval-set freeze, calibration, observability.

name: typesafe-sdk
description: Unofficial .NET SDK for TypeSafe AI that provides fluent builders for Noul (yes/no), Choice, and Score verification questionnaires, DI-integrated clients with Polly-based retries and timeouts, OpenTelemetry tracing, and a typed exception hierarchy for resilient LLM/agent evaluation workflows.

name: sttp-ai
description: sttp-ai is a Scala client library built on sttp client that wraps OpenAI, Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), Jev (TypeSafe AI), and OpenAI-compatible APIs (Ollama, Grok, OpenRouter), offering streaming via fs2/ZIO/Akka/Pekko/Ox, structured outputs, tool calling, an agent loop, and an agent-testkit for testing without paid API calls.

name: jev-lab
description: Jev Lab triages bookmarked captures into a knowledge vault using TypeSafe's Jev model, which returns typed probabilities for page routing, knowledge density, and promotion detection, while a local web app lets you inspect every call, tune link thresholds, and approve proposed links.

name: jev-benchmark
description: Benchmark suite for Jev, TypeSafe's "System One" judgment model: runnable code, labeled data, raw request/response logs, metrics, and an interactive playground testing calibrated-probability judgment on chess move selection and NPC addressee detection.

name: typesafe4s
description: A Scala 3 SDK for TypeSafe's System One API that sends state and typed questions and returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities, exposing one shared runtime natively to ZIO, Cats Effect, Ox, Kyo, and Pekko with optional per-library JSON adapters.

name: tev1
description: tev1 provides a reproducible Together AI recipe, dataset builders, training/evaluation scripts, and saved results for fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B into a decision model that selects one letter from supplied options.

name: jev-1.13-mini-benchmark
description: A self-contained benchmark harness that evaluates the jev-1.13 structured decision model on 34 labeled support-triage cases across its noul/choice/score question types, with offline scoring, threshold sweeps, confusion matrices, and consistency checks on a swappable dataset.

name: openclaw-smart-router
description: OpenClaw Smart Router is an OpenAI-compatible Fastify/TypeScript proxy that selects eligible Surplus Intelligence chat models using capability, cost, latency, history, preference, and jev classification signals while exposing metrics, feedback, routing history, dashboards, and hot-reloadable registries.

name: jev-browser-skill
description: Standalone CLI (`jb`) and `jb-browser` agent skill that drives an isolated Playwright Chromium daemon, letting an LLM (Vercel AI Gateway or TypeSafe) choose in-page actions to complete a scoped browsing goal, with session control, origin allowlists, and video recording.

name: ai-decision-bench
description: A Python CLI harness that benchmarks structured AI decision APIs by running your own labeled JSONL dataset through pluggable provider adapters (TypeSafe, OpenAI, offline mock) and emitting reproducible accuracy, failure-rate, calibration/ECE, latency, and cost metrics.

name: jev-code
description: jev-code gives Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, and shells a common Jev toolset and skill for typed labels, yes/no checks, scores, and rankings with calibrated probabilities and auto/review decisions, enabling fast, consistent evidence-based triage without frontier-model calls or ad hoc heuristics.

name: libsemop
description: libsemop is a C++17 library for defining typed semantic questions (boolean, choice, score, enum) once and running them on any System One classifier model, returning "don't know" instead of guessing, with flows, filtering, reranking, escalation, timeouts, and benchmarks.

name: voicebind
description: Voicebind is an Omarchy/Hyprland plugin that uses local Whisper speech recognition and optional Jev AI interpretation to open apps, move windows between workspaces, chain commands, dictate text, and recall saved window layouts via a wake phrase or F10 key.

name: beebots
description: beebots is an open-source, Docker-deployed system where three AI bees—designed via OpenAI from your prompts and driven by TypeSafe's Jev decision model under a code-enforced risk layer—paper-trade OKX perpetual futures on real prices, streamed to a live dashboard with an opt-in public leaderboard.

name: jev-enterprise-decision-fabric
description: An experimental .NET architecture that centralizes TypeSafe Jev semantic decisions behind versioned contracts, batched provider calls, typed evidence, and deterministic policies, shipped with a 111-case benchmark comparing Jev to Claude, a decision inspector, and runnable samples.

name: pi-saver
description: Pi-Saver is a Pi Coder extension that intercepts conversation context before each inference and uses TypeSafe's Jev to evaluate and drop historical turns irrelevant to the latest request—cutting context tokens by up to 75%+ while preserving full session history, with active, observe, and off modes plus per-call before/after/review logs.

name: jev-eval
description: A CLI evaluation harness that benchmarks Jev's structured judgments against LLM baselines on labeled datasets, computing accuracy, calibration, inter-rater agreement, latency, cost, and paired significance tests so model comparisons rest on statistics, not anecdote.

name: NanoJev
description: NanoJev is a 0.6B-parameter parallel decision model (Qwen3-0.6B backbone plus decision heads) that maps states, questions, and 2–255 candidates to complete probability distributions in a single forward pass—zero output-token decoding—with persistent serving and verified maze/Snake demos.

name: voicevox-jev-proxy
description: A Python CLI and VOICEVOX-compatible proxy server that corrects Japanese text-to-speech readings by consulting TypeSafe's Jev model over the SystemOne API—using Sudachi/UniDic/JMdict dictionaries to resolve word boundaries, readings, accent phrases, and optional intonation—then rewriting the audio query and re-synthesizing corrected WAV output.

name: jevex
description: Jevex is a Python CLI prototype where the Jev controller selects and approves every tool call while a LangChain model only fills argument slots and writes answers, enforcing zero LLM control-flow authority over 12 local read-only MCP tools with token accounting.

name: shopping-minion
description: Shopping Minion is a CLI/web-app tool that turns photos of handwritten grocery lists into a reviewed cart at the Andorinha supermarket via OCR (Claude), deterministic Playwright search and cart actions, and a typed decision model (Jev) for product selection — always stopping before checkout so a human places the order.

name: jev-chess
description: A chess web app demo where TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model picks every move as a structured choice—play against it as White or Black or watch it play itself—displaying each move's confidence, top alternatives, and response time, with a python-chess backend validating moves and enforcing standard endings.

name: jev-grug
description: A demo chat app that coaxes TypeSafe AI's Jev structured-decision model into conversation by repeatedly applying its choice primitive to pick each next word from a 979-word vocabulary via parallel tournaments, with deterministic mock fallback and a probability inspector.

name: jevditor
description: A programmable writing linter that flags patterns you dislike—via exact code checks and a yes/no classifier scoring each versioned rule against sentences, passages, or sections—underlining findings in a Tiptap editor and offering Claude-drafted rewrites only on request.

name: jev-pilot
description: A Claude Code plugin that routes each prompt through Jev, a fast decision model, to set reasoning effort (with mid-turn escalation after repeated tool failures), pick the cheapest adequate subagent model, select one relevant skill, advise on execution strategy, and log every decision—surfaced through an animated terminal pet that reports Jev's choices and confidence.

name: beebrain
description: BeeBrain is a Python CLI/browser tool that simulates a honeybee brain to score live or synthetic memecoin pools through five neural lobes, learn from closed trades via reward and punishment signals, and provide scans, reports, paper-account races, and forward-testing without placing orders.

name: ruleraven
description: RuleRaven is a read-only Kubernetes incident-triage controller that turns workload state and Events into deterministic, explainable incident decisions, persists them in MongoDB, and sends signed at-least-once webhook alerts without changing workloads.

name: jev-connect4
description: A Bun-based web Connect Four harness that plays humans or autoplay matches against TypeSafe’s Jev model through nine query strategies, with a live inspector grading every request/response against engine ground truth to isolate whether bad play stems from the model or prompt design.

name: jev-team-calendar
description: A local web application that analyzes a folder of resumes with Jev to identify candidates qualified for a selected project's required skills, then uses the SolverForge constraint solver to schedule tasks across the work week while enforcing skill matching, availability windows, and no-double-booking rules.

name: hunch
description: A Ruby gem providing probabilistic control flow primitives—`chance`, `pick`, and `rate`—that let programs branch, select, and sample randomly, powered by TypeSafe's Jev.

name: butterfly-jev
description: A browser-based counterfactual simulation: 24 village residents diverge from one altered private memory—fork the world, inject a rumor or evidence, and trace consequences via synchronized timelines, causal ancestry, decision inspectors, and replayable runs.

name: JevX
description: JevX is a CLI and MCP server that scans a codebase for hardcoded judgment-call rules (regexes, keyword lists, magic slices), scores each against AI and learned patterns, replaces strong fits with TypeSafe/Jev decisions while keeping the original as fallback, verifies changes with the project's own tests, and supports preview, undo, and opt-in anonymized pattern sharing.

name: Jev-Network-Packet-Analyzer
description: A Python/FastAPI tool that passively captures Layer 3/4 network traffic via Scapy, pre-filters noise with deterministic rules and Redis flow caching so only anomalies reach the Jev AI triage engine, then streams live telemetry to a WebSocket dashboard, sends Resend email alerts, and simulates attacks for testing.

name: Working-Memory-Jev
description: Passage is a localhost web tool for educators that analyzes instructional text against a selected working-memory slot budget, using the Jev API to estimate per-step cognitive demand, highlight source text, map connections between words, and support manual grouping review and export.

name: tg_accessor
description: CLI toolkit that exports Telegram group history to CSV, narrows it to one user's messages plus context, uses TypeSafe to stitch messages into topical threads scored for conflict and convincingness, and rolls it up into a per-user PROFILE.md.

name: jev-oscillator-playground
description: A dependency-free Node.js playground that turns Jev's answers to 32 Choice questions (amplitudes 0–15, sent in one System One request to TypeSafe via a local proxy that keeps the API key server-side) into a 32×4-bit wavetable you can draw, edit, and play in the browser with Web Audio.

name: jev-brotato
description: An open-source Python harness that lets TypeSafe's Jev play Brotato via a local Godot bridge mod, choosing legal movement, shop, upgrade and crate actions from structured game state while recording each run with probabilities, latency, token usage and cost.

name: keel
description: Keel is a local-first macOS Rust/GPUI coding workspace that unifies sessions, editor, terminal, and provider connections, routing fresh tasks through a local Core ML selector (Laya) or hosted Jev backend—with host-side validation, abstention/fallback inspection, and decision records—while connecting external coding agents via ACP.

name: compact-jev
description: A Claude Code plugin (`/compact-jev`) and TypeScript library that frees context by asking Jev via Vercel AI Gateway which old tool calls and results still matter, then removing or truncating stale ones while keeping messages verbatim—no summary needed.

name: jev-sim-use
description: jev-sim-use is a macOS CLI that drives iOS Simulator and Android devices toward a stated goal, delegating each step to the small Jev model over sim-use for fast, token-efficient navigation that pauses into resumable sessions when unsure.

name: jev-bigquery-cloudrun
description: End-to-end demo that scores 30 fictional support tickets by owning team, urgency, and blocked workflow through TypeSafe's Jev API behind a private Cloud Run adapter, saving typed results via a BigQuery remote function for ordinary SQL queries.

name: agent0
description: agent0 is a desktop AI agent (Electron app and CLI) that pairs your Kimi or OpenAI model with optional TypeSafe Jev tool routing, MCP server integration, task planning, skills discovery, and persistent memory.

name: rein-harness
description: A Claude Code–style terminal chat harness that drives the official `claude` and `codex` CLIs across multiple subscription accounts, with per-task model routing, goal verification, subagents, skills, and project-scoped tools — all without extracting OAuth tokens.

name: jev-ticket-router
description: A FastAPI prototype that routes support tickets by asking Jev, TypeSafe AI's System One decision model, three typed questions (team, urgency, anger) in one batched call via the `jevlang` Python DSL, escalating to human review when team-classification confidence falls below 0.6.

name: Jevstiller
description: Jevstiller is a drop-in proxy for Jev classification calls that trains a small local model on Jev's own probability distributions, then answers most requests itself at ~16 ms (vs ~300 ms) under a statistically bounded agreement target, while forwarding uncertain inputs plus a permanent audit slice to Jev with automatic fallback.

name: jevwire
description: jevwire wires TypeSafe's Jev classifier into agent harnesses — 7 MCP tools, an embeddable library, and Claude Code hooks — to gate risky tool calls, flag injected instructions in fetched results, and catch premature stops with schema-bounded judgments, never generated text.

name: edgextract
description: edgextract turns markdown into a knowledge graph using a user-defined ontology, asking a local Ollama decision model a probability-scored yes/no question per legal link and routing uncertain items to a human review queue rather than silently accepting them.

name: jev-rerank-server
description: A dependency-free Node.js server exposing Cohere-, Jina-, and Voyage-shaped `/rerank` endpoints that score each (query, document) pair as a Jev yes/no question, letting existing RAG stacks rerank documents by changing a configurable base URL.

name: jev-usecases
description: A Python implementation of 30+ runnable use cases for TypeSafe's Jev model, each calling the live `/v1/systemone` API with typed Choice/Score/Noul questions, applying code-based thresholds and rules, and returning a `UseCaseResult` with `decision`, `action_band`, and `actions` for workflows like SOC triage, guardrails, and invoice processing.

name: jev-bouncer
description: jev-bouncer is a single-file, stdlib-only Python gate that gives a coding agent's shell commands, file edits, MCP calls, and web fetches an independent second opinion via typed risk probabilities, hard tripwires, a replayable local audit log, and prompt-injection detection.

name: jev-slop-guard
description: A Chrome MV3 extension that labels each X and LinkedIn post with a Jev-model slop-probability pill (using your own TypeSafe or OpenRouter key), blurring and stamping posts above a configurable threshold while skipping ads, caching scores, and storing settings locally.

name: sentinel-jev
description: Sentinel Jev wraps an abliterated Gemma 4 model on Modal H100s with Jev intent classification, FailproofAI policy enforcement, optional bounded activation steering, and durable trace logging to compare steered versus baseline generation under runtime safeguards.

name: zod-jev
description: zod-jev extends Zod 4 schemas with async semantic() rules sent to TypeSafe Jev in one batched request, turning calibrated model probabilities into ordinary Zod issues (pass/rejected/uncertain/unavailable) so apps can validate meaning-level conditions, threshold them, and fail closed.

name: typesafe-java-sdk
description: An unofficial Java 21+ Maven SDK for TypeSafe AI's System One API (`POST /v1/systemone`), providing sync and async clients with automatic `Retry-After`-aware retries, client-side request validation, fluent question builders, sealed answer hierarchies with forward-compatible unknown types, and typed accessors plus metadata on responses.

name: nano-jev
description: Nano-Jev is a 33M-parameter MiniLM cross-encoder that returns calibrated per-option probabilities for RAG decisions—relevance, sufficiency, groundedness, or custom labels—in ~1–4 ms, enabling filtering, answer verification, and confidence-based escalation to an LLM.

name: ZeroNSFWBot
description: ZeroNSFWBot is an async Rust Telegram moderation bot that inspects commenters’ profiles and group media with local two-stage NSFW models plus optional text, ad, and reaction checks, then applies configurable per-group actions to stop hidden adult-content spam.

name: AirTranslate
description: AirTranslate is a macOS app that captures system or microphone audio and produces live captions and translations via a local-first Apple pipeline or optional cloud engines (OpenAI, Gemini, Qwen, Azure MAI, Grok, Nari, Meta Scribe), with floating captions, saved transcripts, and translated speech.

name: JEV_Feature
description: JEV_Feature provides a local FastAPI orchestrator that uses MLX-based OpenJev intent classification, confidence thresholds, and small Python agents to handle translation, arithmetic, weekday, out-of-scope, and clarification requests.

name: jev-shield
description: A semantic MCP firewall that wraps stdio MCP servers, scoring every tool call, result, and description with calibrated probabilities to block exfiltration, injection, secret leaks, and destructive actions under layered structural rules and session taint tracking.

name: jev-sec-bench
description: A Go CLI that runs blind security benchmarks evaluating the Jev model's typed probability judgments on prompt-injection detection (662 labeled messages) and vulnerable-code ranking (200 matched pairs), with corpus label auditing and a TUI dashboard for results.

name: jev-fast-playwright
description: An MCP server that lets AI coding agents control a real browser via Playwright using ~300 tokens per step, injecting a DOM-compression script and a fast System-1 model (with offline heuristic fallback) to achieve sub-second semantic clicks, typing, scrolling, and multi-tier overlay recovery.

name: laya-rn-executorch
description: A pipeline and bare React Native demo that export the Laya System-1 typed-decision model to ExecuTorch .pte (int8/int4, XNNPACK/Core ML) and run it fully on-device on Android/iOS, returning choice/score/bool answers with calibrated probabilities offline.

name: askgrep
description: askgrep scores every function in a codebase against a plain-English question using a cheap calibrated classifier, returning ranked file:line hits for pennies so agents find semantic patterns—e.g., SQL built by string concatenation—exhaustively instead of sampling files or guessing regexes.

name: openagents
description: OpenAgents is a Rust monorepo home to Coder, a terminal coding agent that routes turns through typed Jev judgments and a model-agnostic generative door, runs a bounded shell loop, and talks to a self-hostable Nostr relay for account-free, inspectable job transport.

name: jev-doom-agent
description: A WASM-compiled Chocolate Doom engine runs two parallel instances of the same Freedoom map, letting a TypeSafe Jev Choice API call (or clearly labeled offline fallback policy) pick tactical macros that a local controller executes as real Doom inputs, enabling side-by-side comparison of LLM-driven vs simulated gameplay.

name: pi-jev-router
description: A Pi Coding Agent extension that routes tasks across model tiers via Jev classification, declared model capabilities, context and cost estimates, and circuit-breaker health, with task-boundary awareness, shadow-by-default operation, and preview/explain/stats controls.

name: jev-block-android-ad
description: An Android noise gate that funnels notifications and SMS through one pipeline — local OTP gate and sender blacklist first, then a model given channel history and user rules — suppressing only flagged ads while every uncertain path fails open.

name: duckdb-jev
description: A DuckDB extension over Jev that asks a constant-criteria question of every table row in SQL—via jev_choice, jev_score, jev_noul, and jev_ask—returning typed ENUM, DOUBLE, or STRUCT columns validated at plan time, with batching, caching, retries, and jev_usage() accounting.

name: jev-swap
description: CLI that finds decision-type LLM calls in TypeScript/JavaScript and Python codebases, converts them to TypeSafe Jev modules with confidence-gated fallbacks, and shadow-tests them on recorded or proxied traffic to measure agreement, latency, and cost savings.

name: athena-jev
description: ATHENA is an open-source cognitive control layer for OpenCode coding agents where TypeSafe Jev judges each step as GO, DELIBERATE, VERIFY, or BLOCK via its AEGIS, METIS, NIKE, and EPISTEMICS modules—observing passively by default and enforcing only when configured.

name: osENV.io
description: osenv.io is a single Go binary that orchestrates four-model "hybrid" agents (muse, deepseek, qwen, Opus) through one HTTP route, with a Jev layer that scores every action against learned lessons and owner rules before it runs.

name: jev-dotnet
description: An unofficial .NET 10 SDK for TypeSafe's Jev System One API that encodes typed decision plans once and reuses them across calls, validates responses strictly against the contract (failing loudly via `JevProtocolException` on malformed answers), enforces a single per-call deadline, disables retries by default, and supports Native AOT with zero third-party runtime dependencies.

name: experiments-with-jev
description: A playground layering Jev's judgment API over Swiggy food search: each retrieved dish is scored against the raw user intent via choice/score/noul verdicts and split into accepted vs rejected, runnable locally on fixtures or live keys with caching and latency metrics.

name: last-train-jev
description: A single-player detective escape room where TypeSafe Jev evaluates free-text player deductions — classifying actions, matching clue-to-claim connections, and verifying evidential support — so a React/Express server can gate story progress in one fixed train mystery.

name: Jev_Star
description: Jev_Star provides unified StarCraft II macro and micromanagement control—JEV-selected actions with optional Astra planning over BurnySC2 full games and SMAC-Hard/PySC2 unit battles—plus CLI tooling, maps, setup scripts, tests, replays, videos, and paper artifacts for reproducing low-cost LLM-driven SC2 experiments.

name: jev-review
description: Jev Review is a local MCP server (stdio, Node.js 20+) that gives AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode a `jev_review` tool that submits a task, focused diff, and optional file context to the Jev API and returns per-dimension 1–10 quality scores with confidence levels, rubric hints, and deltas versus a previous evaluation, enabling a repeated score-driven improvement loop

name: jevkit
description: jevkit is a Rust CLI for TypeSafe's Jev API that sends typed noul/choice/score questions about a passage and returns JSON probabilities, labels, and scores, with offline linting that catches billed-but-useless questions, scriptable exit codes, keyring auth, and a usage ledger.

name: pi-jev-compact
description: A Pi extension whose `/jev-compact` commands use TypeSafe's Jev model to selectively keep, truncate, or drop tool calls—and optionally assistant prose—then write a pruned new session plus an auditable HTML report, reclaiming context without lossy summaries.

name: maza
description: Maza is a local Node.js MCP gateway that aggregates multiple MCP servers behind a single endpoint, exposing only `find_tool` and `execute_tool` to agents while centrally managing connections, OS-stored credentials, per-tool enablement, client allowlists, and bearer-token authentication.

name: jev-chat-windows
description: A Windows overlay tool that screenshots your own WeChat 4.x window (WGC + fully offline OCR), runs new incoming messages through a Jev intent/tension judgment model plus a configurable LLM to generate three ranked reply drafts, and pastes the chosen text into the input box without ever auto-sending.

name: save-token-jev-clean
description: Portable context-compaction plugin and CLI that asks the Jev model which tool calls and results matter, keeping text verbatim while retaining, bounding, or removing tool output across Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Anthropic/OpenAI adapters, failing open to native compaction.

name: model-router
description: Model Router is a provider-independent TypeScript library that filters a defined model catalog by capabilities and context, applies a pluggable evaluator to select an eligible model and safe fallback, and wraps AI SDK generation, streaming, structured output, and telemetry.

name: estack-demo
description: A stdlib-only Python engine for Nowak–May spatial Prisoner's Dilemma on a toroidal lattice, with deterministic seeded simulation, CSV export, an optional Pygame viewer, and pluggable Jev/random/local-LLM thinker backends with replay, experiment, and calibration tooling.

name: jev-voice-browser-agent
description: A local voice browser agent that turns spoken or typed commands into Chromium actions, pairing a Next.js frontend with a Node.js backend that queries the Impossibl Jev API, enforces confidence-based policy checks and confirmations, and executes approved actions via Playwright.

name: jev-askable-arm
description: jev-askable-arm runs a simulated Franka Panda in ManiSkill by having TypeSafe's Jev API chain ~30 hardcoded motion primitives step-by-step from plain-English goals, completing pick, place, and button-press tasks zero-shot without training, demos, or learned policies.

name: openevals
description: An online eval service that grades every trace and every step of production agent traffic with cheap, fast typed jev questions, writes scores back to Langfuse, and supports custom rubrics, deterministic checks, and human-annotation calibration—all in one process and one SQLite file.

name: gpt-researcher
description: GPT Researcher is an open-source deep research agent that plans questions, crawls web and local sources in parallel, filters context, and generates detailed, cited, unbiased reports exportable to PDF/Word, usable via Python package, server, Claude Skill, or MCP integration.

name: jev-research-pipeline
description: jev-research-pipeline is a Python tool that screens new papers and repos against your open research questions—code owns the loop, judgment-only model Jev routes each source keep/review/drop, a chosen LLM writes per-question Obsidian notes, and your ticks steer future runs.

name: your-signal
description: Your Signal is an open-source Manifest V3 Chrome extension that sends eligible X timeline post text to a BYOK TypeSafe Jev API and locally scores, labels, highlights, dims, collapses, or hides posts per user-chosen interests, weights, and reversible filters, with no telemetry.

name: ai-setup
description: Caliber is an open-source CLI context layer for coding agents that bootstraps and keeps agent config files (CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, AGENTS.md, Copilot instructions) fresh via hooks and LLM-free drift scoring, syncs skills, rules, plugins and MCP servers across agents deterministically, and adds Jev compaction that scores and drops stale tool calls instead of lossy summarization.

name: stanley-code
description: Stanley is a Jev-first CLI that routes natural-language requests to deterministic workflows—checking diffs, reviewing changes, finding test gaps, triaging failures—which gather bounded evidence, ask TypeSafe Jev fixed-choice questions, and apply code-based thresholds, falling back to the Pi agent only when unsupported.

name: jev_speedway
description: A dependency-free Node 20+ top-down racing game where a 60 fps physics simulation drives the cars while TypeSafe Jev judges each driver's worded situation every ~0.8 s, answering four questions (line, pace, overtake, boost) to demonstrate LLM-in-the-loop decision-making.

name: opencode-plugin-variantizer
description: An OpenCode v1 plugin that uses TypeSafe to automatically route each request to one of three fixed-model agents (luna, terra, or sol) and select a reasoning variant (none through max), with configurable fallbacks, confidence-aware notifications, secret-tool credential support, and pre-provider validation to prevent silent mismatches.

name: jev-nlgrep
description: nlgrep is a Node.js CLI that searches code, docs, logs, and text by natural-language meaning via the Jev API, returning threshold-ranked probabilistic matches for semantic, format, and code-behavior conditions, with caching, globs, stdin, JSON output, and request limits.

name: mcp_typesafe
description: An MCP server exposing TypeSafe's System One (Jev) API as 12 tools that return fast (~100 ms), calibrated, structured judgments—probabilities, choices, scores, and confidence—enabling agents to filter, rank, classify, dedupe, verify, and select items in bulk without text generation or parsing.

name: compass
description: Compass is a decision model that answers typed questions (choice, yes/no, score) about a document with calibrated probabilities for every permitted answer—read from model logits rather than generated text—served deterministically over TypeSafe's /v1/systemone API.

name: reflex
description: Reflex is a Pi-based coding agent that pairs any LLM with TypeSafe's Jev System One model, which scores each tool call, turn, and voice transcript in ~400 ms for ~$0.00004 so code can gate risky actions, monitor progress, route models, and drive browser and macOS control.

name: spending-effort-with-jev
description: A Claude Code plugin that has TypeSafe's Jev model score each outgoing message and prints a one-line effort verdict (low/medium/high/max) before Claude starts—optionally asking first or flagging vague hand-offs—so you can switch `/effort` level in time.

name: jevpad
description: jevpad is a Python CLI scratchpad for testing TypeSafe's Jev decision model: edit YAML question files (choice, yes/no, score), run them on text or CSV rows, and inspect full call transcripts, probability-scored answers, replayable runs, and HTML report exports.

name: pi-jev-context-curator
description: A pi extension that uses TypeSafe AI’s Jev model to judge newly added atomic context units each turn and permanently prune nonessential ones without orphaning tool results, while preserving system/current messages, checkpointing judgments, logging removals, and failing open on missing keys or API errors.

name: blink
description: Blink is a Bun CLI that uses the Jev model to drive an ensemble of filesystem-walking agents that score path names and converge on files matching a natural-language query, reporting results as percentage-ranked tables with per-walker traces, cost/token metadata, and saved search outputs.

name: jev-automaton
description: jev-automaton is a zero-dependency Node simulation of 40 autonomous agents on a 48×48 grid whose movement, mating, fighting and responses to typed commands are sampled from Jev predictions, with a live viewer, inherited genomes, mock mode and run analysis for inspecting model-driven behavior.

name: astra-jev-left4dead2
description: Windows controller, VScript observation addon, and OBS recording/editing tools used to finish all five Left 4 Dead 2 campaigns on Easy with bots, combining a Jev decision client, GPT-6 Astra screenshot supervision, Python navigation/aiming, a spending ledger, and regression tests.

name: jev-rag-guard
description: Zero-dependency Python library that wraps the retrieval–generation seam in RAG pipelines with three cheap, calibrated checks — relevance filtering, a sufficiency gate, and claim grounding — through a pluggable typed-decision-model interface, returning a fully auditable trace.

name: typesafe-screening-mcp
description: An MCP server that takes a PubMed query, PMIDs, or title/abstract records and returns calibrated include/maybe/exclude probabilities per article against a research question using TypeSafe's Jev model, screening hundreds in seconds without abstracts entering the LLM context.

name: jev-dreaming
description: Benchmarking suite comparing a Jev-gated Dreaming pipeline (Jev chunk triage/mutation + Gemini memory generation) against a Gemini-only pipeline across latency, token cost, and LLM-judged memory quality, with sandboxed runs and knowledge-graph visualization.

name: ideacheck
description: ideacheck is a terminal tool that evaluates an idea by researching it on the web, asking a judge model a set of weighted typed questions, and reporting per-dimension scores plus a build/explore/park/kill verdict, flagging missing facts and offering a JSON agent mode for scripts.

name: aiko-jev-camera-reaction
description: A browser-based verification demo in which the character Aiko answers on-device MediaPipe-detected hand waves, head tilts, and lean-ins with reaction videos, relaying only numeric landmark data through a Cloudflare Pages Function to Jev for gesture classification.

name: jev-pong
description: An open-source playable Pong demo that benchmarks AI decision latency live—each model call moves the ball one step—comparing Jev's ~227 ms typed decisions against chat models via Vercel AI Gateway, with the agent joining players as a peer in an Ably channel.

name: trading-bot-jev
description: A crypto trading bot that runs a medium-term EMA-200 trend-following strategy on 4-hour Bitvavo candles, optionally biased or vetoed by TypeSafe's Jev news classifier, with paper or real USDC trading, a web dashboard, and backtest/event-study tooling.

name: jev-sandbox
description: A repo of six experiments testing when TypeSafe's Jev decision model can replace an LLM—covering email triage and gluten-label detection—with shared tooling for agreement, confidence-threshold, latency, and cost scoring plus reproducible run scripts and datasets.

name: nudgement
description: nudgement is a Bun-based CLI that reviews commit messages, code comments, tests, READMEs, UI copy, designs, and plans by combining exact rule checks with queries to TypeSafe's Jev model, catching issues like misleading commit messages, weak test assertions, and unexplained literals before you commit.

name: typesafe-playground
description: A Next.js playground for TypeSafe AI’s Jev that lets you edit typed-output examples, run A/B evaluations, triage conversations, extract document fields, route tools, inspect policy-gated code decisions, and test interactive simulations locally or against live API calls.

name: jev-operated-drone
description: Autonomous Tello drone mission tool that powers on via smart plug, joins the drone's Wi-Fi, then lets the jev model decide where to fly—scanning 360° frame batches per stop, confirming people with a strict multi-frame check—to photograph a person, flip, dead-reckon home, and land.

name: jev-ios-ultrafast
description: A Python CLI and Brigade host wrapper that runs goal-driven iOS Simulator tasks via Jev, benchmarks decision models against each other, and records every attempt for replay — enabling automated UI testing and systematic model comparison.

name: jev-lint
description: A lint tool that sends ast-grep-matched code to the Jev classifier API to flag what parsers cannot—names, comments, tests, shell scripts, and commit messages that contradict the code they describe—via 98 calibrated, cutoff-scored rules across multiple languages.

name: jev-resume-disqualifier
description: Deterministic resume-screening engine that batch-screens PDF/DOCX/TXT applicants against hard knockout gates (non-overlapping tenure math, visa status, licenses) in sub-25ms, returning verdicts with cited, EEOC/OFCCP-compliant rejection notices and CSV/JSON audit trails.

name: jev-frontier-bench
description: A reproducible $4.83 OpenRouter benchmark comparing TypeSafe's Jev 1.13 decision model against five frontier LLMs on 200 typed decisions (routing, yes/no, rating, ambiguity) from public datasets, reporting accuracy, calibration, latency, cost, human-label agreement, and a Jev-plus-Claude cascade that cuts cost ~63% while retaining 82.5% accuracy, with logged calls, hashed manifests, and analysis/c

name: triage-bot
description: A Node.js demo tool that triages support tickets in real time by using Jev's typed questions (choice/score/noul) to route each ticket to a specialist agent, score urgency, and decide on human escalation, then has Cerebras draft the reply with per-call latency timing.

name: jevkit
description: jevkit is a Python 3.11+ client library (httpx-only dependency) that wraps the TypeSafe Jev decision model—which answers typed yes/no, choice, and score questions with calibrated probabilities—in a control layer that maps answers to act/confirm/escalate confidence bands, and provides countermeasures for known model weaknesses (counting, dates, injection guards, invariance checks, extraction, f

name: tiab-review-plugin
description: A Chrome extension that streamlines title/abstract screening for systematic reviews, syncing decisions to Google Sheets with LLM-assisted judgments via Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenAI, or TypeSafe models, multi-reviewer assignment sets, Drive-based full-text PDF import, and offline save retry.

name: wakegate
description: wakegate is a TypeScript helper that screens wakeups for sleeping long-running agents, spending one ~250 ms Jev judgment call to decide whether an event or observation merits resuming the full LLM turn, and defaulting to wake on user messages, errors, or repeated skips.

name: jev-tokenize
description: A zero-dependency Python terminal chat client that generates text by repeatedly feeding the conversation and draft back to a stateless choice/rating model, with TypeSafe HTTP, command, and manual backends, resumable sessions, and a 154,844-word lexicon.

name: jev-zenfeed
description: Open-source Chrome MV3 extension that uses the Jev AI to collapse or blur unwanted Facebook posts (ads, spoilers, drama, scams) per user-defined natural-language criteria and whitelists, with sub-200ms decisions, BYOK privacy, zero layout shift, and IndexedDB caching.

name: jev-ego
description: jev-ego is a TypeScript browser agent that drives ego lite via Jev's indexed action space, turning page snapshots into numbered element tables and executing CLICK/TYPE_TEXT/SELECT through single-request TypeSafe decisions inside one Node/CDP process—no Chrome or Playwright.

name: jev-system-one
description: jev-system-one is a terminal interface that uses LangGraph to let TypeSafe Jev set response policy, review OpenAI drafts, and trigger autonomous clarification/revision while presenting each answer beside its typed decision trail.

name: measuretwice
description: measuretwice lets you define, inspect, and revise AI judgments: you write readable checks over supplied evidence, an evaluator answers them, and decision rules with calibrated profiles map answers to pass/fail/review outcomes recorded in inspectable reports.

name: jev-dsh-decision
description: Brings TypeSafe AI's Jev structured decision model to DeepSeek Harness natively and OpenCode/Codex via iPolloWork, adding status, connection-test, and evaluate tools that recommend tools, Skills, and task owners with probabilities while the host agent keeps planning/execution.

name: Jevometry
description: Jevometry is an offline Python toolkit for measuring the information geometry of Jev agent decisions—entropy, divergences, Fisher pullback metrics, aggregation information loss, and Cramér–Rao bounds—under explicit statistical contracts that refuse uncomputable results.

name: jev-use
description: jev-use is a macOS voice and typed command agent that performs on-screen actions via the Accessibility tree (no screenshots), offering customizable shortcuts, continuous hands-free listening with optional "Hey Jev" wake phrase, silence recovery, and multi-step task automation driven by an LLM action-selection loop.

name: TypeSafe.Sdk.C-
description: An unofficial C# port of TypeSafe AI's official Python/JavaScript SDKs (v0.6.0) targeting net10.0 with AOT/trim compatibility, providing an async client that submits Content states and Noul/Choice/Score questions with retries, typed error mapping, logging, and mockable interfaces.

name: foreman
description: Foreman is a Python asyncio supervisory runtime that pairs Codex coding workers with TypeSafe's Jev decision model, streaming factory events into ten probabilistic assessments so a deterministic policy can steer, retry, verify, finish, or escalate work without interrupting the agent.

name: GroundingJev
description: GroundingJev is a non-autoregressive visual grounding model that replaces autoregressive coordinate decoding with single-pass bounding-box regression via a lightweight MLP head on Qwen3.5-0.8B, yielding ~8.6× faster inference and higher RefCOCO accuracy.

name: Jev
description: An unofficial companion repo for TypeSafe's Jev System One decision model, bundling an interactive operator lab, TypeScript harness CLI, progressive examples, and agent skills that teach Choice/Score/Noul primitives, parallel fan-out, confidence routing, and guardrails.

name: jev-compaction-harnesses
description: Extensions for pi (and senpi) and opencode that compact agent context by having TypeSafe's Jev model judge each old tool call keep-or-drop, deleting or truncating stale calls instead of summarizing, preserving messages verbatim while falling back to builtin compaction.

name: jevguard-mcp
description: JevGuard MCP is a zero-dependency Python stdio server exposing deterministic guardrail tools—command safety gating, patch auditing, and calibrated decision evaluation with neutral escape options—backed by a local SQLite cache that masks volatile keys to avoid redundant upstream API calls.

name: jev-call-router
description: A TypeScript/Bun service that sits between a PBX (Asterisk/FreePBX via ARI) and call destinations, using Jev to classify transcribed caller speech into predefined routes with confidence thresholds, deterministic overrides, and guaranteed fallbacks — so natural-language call routing replaces keypad IVR without giving an LLM direct PBX control.

name: jev-builder
description: jev-builder is a local, no-install static browser form for composing requests to TypeSafe's Jev: pick a template, fill in the blanks, and copy the generated request without writing JSON or running a build.

name: Pyro
description: Pyro is a self-hosted prompt monitoring and protection service that evaluates untrusted input through fast local rules and configurable semantic detectors powered by System One models, producing explicit allow/review/block decisions with tunable thresholds, shadow-mode policy testing, and a dashboard for tracing every decision's signals, cost, and latency.

name: openJev-verdict-2.0
description: openJev-verdict-2.0 is a 149.6M-parameter non-autoregressive decision model (ModernBERT-base) that evaluates typed schemas (Choice, Score, Noul) in ~20–25 ms single forward passes with dual-channel calibrated confidence, reaching 77.10% accuracy on 2,000 held-out typed-decisions while enabling selective human-escalation gating, permutation-robust outputs, and in-browser WebGPU inference under 60

name: piedpiper-jev-buildathon
description: Guardrail policies for the Helix ITSM agent that vet every tool call—blocking credential leaks, unauthorized privilege grants, production changes during change freezes, and account deletions while redirecting denials to correct procedures—yielding zero harmful actions across 100+ runs.

name: jev-clean
description: jev-clean is an experimental CSV-cleaning tool that combines deterministic profiling, bounded repair generation, Jev probability-based approval, immutable snapshots, offline replay, and rollback to produce auditable, conservative data repairs.

name: pi-fast-jev-compaction
description: A Pi 0.85.1 extension that prunes stale tool-call history via TypeSafe Jev keep/drop_result/drop_call decisions while preserving verbatim conversation text, storing append-only session decisions, and failing open to Pi's built-in summary compaction without ever rewriting the session file.

name: Vej
description: Vej runs small NLI cross-encoders locally—in a browser tab or as a Node server—to answer yes/no, choice, and rubric-score questions with calibrated probabilities in ~150 ms, matching the TypeSafe API on the wire and routing each question to the strongest model.

name: Rime-Capsule-AI
description: Rime-Capsule-AI is a Windows-ready Rime/Weasel input-method package that bundles the Wanxiang pinyin dictionaries and a 400MB grammar model, adds Tab-key AI candidate re-ranking via TypeSafe Jev AI or local Ollama, and provides a web-based macOS-styled control panel for themes, shortcuts, custom phrases, and one-click deployment.

name: reticle
description: Reticle is an MCP server that lets coding agents verify their work by driving your real running app—reading DOM, network, console, state stores, and React internals—and returning pass/fail/unknown verdicts with evidence and file:line, catching silent failures (500s, state/UI mismatches, double-submits) that screenshots miss, with replayable flows that re-verify without a model in the loop.

name: jev-rag-benchmark
description: A reproducible, vendor-neutral benchmarking CLI for a small RAG stack that measures whether Jev improves retrieval, reranking, and generated answers, using locked datasets, ablations, and quality/latency/cost metrics to support deployment decisions.

name: intelliprompter
description: A browser teleprompter that scores each talking point against a live transcript via Jev, checks off covered topics in any order, supports manual typing, browser-local API keys, and terminal replay, keeping improvised presentations complete for fractions of a cent per run.

name: jev-codex-pilot
description: A local workspace for coordinating multiple Codex projects from one interface, recording recommended model and reasoning level per task, running separate sessions, tracking progress, verification, token usage, session costs, and AGENTS.md context.

name: JevTown
description: JevTown is a browser-based pixel-art game engine (forked from a16z's ai-town) where AI agents autonomously live and converse: a System One "Jev" model makes structured decisions from valid options while an LLM handles dialogue, memory, and beliefs, with a local proxy keeping model keys server-side.

name: pilot-typesafeai-jev
description: A pilot project that integrates TypeSafe AI's Jev—a model returning typed answers with probabilities—into LangGraph and Deep Agents for confidence-scored routing, guardrails, and claim verification, with ChatGPT, NVIDIA NIM, or LM Studio backends and executed notebooks documenting measured results.

name: jive
description: Jive is an open-source agent that replaces the linear LLM→tool-call loop with DAG-based "graph calls" mixing tool calls and fast System One (Jev) decisions, delivering dramatically faster, more token-efficient bulk evaluation, profiling, and repetitive engineering tasks.

name: jev-trader-solana
description: jev-trader-solana is a dry-run multi-venue SOL taker trader on Solana that polls Jupiter, DFlow, and Imperial Phoenix quotes each cycle, delegates operation/slippage choices to a JEV bridge, and simulates fills under deterministic routing and fail-closed risk gates—without wallets, signing, or live orders.

name: LLPhant
description: LLPhant is a PHP 8.1+ framework for building generative AI applications and vector database (RAG) workflows, offering a simple API that integrates with Symfony and Laravel and supports LLM providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Ollama, LM Studio, and OpenAI-compatible services like LocalAI.

name: pi-jev-router
description: A Pi extension that routes each session to a model and reasoning effort chosen once by TypeSafe's Jev (via Vercel AI Gateway), then pins both while optionally suggesting forks, auto-loading matching skills, and chunking long prompts — using your existing Pi providers and credentials.

name: jev-btc-test
description: Benchmark repo testing whether TypeSafe AI's Jev model predicts the next BTCUSDT 5-minute candle from technical indicators as well as gradient boosting on identical inputs (it doesn't — Jev reads mean-reverting signals as continuation), with fully reproducible scripts.

name: jev
description: A Claude Code plugin that answers codebase questions without loading files into the agent's context: `jev find` locates code semantically, `jev ask` runs yes/no audits across directories, and a Read hook narrows large files—cutting billed tokens ~30–41% in measured runs.

name: jev-auto-approve
description: A GitHub Action that asks the Jev decision model typed yes/no questions about a pull request (merge-readiness, test coverage, whether a human reviewer is needed) and approves only when every calibrated answer clears a configurable confidence threshold, otherwise commenting with the per-question numbers.

name: jev-adblock
description: Jev Ad Blocker is a free, open-source Chrome Manifest V3 extension that blocks ads without filter lists by sending compact structural descriptions of each ad-looking element to TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model—using your own API key—and hiding elements whose batched, per-category ad probabilities clear configurable thresholds, with caching, pre-paint CSS rules, a daily token budget, and fail-o

name: typesafe-sdk-java
description: A zero-dependency Java 21+ client for the TypeSafe AI System One API that turns natural language and application state into typed judgments—yes/no probabilities, choices with distributions, rubric scores—with retries, async calls, sealed answers, and typed exceptions.

name: composable-jev
description: composable-jev is a PHP/JavaScript/Python library for chaining Jev calls into composable graphs where probabilistic questions, choices, and scores over a shared context feed into rules, gates, and batched requests, enabling multi-step LLM-style reasoning pipelines like ticket triage with token-efficient batching and cross-language result caching.

name: ReckoNim
description: ReckoNim is a Nim library that batches inline `feels`/`choice`/`score` questions about shared state into a single TypeSafe Jev request via a compile-time `withState` macro, offering checked focus paths, typed judgments, concurrent per-record requests, and error separation.

name: typesafe-ai-firewall
description: Shadow-mode validation harness for a pre-execution firewall on AI agent tool calls, using TypeSafe/Jev's five decomposed typed hazard judgments batched in one call with auditable policy-code decisions, achieving 100% synthetic attack catch and 0% hard-negative block rates at $0.0000365/call, plus offline threshold replay.

name: omarchy-jev
description: omarchy-jev is a bounded CLI/JavaScript library that drives Omarchy desktops (Hyprland windows, Nautilus, terminal, Chromium, filesystem) by letting TypeSafe JEV select from a fixed set of pre-approved actions executed via native APIs with verified results—no screenshots, shell commands, or arbitrary input.

name: jev-router
description: jev-router is a loopback proxy that wraps the Claude Code and OpenAI Codex CLIs, sending each fresh user turn to a Jev routing call that picks a fast, balanced, strong, or long model tier while preserving native sessions, tools, auth, and manual model-picker overrides.

name: jev-gateway
description: jev-gateway is a localhost proxy for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Gemini clients that delegates each turn's tool-selection decision to TypeSafe's fast Jev model—steering the main LLM via tool_choice or hints—while safely passing through requests, preserving existing logins/subscriptions, and exposing a dashboard with token, latency, and baseline-comparison metrics.

name: jev-dspy-lab
description: jev-dspy-lab is a reproducible, API-key-free benchmark harness that evaluates TypeSafe/Jev decisions inside DSPy workflows by recording or replaying responses and reporting calibration (Brier, ECE, Platt refit), confidence-gated selective risk, coverage/abstention, latency, and modeled cost with deterministic seeds, hashes, and threshold sweeps.

name: jev-8-ball
description: A Magic 8-ball web app that routes yes/no questions (or GitHub repo context via CodeFundi) through OpenRouter's Decisions API to the TypeSafe Jev-1.13 System One decision model, returning classic 8-ball phrases with calibrated probabilities while billing usage to your own localStorage-stored OpenRouter key.

name: openjev
description: Open-source, Jev-compatible "System One" decision server: answers typed questions (yes/no, choice, score) about a state or images with calibrated probabilities in tens of milliseconds, plus OpenAI-compatible text generation, served by DiffusionGemma via vLLM.

name: jev-mute-words
description: jev-mute-words is a tool that mutes or hides user-specified words and phrases, letting users suppress unwanted terms from the content they see.

name: jev-dino
description: JEV × Dino is a Node.js/TypeScript experiment that connects an asynchronous AI decision service to the unmodified Chromium dinosaur game—selecting actions at 10 Hz while local code handles jump timing via original physics—achieving a recorded 13,724-point run with inspectable metrics, video evidence, and a verified-unchanged upstream codebase.

name: typesafe-ai-rust-sdk
description: An unofficial Rust SDK for the TypeSafe AI API, ported from the official JavaScript SDK, offering a builder-based `TypeSafeClient` with environment-variable configuration, `system_one` calls returning answers as a tagged `Answer` enum (`noul`, `score`, `choice`), `tokio_util` cancellation, and error types carrying request IDs, status, and headers.

name: jev-router
description: jev-router is a TypeScript package that routes each query to the cheapest adequate LLM: it uses Jev (via a TypeSafe API key) to estimate the required capability tier, then picks the model minimizing expected loss from normalized cost plus a quadratic under-capability penalty.

name: system-one
description: system-one turns any LLM into a fast general-purpose decision engine that answers multiple multiple-choice questions about an input in a single batched forward pass, using constrained logit sampling over prefilled choice indexes.

name: signal-weave
description: SignalWeave is an open-source Python MCP/webhook service that converts free-form insight cards plus bounded evidence from source adapters (Superset, Trino) into typed, evidence-backed decisions via TypeSafe Jev, while callers own scheduling, delivery, permissions, and side effects.

name: zio-typesafe-ai
description: A Scala 3/ZIO client for TypeSafe AI's Jev System One API that returns typed answers to atomic questions (noul, choice, score) about state via NamedTuples, with validated criteria, bounded probabilities, state-machine loops, and typed errors.

name: omp-cua-jev
description: An OMP plugin that reuses the host's configured `judge` role to pick actions from a local table and execute/verify authorized GUI actions through Cua Driver, shipping diagnostics commands, absolute helper paths for stock JS eval, a bundled skill, and an isolated localhost demo—without installing a model client or separate credentials.

name: JEV-27B-DEMO
description: JEV-27B-DEMO is a demo repository for the JEV-27B model, showing how one vLLM engine serves both a fast "System 1" decision head returning calibrated probabilities in ~0.1s and the full Qwen-based "System 2" reasoner, with ten measured benchmarks (re-ranking, judging, recommendation, QA) and a Gradio app.

name: jod
