description: jod binds a Standard Schema–validated TypeScript state to semantic questions (choice, score, noul), answers them in one parallel Jev request via the official SDK, and projects results into typed domain values with confidence scores, probabilities, and deterministic fixtures.

name: typesafe-migration-guard
description: Typesafe Migration Guard is a CI/CD safety gatekeeper that uses the TypeSafe AI Jev model to evaluate SQL migrations in ~250ms, returning calibrated SAFE/DANGER verdicts and blocking destructive DDL like DROP TABLE in production with HTTP 403 before it reaches a Supabase PostgreSQL database.

name: jev-voice-computer-use
description: A Windows utility that executes spoken commands hands-free—hold Right Ctrl, speak, and it performs multi-step tasks by driving apps through UI Automation controls (no screenshots), typing only words you dictated via TypeSafe's Jev decision model, with local faster-whisper transcription and confirmation prompts before destructive clicks.

name: ollaya
description: Ollaya is an Ollama-style local CLI and daemon that pulls and serves open decision models, returning calibrated probabilities for typed questions over arbitrary JSON in milliseconds through TypeSafe-compatible, native HTTP, and MCP interfaces.

name: ruby_llm-typesafe
description: A RubyLLM 2 provider gem that integrates TypeSafe's Jev model, letting Ruby apps batch typed questions (Noul, Choice, Score primitives) over a single string or JSON state and receive probability-based, machine-actionable answers through RubyLLM's structured output API.

name: minecraft-agent
description: An autonomous Minecraft Java 1.16.5 speedrun agent that pairs an Astra/Sol planner with JEV action selection via Mineflayer, plus a read-only dragon sensor and hidden native-client recorder that produce verifiable evidence of a deathless 8:43 full-game completion.

name: jev-voice-browser
description: A Node app that voice-controls a headed Chromium browser via Playwright, streaming partial speech transcripts to a server that asks the Jev model typed questions (intent, target, completeness, destructiveness) each update (~300 ms) so it can act mid-sentence.

name: pytest-jev
description: pytest-jev is a pytest plugin that asserts on the semantic meaning of LLM app outputs using TypeSafe's Jev model, which returns calibrated probabilities rather than text; its `jev` fixture checks claims via `holds`, `lacks`, `expect`, `context`, `choice`, and `score` methods, batching all claims per text into one cached request with configurable thresholds.

name: jevort
description: Jevort is a Pi extension that sends each prompt to TypeSafe’s Jev model to recommend an appropriate reasoning-effort tier, maps it to the active model’s supported thinking levels, and can notify or automatically apply it, helping match compute to task complexity.

name: jev-patterns
description: An experiment plus ~100-line TypeScript wrapper that detects repeating patterns in noisy sequences by splitting labor between code and TypeSafe's Jev model: code mines candidate units by counting, Jev makes one independent semantic judgment per candidate, turning 85 compounding failed queries into 2 correct ones.

name: jev-workflow-builder
description: A demo that implements a multiplayer Jev workflow builder with Liveblocks, wiring Jev to LLMs so users can invoke workflows through a REST API, preview test runs, and observe shared state and cursors.

name: failproofai-sub
description: Buildathon CLI and repo providing four deliberately unsafe agents (IT, legal, health, finance domains), letting you run scripted tasks, diagnose failures with Jev evaluations, and enforce real-time syntactic or semantic policies that block or redirect harmful tool calls.

name: jev-reviewer
description: Browser-based systematic review tool that answers extraction-form questions across a study's files (PDF, Word, Excel, slides, etc.) with verbatim, located quotes selected—not generated—by the Jev model, plus checking, an extraction table, PRISMA reporting, and local-only storage.

name: jev-browser-agent
description: An installable agent skill plus pilot scripts that graft TypeSafe's Jev System One model onto the ego-browser skill so each browser step's decision—which operation and which element—resolves in ~280–740 ms at near-zero cost, guarded by prompt-injection, URL-safety, and confidence-escalation rules.

name: jev-guard
description: jev-guard vets an LLM agent's tool calls through one cheap, confidence-aware Jev semantic check before execution—allowing safe calls, blocking destructive ones, and holding uncertain ones—with policy presets, verdict caching, audit logging, and LangChain/Vercel AI SDK adapters.

name: switchyard
description: Switchyard is a macOS menu-bar app that acts as the default browser and routes every clicked link into the correct Dia profile using fast local rules, falling back to TypeSafe's Jev model—which sends only host, path segments, and parameter names—to learn new rules automatically.

name: crypto-arbitrage-bot
description: A cross-exchange crypto spot-arbitrage bot polling 11 venues for fee-aware ask→bid spreads and gating every order through a strict no-fallback TypeSafe Jev decision model, trading on Binance/OKX/MEXC with mock mode on by default and a monitoring dashboard.

name: antseed
description: Antseed is a peer-to-peer AI services network where providers announce LLM capacity via DHT and buyers proxy requests through encrypted P2P connections via a local HTTP endpoint that drop-in replaces ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/OPENAI_BASE_URL, with on-chain USDC payments.

name: jev-kano
description: A Node.js romance adventure game where the Jev judgment model decides the heroine's true feelings in ~0.2–0.5s to drive her facial expression and one-line reaction first, Claude writes the follow-up dialogue, and Gemini TTS voices it, with graceful degradation when keys or quotas are missing.

name: jevcache
description: jevcache is a local OpenAI-compatible proxy that caches chat completions by using TypeSafe Jev's calibrated same-intent matching—rather than cosine similarity—to reuse answers for paraphrased queries, cutting redundant LLM costs and latency while failing open to the upstream model on errors.

name: jev-macos-loop
description: Jev macOS Loop is an open-source Apple-silicon tool for native macOS GUI automation that uses local CoreML detection, OCR, and accessibility with Jev decisions while keeping screenshots and coordinates on-device.

name: super-jev
description: Super Jev is an agent-side judge layer between an LLM agent and local data that finds relevant files for natural-language questions, verifies claims against evidence files, gates actions with a hard-rule permit check, and caches only user-approved answers.

name: myNameisJevToo
description: An MLX/llama.cpp-backed tool that exposes local decoder-only LLMs as a typed decision API (POST /v1/systemone), returning choice, yes/no, and scored answers from a single forward-pass readout of option-letter probabilities, with benchmarked JevBench results, position-bias checks, and observability diagnostics.

name: open-alternative-jev
description: An open-source alternative to TypeSafe’s Jev, it provides a System One-style model layer that turns any open-weights LLM (via Hugging Face or vLLM) into a single-forward-pass engine for typed, calibrated decisions, with benchmarks to evaluate its claims.

name: jev-gamepilot
description: jev-gamepilot is an autonomous AI gaming agent that captures any live Windows game (browser, Steam, or emulator) at 60+ FPS, queries TypeSafe's Jev System One model for tactical decisions via built-in or custom profiles, and executes real keyboard/mouse inputs with emergency stop fail-safes.

name: typesafe-ai-go-sdk
description: Archived Go SDK (moved to latere.ai/x/pkg/typesafeai) for the TypeSafe API: evaluates content against typed noul/choice/score questions in one request, with typed answer accessors, retries, timeouts, structured errors, and runnable examples.

name: jev-playground
description: MoonBit playground for TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model, bundling a typed API client with CLIs and experiments—single questions, Jev-vs-Jev Gomoku with real-time GIF replay, shell-risk gating, a 3v3 MOBA, an ESLint plugin, Claude Code permission hook, jevdsl/jevlang DSLs, and measured pattern reports.

name: Jev-X-Sentiment-Analysis
description: A FastAPI web terminal that analyzes a chosen crypto symbol against 50–1,000 tweets via a two-tier pipeline (statistical pre-processing plus early-stopping SQLite deduplication to cut API costs) and TypeSafe's Jev System One model, fusing Twitter sentiment with CCXT price, volume, RSI, funding-rate, and open-interest data to output a calibrated decision card (Strong Buy–Strong Sell) with entry

name: qualm
description: Qualm is a local-first screen-time app for Apple silicon Macs that runs an on-device model (or hosted Jev) to classify each screen against plain-language rules, interrupting endless feeds, shorts, and livestreams with explanatory pop-ups and check-ins while leaving work and learning alone.

name: jev-ops
description: A Rust CLI that pipes unstructured operational signals (logs, journal entries, Kubernetes events, cloud telemetry) through declarative, security-sandboxed YAML diagnostic packs to TypeSafe Jev inference, returning typed probabilistic decisions (category, severity, attention) with confidence scores for gating alerts and auto-remediation.

name: pg-redact
description: A Next.js demo of content-aware PII redaction in a Neon Postgres support inbox, where TypeSafe's Jev model classifies text spans (name, email, phone, etc.) with calibrated confidence and a `redact()` SQL function enforces role-based clearance so unauthorized data never reaches the browser.

name: snifftest
description: A command-line prose linter that checks Markdown and text drafts against regex-based countable rules locally and opt-in judgment rules scored per-paragraph by a hosted model only after explicit consent, flagging style problems for you to fix without rewriting your text.

name: vibecheck
description: vibecheck is a Python library (`vibecheck-py`) that exposes AI decision models as four async or sync functions — `check`, `classify`, `label`, and `score` — returning typed values with probabilities, thresholds, and batching for fast, cheap judgment calls like intent detection, triage, and rating without prompt templating or text parsing.

name: jev-deterministic-benchmark
description: A reproducible benchmark harness for evaluating the `jev-latest` model on 1,000 deterministic decisions across 25 reasoning families, providing a multi-channel runner, offline test suite, raw result CSVs, confidence-calibration analysis, failure-mode diagnostics, charts, and an interactive dashboard.

name: nl-logic-interpreter
description: A step-through Prolog-style logic interpreter that proves goals by SLD resolution over facts and rules written in plain English, using TypeSafe's Jev model for semantic unification so differently worded statements of the same fact still match and bind variables.

name: jev-intent-review
description: jev-intent-review is a CLI/GitHub Action that checks whether a pull request satisfies its stated requirements by looking beyond the diff—into touched functions, their callers, and sibling callers—asking Jev typed questions per call and sorting findings for human review.

name: kg-jev
description: kgqa is a System One routing layer for knowledge-graph QA: a fast typed controller (jev) makes confidence-gated choices of graph, class, query shape, and schema path, then templates or an LLM emit small SPARQL queries executed across named-graph boundaries.

name: jev_test
description: A Flutter order-support app where Jev picks among six UI screens and known order IDs via typed choices, GenUI renders interactive order, tracking, and return cards from approved templates, and buttons act locally without extra model calls or refunds.

name: egolite-jev
description: A companion runner for ego lite that executes goal-driven browser automation—listing ranked on-page controls, clicking inside a single ego-browser process, and verifying success by URL/title match—returning JSON without dumping page snapshots into the coding model.

name: Edward
description: Edward is a zero-dependency Python supervisor that wraps unattended coding agents, detects cross-turn failures like retry loops, stalls, budget bleed, and dangerous commands, and issues resumable PAUSE/CANCEL/BLOCK interventions with signed Ed25519 audit receipts.

name: mastra-jev-moderation
description: A drop-in Mastra `Processor` that moderates the last user message via TypeSafe Jev's typed yes/no verdict in one HTTP call, blocking at a configurable probability threshold and failing open on errors through a circuit breaker, eliminating LLM text-parsing failures.

name: hello-zio-typesafe-ai
description: A Scala 3 benchmark that runs one Jackson documentation task against the live javadocs.dev MCP catalog under three designs—direct LLM agent, nested Jev evidence tool, and top-level Jev plan/no-plan loops—to compare filter/fanout safety, MCP calls, token use, and latency.

name: jev-audio-beeper
description: TypeScript CLI POC that flags Spanish profanity in audio by scoring timestamped ASR words with Jev's typed Boolean/severity evaluations, then ffmpeg-overlays beeps on padded intervals without changing duration, emitting censored WAV plus a JSON audit report.

name: typesafe-ai-rs
description: Independent Rust client for the TypeSafe AI System One API providing async and blocking clients, typed Noul/Choice/Score questions, model discovery, configurable retries and cancellation, raw HTTP metadata, and typed errors, tracking the official Python/JavaScript SDKs at v0.6.0.

name: pi-jev
description: pi-jev is a Pi coding-agent extension that uses TypeSafe Jev to semantically activate only needed tools, match skills, run fast typed decisions, auto-select models, gate subagent output, orchestrate agent workflows, and guide compaction — opt-in, with graceful fallbacks.

name: jev-monid-poc
description: Three runnable Node.js proof-of-concept scripts demonstrate using Jev’s typed decisions to guard, deterministically route, and verify paid Monid API calls, including async polling, cost normalization, and verified live runs.

name: jev-shooter
description: A browser-based 3D neon arena wave shooter where every enemy's chase/flank/retreat tactic (and optionally the player's moves) is decided by TypeSafe's Jev model via one batched, probability-typed call per tick, with a local API-key proxy, offline mock mode, confidence-gated fallbacks, and live-editable AI prompts and state fields.

name: Helm
description: Helm is a standard-library Python orchestration layer that inventories installed coding agents and auth state, uses TypeSafe Jev’s cheap typed decisions to select and tune the safest agent for each task, then supervises execution and judges completion rather than trusting exit codes.

name: jev-fuse
description: JEV Fuse is a drop-in governance gateway/proxy between AI agents and TypeSafe Jev (or local Laya) decision models that converts raw calibrated probabilities into deterministic actions (ALLOW/ASK/DENY/etc.) via a 4-tier AST/denylist/allowlist/model pipeline with deadband abstention, plus singleflight deduplication, micro-caching, MCP/Claude Code integrations, and a tamper-evident audit trail.

name: jev-runtime-security
description: Linux runtime security for AI coding agents that enforces deterministic policy in the kernel via eBPF/LSM—refusing protected-file operations at the syscall, recording exec/network events, and optionally gating egress—below the agent, which can never loosen a verdict.

name: jev-page-checker
description: A Chrome extension whose Inspector sidebar follows the active tab, using TypeSafe's Jev to audit each page's publisher identity and intent plus category-specific body checks, producing evidence-cited Pass/Review/Alert verdicts without blocking, publishing, or leaking the page.

name: JevScout
description: JevScout is a CLI-driven coding-agent skill that hunts AI/software jobs on real company sites by driving visible Chrome over CDP and delegating all link-clicking and job-scoring decisions to Jev (TypeSafe System One), with mock and fixture-based demo modes.

name: typesafe-offload-bench
description: Benchmark comparing direct, relay, and code-owned cascade workflows to show when offloading typed judgments to a small model saves coding agents time and tokens, with 100 frozen synthetic cases, offline evidence auditing, and a live runner for newer TypeSafe models.

name: JevBenchmarkLab
description: A TypeScript/React benchmark that measures TypeSafe Jev decision accuracy and run-to-run consistency over 200 choice/noul/score tests, tracking option-order bias, answer flips, probability drift, latency, token use, and persistent JSON run records.

name: typesafe-cli
description: typesafe-cli is a Python 3.9+ stdlib-only command-line tool and agent skill that calls the TypeSafe System One API to evaluate a given state against typed Choice/Score/Noul questions, returning structured, non-generative answers for routing, classification, scoring, and guardrails in code.

name: typed-decisions
description: Reproduces Jev's typed-decision shape—many Choice/Score/Noul questions on one program state answered with calibrated probability distributions in a single forward pass—and benchmarks encoder (ModernBERT/DeBERTa) vs diffusion-LLM (LLaDA-MoE) backbones for accuracy, latency, and training cost.

name: grok-build-Jev
description: Grok Build is a Rust terminal AI coding agent (full-screen TUI, headless/scriptable, ACP-embeddable) that edits files, runs shell commands, and searches the web, forked to add TypeSafe Jev as a fast System 1 layer for reasoning-effort allocation, output distillation, and tool safety gating.

name: typesafe-snake
description: A real-time Snake game where TypeSafe's Jev decision model picks each move from code-generated legal options with exact facts (food distance, flood-fill reachable cells, dead ends), defaulting to straight ahead if the answer misses the tick deadline, served via a Hono proxy and dark canvas dashboard.

name: jev-one
description: Jev One is a TypeScript/ESM library for building stateful applications where TypeSafe AI's Jev model answers by pointing to developer-supplied choices—vocabularies, numbered items, capabilities, controls—whose effects a runtime applies and observes until a goal is verified.

name: veil
description: Veil is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension (vanilla JS, no build step) that sends X/Twitter reply text plus a plain-language filter condition to the Jev API using your own TypeSafe key, then locally hides replies whose Noul score meets your threshold, with request caching, retries, and a live hidden-count badge.

name: genai
description: genai is a strictly-typed, stateless Go client library for many LLM providers that offers reflection-based tool calling, struct-driven JSON output, iterator-based streaming, multimodal input/output, web search, rate-limit and usage reporting, and HTTP-level recording for reproducible tests.

name: jev-ncr-demo
description: jev-ncr-demo is a demonstration tool that uses TypeSafe AI's Jev model to generate AI-powered defect code suggestions for Non-Conformance Reports, helping quality teams classify product defects faster and more consistently.

name: dwim
description: DWIM is a macOS menu-bar utility that lets you tap a hotkey, describe an action in plain words, and have the Jev decision model rank the frontmost app's menu items via the accessibility API and trigger the match—no per-app setup required.

name: JevSwiftSDK
description: A dependency-free Swift package wrapping TypeSafe's Jev decision-model HTTP API, providing a Sendable async client that evaluates state against typed Choice, Score, and Noul questions—individually, in batches, or via reusable question sets—with environment or explicit configuration, retries, per-request options, structured JSON state, and granular error handling.

name: jev-mail
description: A read-only Chrome extension that scores Gmail messages with TypeSafe's Jev model for category, priority, spam %, and reply-needed %, displaying verdicts as inline thread-list badges or in a sortable, filterable, CSV-exportable dashboard table.

name: jev-triage
description: A Probot-based GitHub App that uses Jev's typed-question API to classify, score, deduplicate, and label incoming issues and PRs, escalating uncertain decisions to humans, alerting Slack/Discord/Telegram, and logging corrections in SQLite for accuracy reporting.

name: clawd-jev-trading-machine
description: A dry-run-only Solana trading machine that runs a typed JEV decision per cycle over a dynamically probed venue action space (Jupiter, DFlow, pump.fun, Backpack) with CoinGecko regime and Supermemory context, simulating fills and replays—never signing or broadcasting orders.

name: ruby_llm-llm_judge
description: A Ruby gem that uses any RubyLLM chat model to answer RubyLLM Judge `probability`, `choice`, and `score` questions, returning native typed `Judgment` answers via either parallel per-answer 0–9 ratings with softmax and tie-breaking or a single validated JSON distribution call, with retries, token accounting, and request caps.

name: jev
description: jev is a Go CLI that pipes stdin state into a single Jev evaluation question—noul, choice, or score primitives—across TypeSafe AI, Cloudflare, or Vercel providers, returning machine-readable JSON so shell pipelines and CI jobs can gate on model judgments via exit codes and thresholds.

name: reelql
description: ReelQL turns any public video link into a single timestamped JSON document — summary, chapters, scenes, key moments, emotional arc, products, on-screen text and transcript — so agents and code can analyze, rank and branch on video content.

name: jev
description: A Go client library for the TypeSafe System One API and its Jev model that sends a state string or JSON with multiple named questions (yes/no probabilities, multi-option choices, ordered-level scores) in one call, returning typed answers with probabilities, plus built-in rate limiting, retries, structured error sentinels, and struct decoding.

name: gem-search
description: Local-first Chrome extension and Python backend whose animated spider overlay captures posts visible on your X feed, groups topics and links, crawls public sources, runs local checks and optional four-role Grok reviews, and surfaces evidence-linked findings on a dashboard.

name: skillbox
description: Skillbox is a self-hosted, versioned skills library for AI agents that combines Markdown editing, immutable revisions, scoped permissions, revocable client keys, MCP/CLI access, imports/backups, and optional model-backed recommendations to manage, distribute, and audit reusable agent skills.

name: slop-filter
description: A Chrome extension that hides AI-generated posts and comments on X, LinkedIn, Reddit, and YouTube by scoring each post with 19 probability-only writing-pattern checks plus textual tells, collapsing entries above a user-set threshold with weights fittable from the user's own AI/Human labels.

name: flappy-jev
description: A Next.js Flappy Bird arena that runs identical seeded boards for you and TypeSafe’s Jev, turning raw game state into server-side FLAP/NONE decisions with live confidence so you can race a typed, non-hardcoded AI pilot.

name: jev-seo
description: A free Rust CLI and 15-tool MCP server that audits local files and live sites under 58 SEO rules, scores AI answer-engine citation readiness, tracks rank drift in SQLite, and gates CI—giving devs and agents SEO checks without a subscription.

name: SpiderSense
description: SpiderSense is a fail-closed control plane that sits outside a service-desk agent at the tool boundary and decides whether password resets, MFA resets, or new-factor enrollments may execute, enforcing rule-based policies via Jev/OpenRouter with attack blocking, red-team evaluation, and Failure-to-policy mining against an in-memory mock enterprise.

name: naza-jev-research
description: NAZA JEB Local is a hardened terminal client that routes NAZA's local Llama/GGUF path to TypeSafe's Jev System One model via direct httpx calls to api.typesafe.ai, providing typed road/food-water classifications and JSON evaluations with AES-256-GCM-encrypted, HMAC-chained local history, permission-checked storage, hash-locked dependencies, and no inbound socket or SDK.

name: agents-mail
description: Agents Mail is a Cloudflare Workers/D1/R2 mailbox for AI agents that receives catch-all email on a dedicated domain and exposes search, read, wait, send, reply, and forward operations over MCP or a token-authenticated REST API, with optional spam/prompt-injection labeling and retention cleanup.

name: jev-the-janitor
description: A Python CLI that triages markdown vaults by asking the TypeSafe Jev API which bucket each note belongs in—redacting content locally, estimating cost before sending, quarantining suspected secrets, and stamping frontmatter without ever deleting or rewriting a note.

name: crossTagWithJev
description: crossTagWithJev is an early-stage tool that automates identification and disambiguation tagging of closely-spaced satellites by analyzing ground-sensor observations — optical photometry/light curves, angle tracks, and RF signatures — rather than relying on orbital propagation alone.

name: jev-robot-control
description: MuJoCo toolkit for direct Cartesian LLM control of an xArm7 arm on an apple-to-plate pick-and-place task, bundling recorded multi-controller trials, an offline hash-and-physics trajectory verifier, synchronized three-way replay, and scripts for running fresh OpenRouter-controlled trials.

name: hermes-jev-router
description: A Hermes plugin that routes each LLM call through TypeSafe Jev to pick cheaper or stronger models with primary-model fallback, enforces trim-before-compress context handling, and optionally adds fail-closed Jev auto-approval, event logging, and local install/config toggles.

name: jev-browser
description: Jev-browser drives a headless browser via MCP server, CLI, or library, with TypeSafe's Jev model choosing one action per step while code enforces budgets and stop gates, returning the final page, a step trace with confidences, errors, and a screenshot at sub-cent cost.

name: mcts-agent
description: A closed-loop autonomous agent that couples discriminative Monte Carlo Tree Search with TypeSafe Jev primitives (Noul, Choice, Score) for batched action pruning, policy priors, and state-value scoring while Gemini generates candidate actions, plus a D3.js tree-replay visualizer and headless JSON CLI modes.

name: robojev
description: Drive a Trossen WidowX arm or MuJoCo sim from natural language and live standing orders: code renders a situation report, asks the Jev model typed judgments ~10x/sec via event-driven requests, and composes answers into verified arm commands with safety overrides.

name: antivirus
description: Jev-AV is an AI-powered antivirus and EDR scanner that analyzes files, URLs, and live Windows processes for threats via structural feature extraction and calibrated verdicts, offering real-time folder protection, quarantine, bulk triage, and GUI/CLI access.

name: jev-arena
description: Jev Arena is a calibration benchmarking tool that poses batched questions about analytically exact stochastic worlds to TypeSafe Jev, collecting its native probability outputs to score honesty via Brier, log loss, ECE, reliability curves, and risk-coverage tables — with offline oracle/miscalibrated stubs for verification.

name: jev-realtime-brain-scanner
description: jev-realtime-brain-scanner is a macOS web application that turns live Japanese speech into a continuously updating “Nounai Maker” profile-head diagram, using local Apple SpeechAnalyzer captions, TypeSafe Jev probability judgments, smoothing, and p5.js rendering.

name: jev-cua
description: Jev Voice is an open-source macOS app whose floating bar turns continuous spoken or typed requests into real GUI actions, with the Jev model repeatedly observing live Accessibility controls and choosing each next step until the task completes.

name: typesafe-ai-rails
description: A community Rails integration for TypeSafe AI's System One API that adds configuration, batched question helpers, persisted usage/cost telemetry, and fail-closed confidence policies so Rails apps can safely gate Choice and Score side effects.

name: jev-test-1
description: jev-test-1 is a dependency-free Node.js demo that runs a local TypeSafe Jev evaluation server, submits one customer message to three typed questions (Choice, Noul, Score), and renders structured JSON answers with probability bars while keeping the API key server-side.

name: jev-search-rerank-eval
description: A reproducible graded-relevance benchmark that evaluates whether a TypeSafe Jev rerank improves skill search over the Agent Skills Hub catalog, comparing keyword, BM25, embedding, Jev-rerank, and RRF-fusion systems on 9,831 dual-judge-labelled query–skill pairs with bootstrap confidence intervals and judge-circularity corrections—finding fusion, not standalone reranking, is the real win.

name: jev-use-cases
description: Demo app showcasing Jev-driven UI decisions—intent search, typing interactions, model selection, response depth, JSON rendering, and Twitch moderation—using server-side probability evaluation, confidence tiers, calm-UI hysteresis, and offline keyword fallbacks.

name: TYPESAFE_JEV
description: Python demo tooling for TypeSafe AI's Jev "System One" endpoint, which returns typed decisions (choice, score, or yes/no probability) with calibrated confidence, including a user-upgrade triage script that repeats calls to measure stability and gates on confidence, plus seven example scenarios for routing uncertain cases to human review.

name: live-jev
description: Live Jev is a macOS tool that lets you control Ableton Live 12 by typing or dictating short English or Japanese commands into a ⌘⇧Space bar, using a small model and a Python Remote Script to adjust mixer, transport, clips, notes, devices, and tracks.

name: deepopen
description: An open-source non-autoregressive decision engine that produces typed, statistically calibrated decisions across 100+ languages in a single forward pass, delivering millisecond-level latency and automatic per-request checkpoint routing for intent classification, routing, and scoring workloads.

name: neo4jev
description: neo4jev is a schema-agnostic Python library (with notebooks and a Streamlit app) that navigates any Neo4j graph one hop at a time via TypeSafe's `system_one` API, using beam search over per-hop Choice/Noul probability distributions to find best-scoring paths and render them with `neo4j-viz`.

name: superqode-jev-engineering
description: A hands-on walkthrough for running Jev context selection in the SuperQode TUI: connect a coding model, exercise shadow mode against a synthetic runbook, inspect keep/excerpt decisions, retrieve retained evidence by reference, then enable enforcement.

name: jev-geo-audit
description: A three-script Python toolkit that audits 300 public pages for AI citability with nine cheap Jev decisions each, benchmarks agreement, cost and latency against an LLM judge, and renders a static report of scores and fixes.

name: jev_ampcode
description: An Amp plugin registering `jev_evaluate`, an advisory tool comparing 2–6 supplied candidates against given evidence, priorities, and requirements via a TypeSafe API call, returning a probability distribution and per-candidate requirement judgments for scoped decisions.

name: jevgo
description: jevgo is a dependency-free Go client for TypeSafe AI's System One API and Jev model, letting programs submit a state plus typed Noul/Choice/Score questions and receive validated, typed answers with probabilities and confidence, with functional options, retries, context cancellation, sentinel errors, and optional Langfuse tracing.

name: skibidu
description: A Chibi Scheme tool that live-prompts TypeSafe's Jev model to construct a Scheme program node-by-node from an empty AST—defaulting to a nested `+`/`*` integer calculator—then iteratively rebakes rejected subtrees until every node earns contextual approval and sandboxed acceptance tests pass, with resumable checkpoints and cost reporting.

name: jevgrep
description: jevgrep is a grep-like CLI that filters piped text by meaning — scoring each line with TypeSafe's Jev model against a plain-English yes/no question — supporting grep flags and exit codes, ~0.7 s latency on live streams, ~$0.004 per 1,000 lines, and an --explain summary mode.

name: fm-with-jev
description: A tested guide and demo suite for pairing Apple's free offline fm CLI (titles, short text) with TypeSafe's Jev decisions API (fast, confidence-scored picks from tiers, model lists, and tools), including accuracy benchmarks, latency numbers, and gotchas.

name: JevFish
description: JevFish is an OASIS-based social-simulation runtime that turns seed inputs into agent societies, uses TypeSafe Jev for fast typed multi-action decisions, invokes generative models only when needed, and provides A/B benchmarks and metrics for scalable outcome analysis.

name: moss-jev
description: A static browser demo replaying, at 25 fps, three MuJoCo-recorded missions of the MOSS litter-picking rover whose manipulation steps were chosen by the Jev decision model — plus seven earlier scenarios and a local CPU simulator package — requiring no live inference, API key, or backend.

name: semdecide
description: SemDecide pipes text or JSONL through TypeSafe AI Jev to yield semantic decisions—predicates, option routing, rubric scores, record filtering, and an agent-action guard—with grep-like exit codes distinguishing true, false, uncertain, and provider failure in scripts and CI.

name: nola-typesafe-test
description: A Nola example app that triages tickets by routing typed asks (string/number literal unions, booleans, flat objects) to typesafe.ai's Jev model, with fallback to OpenAI/Cerebras chat models and console traces for side-by-side provider comparison.

name: auto-mode-for-paseo
description: A Paseo plugin that automatically routes each incoming message to the best-matching configurable persona—each with its own provider, model, reasoning effort, task types, depth limit, and instructions—using a Jev API or local Laya classifier.

name: diffjury
description: DiffJury turns a public GitHub PR URL into a one-click TypeSafe Jev judgment, fetching the PR's title, body, diff, and contributors to score merge risk, test gaps, docs debt, and blast radius and flag design, security, or merge-blocking concerns.

name: ROCmFPX
description: A ROCm/HIP llama.cpp server runtime that runs Qwen3.8-27B at 80k context entirely on a 20 GB RX 7900 XT via ROCmFP4 weights, MTP speculative decoding, and an SSD prompt cache that restores swapped-out conversations in seconds for multi-agent use.

name: snake-jev
description: A desktop Snake game where each tick makes one Jev/System One API call answering nine collision-and-food-progress questions for left, straight, and right moves, which Python composes into the snake's next direction, with pause, seeding, and trace controls.

name: webctl
description: webctl is a CLI for AI agents that fans queries out to multiple web search providers, dedupes and relevance-scores results via Jev, and can scrape pages returning only goal-relevant chunks, sharply reducing token usage versus raw search output or full-page reads.

name: jevpilot
description: JevPilot is a minimal browser agent that snapshots a page's DOM, sends it to an LLM via OpenRouter to decide the next action, and executes that action on real elements in Chrome via Playwright—typing only when a field requires it—letting you automate tasks like product searches from a single CLI command.

name: jev-for-engineers
description: Eight minimal, dependency-free Python examples (plus a ~100-line stdlib client and 28 offline tests) showing how to use TypeSafe's Jev model—typed noul/choice/score questions with calibrated probabilities over arbitrary text/JSON state—for mechanical/electrical engineering tasks like FEA triage, BOM alignment, drawing-tolerance extraction, ECR routing, and CAM guardrails, all executed against

name: xjevboost
description: xjevboost classifies tabular rows by learning—via greedy tree search—which small views of labeled examples and columns to send a Jev model, stopping within call/token budgets to approach full-context accuracy at lower cost.

name: jev-tree
description: jev-tree recursively walks a JSON taxonomy, calling TypeSafe's Jev via Vercel AI Gateway once per level and auto-bucketing sibling lists that exceed `maxFanout`, so the model can select among thousands of leaves despite Jev's 255-option-per-call limit.

name: jev-vj
description: jev-vj is a local VJ app that builds a footage library (folders, drag-and-drop, per-clip text descriptions and BPM), uses an AI "Choice" feature driven by your TypeSafe API key to suggest clips and effects per prompt, and provides a live performance deck with keyboard cuts/crossfades, BPM-synced playback speed, strobe/blackout controls, a fullscreen output window, 15 WebGL effects, and local-only

name: OnebrainwithJev
description: Onebrain is a unified agent runtime that strictly separates typed decision-making (Jev picks task kind, model tier, provider, tool approval, risk, and done-ness) from text/code generation across many LLM providers, exposed via an MCP server, Claude Code plugin, CLI, and local HTTP API.

name: home-assistant-typesafe-conversation-agent
description: A Home Assistant conversation agent that resolves device commands and state queries with a TypeSafe System One model's typed, calibrated judgements in a single ~250 ms API call, falling back to an LLM only for compound requests and general questions.

name: thiscita-typesafe
description: OBRA is a Next.js 15/TypeScript workspace demonstrating typed AI decisions via the TypeSafe SDK across three bilingual tools—government services search, PDF/DOCX/TXT proposal review with deterministic readiness scoring, and a voice-enabled personal agenda—keeping LLM classification separate from rule-based execution with server-side key handling and no document persistence.

name: embodied-jev
description: A browser-based MuJoCo workbench for running, replaying, and comparing Franka Panda manipulation experiments with rule baselines or connected models, exposing decisions, probabilities, costs, and physical outcomes.

name: jev-trader
description: jev-trader is a 24/7 market-making system that keeps state math, Avellaneda-Stoikov pricing, hard risk vetoes, and execution in deterministic code while delegating six atomic judgments to Jev inside ~300 ms blocks, logging state-decision-outcome triples for calibration.

name: pi-jev
description: Pi-jev is a TypeSafe Jev (System One) extension monorepo that semantically validates Pi file edits and new-file placement via separate content-guard and placement-guard packages sharing core config discovery, glob/rule matching, auth, Jev invocation, and failure formatting.

name: rayo
description: Rayo is a Ruby CLI/web tool that turns local Ollama models into a fast decision engine—returning typed values (boolean, enum, integer) with calibrated confidence from 1-token logprob generation over cached prompts—exposed via shell commands, an HTTP API, and a demo web UI.

name: jev-browse
description: jev-browse adds `fast_run` helpers to browser-harness that execute whole multi-step website sub-tasks in one call via fast, typed Jev model decisions, making form-filling and navigation 1.6–3.0× faster and 2.1–5.3× cheaper than agent-driven browsing at the same pass rate.

name: omp-auto-mode
description: An oh-my-pi plugin and CLI that pre-classifies every agent tool call as safe, ask, or unsafe by scoring it against seven independent hazard probabilities via the TypeSafe Jev API, enforcing code-owned policy with configurable thresholds and pattern-based allow/deny rules.

name: ardana
description: Ardana is an Ollama-style local runner for System 1 decision models that reads a text state once and answers structured questions — multi-option choices, ordered scores, or yes/no probabilities — via CLI, HTTP API, or browser playground, with no text generation to parse.

name: zerosweep
description: ZeroSweep is a Next.js benchmark app showcasing TypeSafe AI's Jev System One model against autoregressive LLMs, providing a 1,000-email triage mailbox, head-to-head latency/cost races, confidence-calibrated human-review gating, and unit-economics calculators.

name: jevlens
description: JevLens is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension that annotates X/Twitter posts, Threads posts, and user-triggered articles with typed risk signals—spam, bot, adult/promo, political framing, AI-farm, engagement manipulation—via the TypeSafe Jev API plus privacy-preserving local image analysis and a deterministic fallback.

name: jev-yarn
description: jev-yarn is a serverless PWA party game where players join filtered rooms, write timed one-sentence story contributions, and TypeSafe’s Jev picks winners and scores stories using adjustable taste sliders.

name: fishy
description: Fishy is a Manifest V3 browser extension for Chrome, Firefox, and Safari that sends the open Gmail message to TypeSafe's Jev AI model via your own API key, returning a phishing verdict from eight configurable yes/no scam signals plus a 0–100% scam score.

name: astra-jev
description: Astra-Jev is a macOS CLI wrapper for stock Codex that lets Jev adaptively set GPT-6 Astra's reasoning effort per turn and at supported local-tool checkpoints, surfacing selected-versus-confirmed effort inline in the native TUI with explicit modes and read-only resume.

name: jev-k8s-awareness
description: A proof-of-concept real-time Kubernetes cluster awareness dashboard that uses an informer to watch pods in a namespace, evaluates unhealthy pods via TypeSafe Jev for severity, remediation, and escalation, and streams results to a browser UI over SSE.

name: jev-scroll
description: A Chrome extension that labels every post on X while scrolling — Insight, News, Discussion, Humor, Personal, Promo, Bait, Filler, or Ad — via batched Jev decisions (~$0.000039/post), collapsing filtered categories to one-line placeholders with Signal/Balanced/Everything presets, a local API key, and per-post caching.

name: jevia
description: Jevia is an experimental CLI that routes coding-agent tasks to capability tiers using Jev's typed decisions, enforces deterministic fallback policy, executes configured harnesses, and records outcomes in JSONL/SQLite/PostgreSQL history so prior results inform future routing.

name: mu
description: mu is a pi-based coding-agent CLI and desktop app whose judgment kernel delegates 35 bounded per-turn decisions—context admission, memory, safety approval, drift control, cache warming, and hive routing—to fast judges, preserving main-model attention and tokens while logging every verdict.

name: hunch-js
description: hunch-js is a TypeScript library that turns AI judgment into typed function calls: verbs like classify, score, check, where, extract, pick, rank, verify, and route return per-item probabilistic answers, batched in parallel and cached, that code can branch on.

name: Kev
description: Kev is a self-hosted, Apache-2.0 "System One" decision engine that turns any LLM (Ollama, vLLM, OpenAI-compatible, or mock) into a typed classifier returning calibrated `choice`, `score`, and `noul` probabilities instead of prose, exposed via HTTP API, TypeScript/Python SDKs, CLI, MCP, and a built-in playground.

name: agent-jev
description: AgentJev-0.6B is a Qwen3-0.6B–based scorer that answers typed boolean, choice, and score questions over a serialized state in one forward pass—zero decoded tokens, full probability distributions—serving agent loops a fast, thresholdable gate, route, or score reflex.

name: postgres-search
description: Adds Algolia-style search—whole words, prefixes, trigram typo matching, barcodes, typeahead, and facet counts—to plain Postgres in SQL, adapting to your data through one seven-column view and demoed on 440k USDA products.

name: jev-form-filler
description: A Chrome extension that auto-fills web forms from a saved profile, using the typesafe-ai/jev evaluation model to map fields in a single round-trip, showing confidence scores, highlighting filled fields without submitting, and keeping personal values local.

name: stuntdouble
description: A zero-dependency Node proxy that shadows your app's calls to TypeSafe's Jev API to local decision models (e.g., Kev, Laya), records every answer, and reports label/policy agreement, confidence, latency, cost, and a swap verdict—with free replay against new checkpoints.

name: failsafe-jev-buildathon
description: A buildathon repo and CLI where you tame four deliberately unsafe AI agents (ITSM, legal, health, finance) using Jev evaluations and real-time failproofai policies that block or redirect bad tool calls, scored on task success minus harm.

name: jev-triage
description: A multiplayer triage dashboard for GitHub repos that live-syncs issues and PRs through Postgres and Zero, has a TypeSafe model answer typed questions (kind, severity, urgency, next step), and lets maintainers correct, claim, and close work without writing back to GitHub.

name: jevmlx
description: jevmlx scores every allowed option for each field of a schema (booleans, enums, multi-selects) from logits in one batched forward pass on Apple Silicon — no text generation — returning valid-by-construction JSON with per-field probabilities via Python, CLI, or HTTP server.

name: JevHarness
description: JevHarness lets an authoring LLM generate a task-specific harness—feature extraction, structured Jev questions, criteria, and control flow—that executes fast fuzzy decisions via Jev calls without per-decision LLM calls, with optional GEPA-based reflection improving the harness from rewards and complete execution traces.

name: jev-bench
description: jev-bench evaluates models behind a System One-style endpoint (POST /v1/systemone) that returns probability distributions over named options instead of generated text, measuring multiple-choice accuracy and calibration plus per-step decision skill in Snake, maze, and find-the-bug games.

name: s1-tui
description: A Textual terminal UI for System One models: type a state and question, get a typed answer (yes/no, labeled choice, or ordered score) with calibrated confidence and full probabilities, via local MLX or hosted backends, with JSONL run history.

name: jev2048
description: jev2048 is a Playwright-powered CLI agent that shows low-latency constrained decision-making on real DOM-based 2048 sites: it reads the board, asks TypeSafe’s Jev model for one of four moves in one API call, presses the key, and reports calibrated probabilities.

name: jev-sift
description: jev-sift is an MCP tool that sends batches of file paths, public URLs, or text to TypeSafe's Jev model against a query or typed questions, returning compact relevance probabilities so an agent only opens items worth a closer look without loading their contents into its context.

name: jev-foundation-models
description: A Swift 6 package bridging TypeSafe AI's Jev System One decision model into Apple's Foundation Models framework, evaluating strongly typed `@Generable` structs and enums against application state in 40–150ms with calibrated probabilities, confidence metadata, zero hallucinations, and full `LanguageModelSession` API compatibility.

name: classify-plugin
description: A Claude Code plugin that labels every human prompt and agent tool call with configurable categories via TypeSafe AI Jev, recording counts, token usage, cost, confidence, and noise scores in SQLite for pyramid-chart usage analytics and session-log backfill.

name: jev-studio
description: Jev Studio is a Python kit for TypeSafe's Jev that provides a `jev` CLI for typed judgments (verify, screen, classify, extract, match, route, ask, find, rerank, compact, batch) plus a `jev-studio` MCP server exposing the Jev ruleset and instructions to MCP hosts over stdio.

name: jev-techstack-classifier
description: Turns a plain-English project description into a probability-ranked stack across frontend, backend, database, hosting, and mobile, exposing alternatives, confidence, clarifying questions, and contradiction warnings so you can compare trade-offs instead of accepting one opaque pick.

name: rag-gate
description: rag-gate is a TypeSafe-powered HTTP API (`POST /v1/gate`) that sits between retrieval and generation: it scores each already-retrieved RAG chunk for relevance and prompt-injection, drops junk, low-relevance, and injection candidates per tunable `topK`/`minRelevance`/`injectionMax` thresholds, and returns kept/dropped chunks plus token usage — filtering noise before it reaches your LLM without do

name: OpenJev-Vision
description: OpenJev-Vision is an open research toolkit that encodes each image once into a shared probability distribution, enabling reproducible multi-question visual decisions with synthetic scenes, public-image experiments, trained readouts, and evaluations.

name: LibLayaX
description: LibLayaX is a cross-platform C library embedding the Laya AI decision engine in-process via JSON-based functions, delivering fast on-device text classification (yes/no, choice, score) at hundreds of queries per second without servers, cloud, or Python.

name: kleene
description: Kleene is a Kotlin library that asks a non-autoregressive judge model yes/no, pick-one, or rating questions about text or JSON and returns typed TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN verdicts with real probabilities, so policy thresholds, contract checks, and reapplication replace unreliable self-reported confidence and silent defaults.

name: jev-go
description: jev-go is a community-maintained, stdlib-only Go SDK and installable CLI for TypeSafe AI's Jev/System One evaluation API, letting Go apps pose named Noul, Choice, and Score questions via the TypeSafe direct or Vercel AI Gateway providers with typed answers, retries, timeouts, and structured error handling.

name: eslint-plugin-jev
description: An ESLint plugin that goes beyond conventional linters' structural checks by analyzing what code actually means, enabling it to catch semantic issues that shape-only linting cannot detect.

name: JevRouter
description: JevRouter is a TypeScript/Node.js routing layer that uses the Jev decision model to select among models, subagents, skills, MCP tools, CLIs, and plugins—reducing reasoning-token overhead while enforcing availability, permissions, risk, confirmation, and auditable single- or multi-step plans.

name: vgi-typesafe
description: A DuckDB extension worker exposing TypeSafe System One question primitives—choice, noul, and score—as table functions that classify, rate, or filter rows via LATERAL joins, returning typed columns including per-answer confidence for routing decisions, with multi-question ask() calls, per-row dynamic questions, scalar is_true() filtering, and bind-time validation.

name: llamacpp-jev
description: llamacpp-jev wraps an unmodified llama-server to serve TypeSafe Jev's /v1/systemone structured-decision API, returning probability distributions for batched typed questions (yes/no, choice, score) over text or images from any GGUF model on macOS, Linux, or Windows.

name: dbt_jev
description: dbt_jev is a dbt package whose macros emit SQL that calls Jev decision models via TypeSafe AI or OpenRouter on DuckDB or ClickHouse, returning nullable labels, pair-match probabilities, and rubric scores so LLM-powered row decisions run inside ordinary dbt models.

name: jev-product-compliance
description: A CLI harness that bulk-screens a store's product catalog for goods illegal or problematic to sell per country, calling the Jev evaluation model through Vercel AI Gateway to get calibrated probabilities, risk category, and severity verdicts — about $59 per million products.

name: typesafe-mcp
description: A Go binary `evaluate` that runs a stdio MCP server exposing one read-only tool: coding agents send observed state plus typed noul/choice/score questions to TypeSafe Jev (or OpenRouter) and get back probabilities, choices, and scores to branch on in code.

name: typesafe-playground
description: typesafe-playground provides three Dockerized interactive demos—Decision Lab, Jev Driving Lab, and a Fable implementation—that expose TypeSafe Jev's real API-driven judgments, sensor inputs, and driving decisions via inspectable localhost interfaces.

name: omnia-news
description: A Python CLI/library that evaluates supplied source records through local model inference and deterministic metadata gates to produce keep/suppress/review feed decisions, each persisted as a durable, auditable assessment with policy, evidence fingerprints, and timestamps.

name: hx
description: Hx watches a clinician type or dictate a note, opens the questions that note calls for, ticks them off against what was actually written, and surfaces what remains undocumented — quoting only clauses and values from the note, never generating text.

name: plz
description: A Rust daemon for fish that intercepts commands before execution, sending them to TypeSafe's API for a verdict — allowing, prompting for confirmation (once/always/no), or denying — with a permanent SQLite cache keyed to command and context, an editable review prompt, on/off toggling, and usage/latency statistics.

name: fast-browser-use
description: Fast Browser Use is a local-first, fully offline browser-automation engine and agent skill that runs open-source Qwen3.5 models via MLX or PyTorch, scoring DOM-derived candidate actions in one forward pass for second-level, hallucination-free steps with zero cloud calls.

name: JevCoreML
description: JevCoreML provides ready-to-embed Core ML decision models, a Swift package, CLI/HTTP server, and demo app that turn text into calibrated choices, scores, or yes/no answers with probabilities, privately on Apple-silicon GPUs in milliseconds.

name: livesignal
description: LiveSignal is a local, real-time livestream-chat intelligence system that runs live TypeSafe Jev decisions on every comment to surface, cluster, and rank genuine questions for creators, with typed signals, telemetry, and a reproducible 240-comment evaluation corpus.

name: jevable
description: jevable is a bash-native CLI that filters any line stream by meaning: a plain-English question or CEL rules mixing exact conditions with Jev judgments pass only matching lines through unchanged, with grep-style exit codes and stateful watches (keys, cooldowns, windows).

name: system-one-reviewer
description: A dependency-free single-file local PR reviewer: deterministic Python owns diff gathering, clustering, thresholds, verdicts, while TypeSafe's Jev model makes typed severity/category judgments per cluster; a metrics harness scores precision/recall/F1 on planted fixtures.

name: jev-browser
description: jev-browser is an MCP/CLI/library automation layer where an LLM states one outcome and values, Jev picks the element/action/status, and Playwright executes it—cutting page-context tokens while handling complex UIs and flagging blocked, ambiguous, or irreversible steps.

name: jeveora-scout
description: A read-only terminal dashboard that scans Meteora DLMM/DAMM v2 pools every minute, applies hard safety filters plus TypeSafe AI (Jev) judgments to flag LP entry, rebalance, and exit signals in the terminal and Discord, tracks your positions, and logs outcomes for evaluation.

name: eval-layer
description: A Codex/Claude Code skill that reads an agent's code, instructions, domain docs, tools, and memory to generate a reusable eval layer—grounded rubric, test cases, execution checks, CLI harness—that scores real runs via Jev or an LLM judge into JSON/Markdown reports.

name: feed-lens
description: Feed Lens is an open-source Chrome extension that labels Weibo, Threads, and X posts with customizable topic and expression-style tags, classified via your TypeSafe API key using editable label descriptions, with per-platform dictionaries and JSON import/export.

name: jev-movie-finder
description: Local movie search app that live-filters a 1.5M-title TMDB catalog via staged, cancellable SQLite FTS5 passes in worker processes, rendering an updating poster grid with hover/tap details and optional server-side Jev AI ranking, plus benchmark scripts for regression testing.

name: jev-claude
description: A Claude Code plugin that routes judgment calls—plan approvals, user questions, dependency installs, destructive commands—through Jev, a typed decision model returning calibrated probabilities, enforced by bounded hooks and recorded in an auditable ledger.
